  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3d Task 1: the quarantine, at a phone's width

  /** The case as the fixtures hold it, with a seal for good of its own, in force or lifted, whose custody is as given. */
  function withSealForGood(view: CaseView, custody: NonNullable<CaseView["decisions"][number]["custody"]>, inForce: boolean): CaseView {
    const interim = view.decisions[0]!;
    return {
      ...view,
      decisions: [

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3d Task 2: the release, at a phone's width

  const RELEASE_LEAVE = "c5364758-6a7b-4c8d-9e0f-142536475869";
  /** A release block as the API answers it: a seal reported, assessed illegal, moved, with a leave from a court and a hostile reference. */
  function releaseBlock(overrides: Partial<NonNullable<CaseView["decisions"][number]["release"]>> = {}): NonNullable<CaseView["decisions"][number]["release"]> {
    return {
      reported: true,
      theirReference: HOSTILE.bidi,
      answer: "illegal",
      answeredAt: new Date(Date.now() - 2 * 24 * 3_600_000).toISOString(),
      handedOverAt: null,
      quarantined: true,
      preserved: false,
      leave: { id: RELEASE_LEAVE, from: "court", reference: "4 O 1/26", receivedOn: "2026-10-15", untold: false, untoldUntil: null },
      tellHeld: false,
      postIds: [POST_ID],
      remaining: 0,
      silenceDays: null,
      releasedAt: null,
      basis: null,
      backupsClearAt: null,
      noticeHeld: null,
      releasedPosts: 0,
      releasedImages: 0,
      ...overrides,
    };
  }
  /** The case with a seal for good in force whose decision carries this release block and its custody, all files moved. */
  function withRelease(view: CaseView, release: NonNullable<CaseView["decisions"][number]["release"]>): CaseView {
    const sealed = withSealForGood(view, { files: 2, moved: 2, movedAt: new Date(Date.now() - 3_600_000).toISOString(), toReturn: 0, filesLeft: 0, lost: 0 }, true);
    return { ...sealed, decisions: sealed.decisions.map((decided, index) => (index === sealed.decisions.length - 1 ? { ...decided, release } : decided)) };
  }
  const releaseRegion = () => page.getByRole("region", { name: RELEASE_WORDS.title, exact: true });

  test("3d Task 2: at 360 by 740 px, the release block in each state: a leave with the control, an assessment without one, the answers that support nothing, a conflict, more posts than one release names, and the author's telling in its three values", async () => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 360, height: 740 });
    fixtures.state.role = "admin";
    const view = fixtures.state.cases.get(CASE_FROZEN)!;
    const until = new Date(Date.now() + 5 * 24 * 3_600_000).toISOString();
    const states: [NonNullable<CaseView["decisions"][number]["release"]>, string[], boolean][] = [
      [releaseBlock(), [RELEASE_WORDS.leave("from a court"), RELEASE_WORDS.sign(1), `${RELEASE_WORDS.facts.tell.label}${RELEASE_WORDS.facts.tell.atOnce}`], true],
      [releaseBlock({ leave: null }), [RELEASE_WORDS.assessed], false],
      [releaseBlock({ leave: null, answer: "not_illegal" }), [RELEASE_WORDS.notIllegal], false],
      [releaseBlock({ leave: null, answer: "no_assessment" }), [RELEASE_WORDS.nothing], false],
      [releaseBlock({ leave: null, answer: null, answeredAt: null }), [RELEASE_WORDS.nothing, RELEASE_WORDS.facts.answer.none], false],
      [releaseBlock({ answer: "not_illegal" }), [RELEASE_WORDS.conflict], true],
      [releaseBlock({ remaining: 7 }), [RELEASE_WORDS.more(RELEASE_POSTS_MAX, 7)], true],
      [releaseBlock({ tellHeld: true, leave: { ...releaseBlock().leave!, untold: true, untoldUntil: until } }), [RELEASE_WORDS.facts.tell.untold(bothTimes(until))], true],
      [releaseBlock({ tellHeld: true, leave: { ...releaseBlock().leave!, untold: true, untoldUntil: null } }), [RELEASE_WORDS.facts.tell.untold(null)], true],
      [releaseBlock({ tellHeld: true }), [RELEASE_WORDS.facts.tell.record], true],
    ];
    try {
      await page.goto(`${origin}/`);
      for (const [block, words, control] of states) {
        fixtures.state.cases.set(CASE_FROZEN, withRelease(view, block));
        await page.goto(`${origin}/cases/${CASE_FROZEN}`);
        await shown(releaseRegion());
        const text = (await releaseRegion().textContent()) ?? "";
        for (const sentence of words) expect(text, sentence).toContain(sentence);
        expect(text).toContain(RELEASE_WORDS.what);
        expect(text).toContain(RELEASE_WORDS.backups(RETENTION.backupDays));
        expect(text).toContain(RELEASE_WORDS.periodUnset);
        expect(await releaseRegion().getByRole("button", { name: RELEASE_WORDS.button }).count(), words[0]).toBe(control ? 1 : 0);
        // The authority's reference is an outsider's text, in its frame, never in a label's place.
        expect(await releaseRegion().locator(".frame").count()).toBeGreaterThan(0);
        await texts();
        await cleanOnPhone();
      }
    } finally {
      fixtures.state.cases.set(CASE_FROZEN, view);
      fixtures.state.role = "moderator";
      await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 900 });
    }
  });

  const CASE_PROGRAM = "9d0e1f2a-3b4c-4d5e-8f6a-0b1c2d3e4f5a";
  const ITEM_PROGRAM = "ae1f2a3b-4c5d-4e6f-9a7b-1c2d3e4f5a6b";
  const DECISION_PROGRAM = "bf2a3b4c-5d6e-4f7a-8b8c-2d3e4f5a6b7c";
  /** What a hostile author could ask a person: a bidirectional override, a look-alike console label and a link (8.9). */
  const OBJECTION = `${HOSTILE.bidi} ${LOOKALIKE.label} ${HOSTILE.url}`;
  const LIFT_REASON = `The image is a painting in a museum ${HOSTILE.quote}`;

  /** A post's case a program's score opened, its withhold of the first image in force since `decidedAt`, and the author's request. */
  function programView(decidedAt: string, askedAt: string): CaseView {
    return postCase({
      id: CASE_PROGRAM,
      stateVersion: 2,
      intakeSeq: 1,
      items: [itemFixture({ id: ITEM_PROGRAM, source: SOURCES.program, explanation: null, mediaId: IMAGE_ONE, ruleId: "R1" })],
      decisions: [
        decisionFixture({
          id: DECISION_PROGRAM,
          byProgram: true,
          staffHandle: null,
          source: "own_initiative",
          rulesVersion: 3,
          redressVersion: 4,
          decidedAt,
          facts: null,
          reason: null,
          actions: [{ id: "c03a4b5c-6d7e-4f8a-9b9c-3e4f5a6b7c8d", kind: "withhold_media", mediaId: IMAGE_ONE, noEffect: null, inForce: true, reversesActionId: null, liftedBy: null, sealed: null, ...NO_STANDING }],
        }),
      ],
      notes: [],
      history: [],
      signals: [{ itemId: ITEM_PROGRAM, kind: "r1_score", thresholdVersion: 0, match: null }],
      objection: { text: OBJECTION, createdAt: askedAt },
    });
  }

  test("3d Task 6: at 360 by 740 px, the queue with the three chips and the objected case first in its lane; Home with [home.automated] and [home.objected]; After a restore with [restore.program]", async () => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 360, height: 740 });

    const askedAt = new Date(Date.now() - 3_600_000).toISOString();
    fixtures.state.cases.set(CASE_PROGRAM, programView(decidedAt, askedAt));
    // The API's order: inside lane 2 the case whose author asked for a person comes first, before an older case.
    fixtures.state.queueRows = [
      queueRow({ id: CASE_PROGRAM, oldestOpenAt: decidedAt, openItems: 1, rules: ["R1"], categories: ["STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC"], allegesIllegal: false, foundByProgram: true, takenByProgram: true, objected: true }),
      queueRow({ id: CASE_POST, oldestOpenAt: new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 3_600_000).toISOString() }),
    ];
    fixtures.state.automated = { waiting: 1, oldestAt: decidedAt, objected: 1, oldestObjectionAt: askedAt, flags: 0, cases: [CASE_PROGRAM], objectedCases: [CASE_PROGRAM] };
    const at = new Date(Date.now() - 26 * 3_600_000).toISOString();
    const gap: RestoreGap = {
      id: "0000000b-7a1b-4c2d-8e3f-4a5b6c7d8e9f",
      class: "restriction",
      actedAt: at,
      action: "automated_decided",
      caseId: CASE_PROGRAM,
      orderId: null,

      kinds: ["withhold_media"],
      closedAt: null,

      closedByDecisionId: null,
    };
    try {
      await page.goto(`${origin}/queue`);
      const rows = page.locator("table.queue tbody tr");
      await shown(rows.first());
      const first = (await rows.nth(0).textContent()) ?? "";
      for (const chip of [AUTOMATION_WORDS.queue.found, AUTOMATION_WORDS.queue.taken, AUTOMATION_WORDS.queue.objected]) expect(first).toContain(chip);
      expect((await rows.nth(1).textContent()) ?? "").not.toContain(AUTOMATION_WORDS.queue.objected);
      await texts();

      await page.goto(`${origin}/`);

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3d Task 7: known material, at a phone's width

  const CASE_MATCH = "c03b4c5d-6e7f-4a8b-9c9d-3e4f5a6b7c8d";
  const ITEM_MATCH = "d14c5d6e-7f8a-4b9c-8d0e-4f5a6b7c8d9e";
  const DECISION_MATCH = "e25d6e7f-8a9b-4c0d-9e1f-5a6b7c8d9e0f";
  const REFUSAL_OPEN = "f36e7f8a-9b0c-4d1e-8f2a-6b7c8d9e0f1a";
  const REFUSAL_REPORT = "047f8a9b-0c1d-4e2f-9a3b-7c8d9e0f1a2b";
  const REFUSAL_NO_REPORT = "15809b0c-1d2e-4f3a-8b4c-8d9e0f1a2b3c";
  const REFUSAL_RELEASED = "26910c1d-2e3f-4a4b-9c5d-9e0f1a2b3c4d";
  const UPLOAD_LEAVE = "37a21d2e-3f4a-4b5c-8d6e-0f1a2b3c4d5e";
  /** A source's strings as an adapter could return them: a bidirectional override, a look-alike label, a script address (8.9). */
  const MATCH_RECORD: MatchRecord = { source: HOSTILE.bidi, listVersion: LOOKALIKE.label, hashType: "sha1", matchKind: "exact", classification: HOSTILE.url, listed: true, acting: true, queriedAt: new Date(Date.now() - 3_600_000).toISOString() };
  /** What a hostile uploader could write in an objection. */
  const UPLOAD_OBJECTION = `${HOSTILE.bidi} ${LOOKALIKE.label} ${HOSTILE.url}`;

  /** A post's case a match opened on its first image: listed (acting or not) it cites R2 and freezes; another class cites no rule. */
  function matchView(match: MatchRecord, more: Partial<CaseView> = {}): CaseView {
    const listed = match.listed;
    return postCase({
      id: CASE_MATCH,
      lane: listed ? 0 : 2,
      stateVersion: 2,
      intakeSeq: 1,
      imagesAllowed: !listed,
      suspicion: listed ? { open: true, reach: { posts: 1, images: 2, sealed: 0, served: 2, newestPostOn: "2026-09-30" }, earlier: { target: { count: 0, lastOn: null, imagesOpenedOn: null }, author: { count: 0, lastOn: null } } } : null,
      items: [itemFixture({ id: ITEM_MATCH, source: SOURCES.program, explanation: null, mediaId: IMAGE_ONE, ruleId: listed ? "R2" : null, csam: listed, suspect: listed, lane: listed ? 0 : 2, category: "STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS" })],
      decisions: [],
      notes: [],
      history: [],
      signals: [{ itemId: ITEM_MATCH, kind: "known_match", thresholdVersion: null, match }],
      matchedImages: [IMAGE_ONE],
      ...more,
    });
  }

  /** One refusal of each state, as Held uploads lists them (8.6). */
  function heldUploads(): HeldUpload[] {
    const hour = 3_600_000;
    const at = (hours: number) => new Date(Date.now() - hours * hour).toISOString();
    const base = { match: MATCH_RECORD, otherRefusals: 0, uploaderGone: false, objection: null, objectedAt: null, endedAt: null, endAs: null, endReason: null, deletesAt: null, reported: false, quarantined: false, release: null };
    const release = {
      reported: true,
      theirReference: LOOKALIKE.label,
      answer: null,
      answeredAt: null,
      handedOverAt: null,
      quarantined: true,
      leave: { id: UPLOAD_LEAVE, from: "authority" as const, reference: "4 O 1/26", receivedOn: at(30).slice(0, 10), untold: false, untoldUntil: null },
      tellHeld: false,
      silenceDays: null,
      releasedAt: null,
      basis: null,
      backupsClearAt: null,
      noticeHeld: null,
    };
    return [
      { ...base, id: REFUSAL_OPEN, refusedAt: at(5), otherRefusals: 1, uploaderGone: true },
      // An objection that arrived after "Report".
      { ...base, id: REFUSAL_REPORT, refusedAt: at(50), endAs: "report", endedAt: at(40), reported: true, quarantined: true, objection: UPLOAD_OBJECTION, objectedAt: at(2), release },
      { ...base, id: REFUSAL_NO_REPORT, refusedAt: at(30), endAs: "no_report", endReason: "counsel_no_duty", endedAt: at(3), deletesAt: new Date(Date.now() + 21 * hour).toISOString() },
      { ...base, id: REFUSAL_RELEASED, refusedAt: at(90), endAs: "report", endedAt: at(80), reported: true, quarantined: true, release: { ...release, releasedAt: at(10), basis: "leave", backupsClearAt: new Date(Date.now() + 30 * 24 * hour).toISOString(), noticeHeld: false } },
    ];
  }
  const uploadBlock = (id: string) => page.locator("article.upload", { has: page.locator(`#upload-${id}`) });

      await shown(page.getByText(C.holdLine(bothTimes(at), "no_report"), { exact: true }));
      await shown(page.getByText(C.holdEnd(true), { exact: true }));
      await shown(page.getByText(C.holdEnd(false), { exact: true }));
      expect(await page.getByRole("link", { name: C.holdLink }).count()).toBe(1);
      expect(await page.getByRole("button", { name: RECOVERY_WORDS.notNeeded }).count()).toBe(0);
      await texts();
      await cleanOnPhone();
    } finally {
      fixtures.state.automated = { waiting: 0, oldestAt: null, objected: 0, oldestObjectionAt: null, flags: 0, cases: [], objectedCases: [] };
      fixtures.state.heldUploads = { open: 0, oldest: null, objected: 0, capped: 0 };
      fixtures.state.destructive = [];
      fixtures.state.restore = restore;
      fixtures.state.restoreOverview = restoreOverview;
      fixtures.state.role = "moderator";
      await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 900 });
    }
  });

  // ---------------------------------------------------------------- 3d Task 8: the flag, and every screen of 3d once more

  const CASE_FLAG = "c13d5f7b-8a9b-4c0d-8e1f-2a3b4c5d6e7f";

  test("3d Task 8: at 360 by 740 px, the queue with [queue.flag] where its lane and age put it; a case with [case.flag] and [case.sameSource]; then every screen of 8.9 once more in one pass, under the phone's rules", async () => {
    await page.setViewportSize({ width: 360, height: 740 });
    const older = new Date(Date.now() - 30 * 3_600_000).toISOString();
    const newer = new Date(Date.now() - 3_600_000).toISOString();
    const view = postCase({ id: CASE_FLAG, flag: { items: 6, reporters: 5 } });
    // The first item's reporter has two other open items elsewhere; the others none.
    fixtures.state.cases.set(CASE_FLAG, { ...view, items: view.items.map((entry, index) => ({ ...entry, sameSourceOpen: index === 0 ? 2 : 0 })) });
    // The API's order: lane and age alone. The flagged case is the newer of two in its lane, and stays second.
    fixtures.state.queueRows = [queueRow({ id: CASE_POST, oldestOpenAt: older }), queueRow({ id: CASE_FLAG, oldestOpenAt: newer, flag: { items: 6, reporters: 5 } })];
    try {
      await page.goto(`${origin}/queue`);
      const rows = page.locator("table.queue tbody tr");
      await shown(rows.first());
      expect((await rows.nth(0).textContent()) ?? "").not.toContain(AUTOMATION_WORDS.queueFlag);
      expect((await rows.nth(1).textContent()) ?? "").toContain(AUTOMATION_WORDS.queueFlag);
      await texts();
      await cleanOnPhone();

      await page.goto(`${origin}/cases/${CASE_FLAG}`);
      await shown(page.getByText(AUTOMATION_WORDS.caseFlag(6, 5), { exact: true }));
      expect(AUTOMATION_WORDS.caseFlag(6, 5)).toContain(`within ${SIGNAL_RULES.windowMinutes} minutes`);
      await shown(page.getByText(AUTOMATION_WORDS.sameSource(2), { exact: false }));
      expect(await page.getByText("other open item", { exact: false }).count()).toBe(1);
      // The line is under the header, before the evidence.
      const body = (await page.locator("main").textContent()) ?? "";
      expect(body.indexOf(AUTOMATION_WORDS.caseFlag(6, 5))).toBeLessThan(body.indexOf("Evidence"));
      await texts();
      await cleanOnPhone();

      // Every screen 3d touches, once more, at this width: Home with its block, Held uploads, After a restore.
      const screens: [string, Locator][] = [
        ["/", page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Home" })],
        ["/queue", page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Queue" })],
        ["/uploads", page.getByRole("heading", { name: CUSTODY_WORDS.uploads.title })],
        ["/restore", page.getByRole("heading", { name: RECOVERY_WORDS.title })],
        [`/cases/${CASE_FLAG}`, page.getByText(AUTOMATION_WORDS.caseFlag(6, 5), { exact: true })],
      ];
      for (const [path, mark] of screens) {
        await page.goto(`${origin}${path}`);
        await shown(mark.first());
        expect(page.url(), path).toBe(`${origin}${path}`);
        await texts();
        await cleanOnPhone();
      }
    } finally {
      fixtures.state.queueRows = null;
      fixtures.state.cases.delete(CASE_FLAG);
      await page.setViewportSize({ width: 1280, height: 900 });
    }
  });

  test("an address the console does not have says so, inside the console", async () => {
    await page.goto(`${origin}/no/such/page`);
    await shown(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "No such page" }));
    await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Go to the home page" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Home" }));
    // Every read the home screen started has finished before the walk moves on, so none is in flight when the session ends.
    await shown(page.locator("ul.signins"));
    await shown(page.locator("ul.keys"));
    await shown(page.getByRole("cell", { name: "This session" }));
    await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Audit log" }).click();
    await shown(page.locator("table.audit tbody tr"));
    await clean();
  });

  test("the ended session: sign-in in place at the same address, both staff cookies gone, and the same page after", async () => {
    fixtures.endEverySession();
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Load older" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByText("Your staff session ended."));
    expect(page.url()).toBe(`${origin}/audit`);
    expect((await context.cookies()).filter((cookie) => cookie.name.startsWith("__Host-korbat_staff"))).toEqual([]);
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in with your staff key" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Audit log" }));
    await shown(page.locator("table.audit tbody tr"));
    expect(page.url()).toBe(`${origin}/audit`);
    await clean();
  });

  test("a second key enrolled while signed in: its success page asks that key, never the session's, and signs in with it", async () => {
    const first = staffAuthenticator;
    const token = fixtures.issueEnrolment();
    // The first key holds the live session; it could answer nothing here unless the page asked it, which this would show.
    await watcher.cdp.send("WebAuthn.setAutomaticPresenceSimulation", { authenticatorId: first, enabled: false });
    const second = await addAuthenticator("device-bound security key");
    staffAuthenticators.push(second);
    await page.goto(`${origin}/enroll/${token}`);
    await shown(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Register a staff key" }));
    await page.getByLabel("Name of this key").fill("Backup key");
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Register a security key" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByText("is registered", { exact: false }));
    const newKey = fixtures.state.keys[fixtures.state.keys.length - 1]!;
    expect(newKey.name).toBe("Backup key");
    const [firstBefore, secondBefore] = [await signaturesOf(first), await signaturesOf(second)];
    // The browser still holds the first key's session: the sign-in page would show home and ask no key.
    expect((await context.cookies()).some((cookie) => cookie.name === "__Host-korbat_staff")).toBe(true);
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in with this key" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByText("opened the console", { exact: false }));
    expect(await signaturesOf(second)).toBe(secondBefore + 1);
    expect(await signaturesOf(first)).toBe(firstBefore);
    // The session it opened is the new key's.
    expect([...fixtures.state.sessions.values()].filter((s) => s.credentialId === newKey.credentialId)).toHaveLength(1);
    await watcher.cdp.send("WebAuthn.setAutomaticPresenceSimulation", { authenticatorId: first, enabled: true });
    await page.getByRole("link", { name: "Go to the home page" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByRole("heading", { name: "Home" }));
    await shown(page.locator("ul.signins"));
    await shown(page.locator("ul.keys"));
    await shown(page.getByRole("cell", { name: "This session" }));
    await clean();
  });

  test("sign-out ends the session and shows sign-in at its own address", async () => {
    const before = fixtures.state.sessions.size;
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign out", exact: true }).click();
    await page.waitForURL(`${origin}/signin`);
    await shown(page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in with your staff key" }));
    expect(await page.getByText("Your staff session ended.").count()).toBe(0);
    // The session the page held, the second key's, is gone; the first key's, which this browser no longer names, stays.
    expect(fixtures.state.sessions.size).toBe(before - 1);
    expect([...fixtures.state.sessions.values()].some((s) => s.credentialId === fixtures.state.keys[fixtures.state.keys.length - 1]!.credentialId)).toBe(false);
    await clean();
  });

  test("sign-in options that carry a step-up challenge are refused before the key is asked", async () => {
    const before = await signatures();
    const served = fixtures.state.signInOptionsServed;
    const verifies = fixtures.state.requests.filter((r) => r.path === "/api/staff/signin/verify").length;
    fixtures.state.stepUpChallengeAtNextSignIn = true;
    await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Sign in with your staff key" }).click();
    await shown(page.getByText(messageFor("signin_mismatch")));
    expect(fixtures.state.signInOptionsServed).toBe(served + 1);
    // No key signed anything and nothing was sent after the options: the forged confirmation was never made.
    expect(await signatures()).toBe(before);
    expect(fixtures.state.requests.filter((r) => r.path === "/api/staff/signin/verify").length).toBe(verifies);
    expect(page.url()).toBe(`${origin}/signin`);
    await clean();
  });

  test("every request the walk sent was its person's own, marked, and every string the fixtures wrote was shown as text", () => {
    expect(watcher.take()).toEqual([]);
    expect(fixtures.state.requests.length).toBeGreaterThan(20);
    // An image is asked for by the browser itself, which sends no mark, and the queue reads itself again every 60 seconds
    // while it is open, unmarked so that it never keeps a session alive (should a step of the walk ever last that long);
    // so do Orders and an order's page every 20 seconds (3f); and the console reads After a restore once a session, for its
    // navigation (3f Task 6), unmarked. Every other request was the person's own.
    const pagesOwn = (r: { method: string; path: string }) =>
      IMAGE_PATH.test(r.path) || (r.method === "GET" && (r.path === "/api/staff/queue" || r.path.startsWith("/api/staff/queue?") || r.path === "/api/staff/orders" || r.path.startsWith("/api/staff/orders/") || r.path === "/api/staff/restore"));
    expect(fixtures.state.requests.filter((r) => !r.activity && !pagesOwn(r))).toEqual([]);
    expect(fixtures.state.problems).toEqual([]);
    expect(HOSTILE_TEXTS.filter((text) => !seen.has(text))).toEqual([]);
  });
});

/**
 * An account's case that holds an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material and reaches images that are still
 * served: the seal and "Do not seal now" are offered on it. Its newest snapshot holds the account's fields as they read
 * now, so nothing asks for a fresh one.
 */
export function sealableCase(id: string, accountId: string): CaseView {
  const fields = { handle: "an_account", displayName: HOSTILE.quote, bio: LOOKALIKE.label };
  const base = accountCase();
  const [copied] = base.snapshots;
  if (!copied || copied.withheld) throw new Error("the account case's snapshot shows its content");
  return accountCase({
    id,
    target: { type: "account", id: accountId, ...fields, deleted: false },
    suspicion: { open: true, reach: { posts: 2, images: 3, sealed: 0, served: 3, newestPostOn: "2026-09-30" }, earlier: { target: { count: 0, lastOn: null, imagesOpenedOn: null }, author: { count: 0, lastOn: null } } },
    snapshots: [{ ...copied, id: accountId.replace(/^.{8}/, "5a5a5a5a"), targetId: accountId, authorHandle: fields.handle, ...fields }],
    // An item of its own, so that no two fixture cases hold the same one.
    items: base.items.map((each) => ({ ...each, id: accountId.replace(/^.{8}/, "6b6b6b6b") })),
    history: [],
  });
}

  };

````ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
import path from "node:path";
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { ALERT_RULES, ALERT_TEXTS, AUTOMATION_RULES, EDGE_CACHE, EDGE_RULES, HEAD_RULES, ORDER_RULES, RECIPIENT_RULES, REPLY_AIM_HOURS, RETENTION, SIGNAL_RULES, STANDING_RULES, TRANSPARENCY_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { AUTOMATION_WORDS } from "../src/messages";
import { ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK, RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK } from "../src/screens/Home";

/**
 * The README's moderation runbook and the console's home screen say the same thing (3c design, section 13, Task 12).
 * When decided items wait for the daily release longer than it ever takes, or an erasure is more than a day late, the
 * home screen shows the count with the runbook's sentence for it, and each sentence is a constant of the screen. This
 * test reads README.md from the repository's root and holds the runbook to the same two constants, word for word, so
 * that what staff are told on the screen is what the operator reads in the runbook: whoever changes one changes both.
 */
const README = path.resolve(import.meta.dirname, "..", "..", "..", "README.md");

/** Markdown's code mark. The README sets a log line or a setting in code marks; the console shows the same words as plain text. */
const CODE_MARK = "`";

/** A text as its reader sees it: without the code marks. Nothing else is changed, so every word and every sign must agree. */
const withoutCodeMarks = (text: string): string => text.split(CODE_MARK).join("");

/** The README's lines, as written. */
function readmeLines(): string[] {
  return readFileSync(README, "utf8").split("\n");
}

/** The lines of the README's section "Moderation": from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function moderationSection(): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf("## Moderation");
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}

/** The section's runbook as its reader sees it: every line after "The runbook:", without the code marks. */
function moderationRunbook(): string {
  const section = moderationSection();
  const start = section.indexOf("The runbook:");
  return start === -1 ? "" : withoutCodeMarks(section.slice(start + 1).join("\n"));
}

/** How often `part` stands in `text`. */
const count = (text: string, part: string): number => text.split(part).length - 1;

describe("the README's moderation runbook says what the home screen says", () => {
  const sentences: [string, string][] = [
    ["decisions not released", RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
    ["late erasures", ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK],
  ];

  test("the README has a section Moderation, and the section has a runbook", () => {
    expect(readmeLines()).toContain("## Moderation");
    expect(moderationSection()).toContain("The runbook:");
    expect(moderationRunbook().trim()).not.toBe("");
  });

  test("neither constant holds a code mark or a line break, so reading the README without its code marks hides no difference", () => {
    for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain(CODE_MARK);
      expect(sentence, name).not.toContain("\n");
      // A whole sentence: it opens with "A count of" and ends in a full stop, as the runbook's bullet writes it.
      expect(sentence.startsWith("A count of "), name).toBe(true);
      expect(sentence.endsWith("."), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  for (const [name, sentence] of sentences) {
    test(`the runbook holds the home screen's sentence for ${name}, word for word`, () => {
      expect(moderationRunbook()).toContain(sentence);
    });

    test(`the sentence for ${name} stands once in the README, in that runbook: no second copy can drift from it`, () => {
      expect(count(withoutCodeMarks(readmeLines().join("\n")), sentence)).toBe(1);
      expect(count(moderationRunbook(), sentence)).toBe(1);
    });
  }

  test("both sentences stand in one bullet of the runbook, the release's first, as the home screen orders its two lines", () => {
    const bullets = moderationRunbook()
      .split("\n")
      .filter((line) => line.includes(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK) || line.includes(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
    expect(bullets).toHaveLength(1);
    const bullet = bullets[0] ?? "";
    expect(bullet.startsWith("- ")).toBe(true);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(-1);
    expect(bullet.indexOf(ERASURE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK)).toBeGreaterThan(bullet.indexOf(RELEASE_OVERDUE_RUNBOOK));
  });
});

/**
 * The README's account sanctions (3e design, section 13, Task 7) and the constants they print. The section Moderation
 * describes 3e in a paragraph that opens with ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD and a bullet for each title below, and its runbook
 * gains the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h). Every number in that text is a number of STANDING_RULES or
 * REPLY_AIM_HOURS: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused, so the README cannot
 * keep a number the constants changed. A bullet added to 3e's text joins its list here.
 */
const ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD = "Account sanctions (sub-project 3e;";
const STANDING_TITLES = [
  "Strikes.",
  "The ladder.",
  "Announced suspensions and the reply.",
  "Suspensions at once.",
  "While suspended.",
  "Termination.",
  "The restriction of reporting.",
  "Handle retirement.",
  "What is kept of them.",
  "The Standing screen.",
  // The runbook's bullets (a) to (h).
  "Account sanctions each working day.",
  "Answering a reply.",
  "A protective suspension.",
  "A breach that lies only in a handle",
  "A notice a person did not get by mail.",
  "A measure at once while an announced suspension waits.",
  "A mark that was wrong.",
  "Reports before an account measure.",
] as const;

/** The lines of 3e's text in Moderation, without code marks: the lead paragraph and each bullet by its bold title. */
function standingLines(): { lead: string | undefined; bullets: Map<string, string[]> } {
  const section = moderationSection().map(withoutCodeMarks);
  const bullets = new Map(STANDING_TITLES.map((title) => [title as string, section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`- **${title}`))]));
  return { lead: section.find((line) => line.startsWith(ACCOUNT_SANCTIONS_LEAD)), bullets };
}
const standingText = (): string => {
  const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
  return [lead ?? "", ...[...bullets.values()].flat()].join("\n");
};

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const S = STANDING_RULES;
const STANDING_NUMBERS: { constant: string; phrase: string }[] = [
  { constant: "strikeDays", phrase: `which counts for ${S.strikeDays} days` },

  { constant: "ladderMemoryDays", phrase: `the ladder suspensions decided in the last ${S.ladderMemoryDays} days` },

  { constant: "undeliveredHours", phrase: `or ${S.undeliveredHours} hours after the decision` },

  { constant: "protectiveDays", phrase: `for at most ${S.protectiveDays} days, never worded as a finding` },
  { constant: "reportWarnMarks", phrase: `At least ${S.reportWarnMarks} marked reports in ${S.reportFrameDays} days` },
  { constant: "reportRestrictMarks", phrase: `${S.reportRestrictMarks} marked reports sent after it, while it counts (${S.reportFrameDays} days)` },
  { constant: "reportRestrictDays", phrase: `open a restriction of at most ${S.reportRestrictDays} days` },
  { constant: "reportFrameDays", phrase: `the marks and the daily tallies ${S.reportFrameDays} days after their report's UTC day` },
  { constant: "REPLY_AIM_HOURS", phrase: `korbat aims to answer a reply to one within ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours` },
  { constant: "REPLY_AIM_HOURS", phrase: `answer within ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS} hours` },
];

describe("the README's account sanctions say what the constants say (3e design, section 13, Task 7)", () => {
  test("Moderation opens 3e's part with its paragraph, and each of its bullets stands there once", () => {
    const { lead, bullets } = standingLines();
    expect(lead).toBeDefined();

  });

  test("the runbook holds the bullets of section 13's (a) to (h), after The runbook: and before the records kept off the server", () => {

/**
 * The README's authorities' orders (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10) and the constants they print. 3f's text
 * is the section "Authorities' orders", Upgrading from its 3f paragraph on (Task 1), Restoring's block "Restoring with
 * the keeper's copy" (Task 6) and Before going public's owner's list. Every number in it is a number of ORDER_RULES or
 * ALERT_RULES: a table holds each in its sentence, and every other run of digits is refused but for what names a
 * reference (an article, a research finding, a row of the design's section 2, a check P1 to P8, a list's numbering, a
 * path, a date), so the README cannot keep a number the constants changed. A setting is written as the operator sets it
 * in infra/.env, an API setting with the prefix Compose maps. A section added to 3f's text joins its list here.
 */
const FENCE = "```";

/** The lines of a "## " section of the README, from its heading to the next heading of the same level. */
function sectionLines(heading: string): string[] {
  const lines = readmeLines();
  const start = lines.indexOf(heading);
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start + 1);
  const end = rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith("## "));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** A section's lines from the first that begins with these words to the section's end, or to the first that begins with `until`. */
function linesFrom(lines: string[], lead: string, until?: string): string[] {
  const start = lines.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(lead));
  if (start === -1) return [];
  const rest = lines.slice(start);
  const end = until === undefined ? -1 : rest.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(until));
  return end === -1 ? rest : rest.slice(0, end);
}
/** Lines without their fenced code: a command's own numbers and words are not the runbook's. */
function withoutFences(lines: string[]): string[] {
  let inside = false;
  return lines.filter((line) => {
    if (line.startsWith(FENCE)) {
      inside = !inside;
      return false;
    }
    return !inside;
  });
}

const ORDERS_HEADING = "## Authorities' orders";
const ORDERS_TITLES = [
  "The contact point.",
  "On call.",
  "A removal order, step by step",
  "Other messages and orders.",
  "When nobody can act within the hour.",
  "Notifications and hand-overs.",
  "A person asks about a missing post.",
  "An author writes about an order's notice.",
  "The daily copy.",
  "A key in someone else's hands.",
  "The yearly counts.",
] as const;
const OWNERS_LEAD = "**The owner's list (sub-project 3f).**";
const OWNERS_TITLES = [
  "The Member State.",
  "The mailbox.",
  "The people's own access to the mailbox.",
  "Registering.",
  "The push hostname and ntfy's users.",
  "The phones.",
  "The keys.",
  "The papers, and counsel.",
  "The contact address.",
  "The page for the yearly report.",
  "The keeper, and the two places files rest.",
  "Decide",
  "Counsel",
] as const;

/** 3f's text, part by part, without code marks and fenced code. */
function ordersParts(): Record<"orders" | "upgrading" | "restoring" | "owners", string> {
  const read = (lines: string[]) => withoutCodeMarks(withoutFences(lines).join("\n"));
  return {
    orders: read(sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING)),
    upgrading: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f)")),
    restoring: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")),
    owners: read(linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in")),
  };
}
const ordersText = (): string => Object.values(ordersParts()).join("\n");

/** A number in a sentence as the README writes it, and the constant it is. */
const O = ORDER_RULES;
const A = ALERT_RULES;
const ORDER_NUMBERS: { constant: string; part: keyof ReturnType<typeof ordersParts>; phrase: string }[] = [
  { constant: "ALERT_RULES.pollSeconds", part: "orders", phrase: `reads the inbox and the junk folder every ${A.pollSeconds} seconds` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.escalateMinutes", part: "orders", phrase: `it rings every staff phone ${O.escalateMinutes} minutes after its arrival` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.itemsPerAction", part: "orders", phrase: `one key touch for up to ${O.itemsPerAction} posts` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.holdWarningDays", part: "orders", phrase: `alerted daily in the last ${O.holdWarningDays} days before any release` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "orders", phrase: `the address is kept for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.reportHoldDays", part: "upgrading", phrase: `keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most ${O.reportHoldDays} days` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.copyOverdueHours", part: "orders", phrase: `once the newest copy is more than ${O.copyOverdueHours} hours old` },
  { constant: "ORDER_RULES.quietMinutes", part: "owners", phrase: `bounded only by the quiet period of ${O.quietMinutes} minutes` },
];

/** What names a reference and is no number of the runbook's, taken out before the digits are counted; only the second keeps a group, the character before the name. */
const REFERENCES: RegExp[] = [
  // A path, a file or a regulation's number: whatever holds a slash.
  /[A-Za-z0-9_.()-]*[/][A-Za-z0-9_./-]+/g,
  // A sub-project's name (3f, 3d, 1b) and a phone check (P1 to P8).
  /(^|[^0-9A-Za-z])([0-9][a-f]|P[1-8])(?=[^0-9A-Za-z]|$)/gm,
  // A list's numbering.
  /^[0-9]+[.] /gm,
  // An article of an act, with its paragraphs.
  /Art(?:icle|[.]) [0-9]+(?:[(][0-9a-z]+[)])*/g,
  // A finding of the research, with its questions; a row of the design's section 2, and the section itself.
  /(?:OL|AU) E[0-9]+[.][0-9]+(?: questions [0-9]+ to [0-9]+)?/g,
  /[(]rows? [0-9]+(?: and [0-9]+)?[)]/g,
  /section [0-9]+/g,
  // A step of a list named in a sentence.
  /steps? [0-9]+/g,
  // An instant as an example of the form, a date of the year, the hand-over's user, a hash's name, a status's code.
  /[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9:]+Z/g,
  /[0-9]+ March/g,
  /uid [0-9]+/g,
  /sha256/g,
  /answers 503/g,
];

describe("the README's authorities' orders say what the constants say (3f design, section 13, Task 7; W.9 and W.10)", () => {
  test("the README has the section Authorities' orders after Moderation, and each of its parts stands there once, in W.9's order", () => {
    const lines = readmeLines();
    expect(lines.indexOf(ORDERS_HEADING)).toBeGreaterThan(lines.indexOf("## Moderation"));
    const section = sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING).map(withoutCodeMarks);
    const at = ORDERS_TITLES.map((title) => section.findIndex((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)));
    for (const title of ORDERS_TITLES) expect(section.filter((line) => line.startsWith(`**${title}`)), title).toHaveLength(1);
    expect([...at].sort((a, b) => a - b)).toEqual(at);
  });

  test("Before going public holds the owner's list of thirteen, each line by its title, in W.10's order", () => {
    const owners = linesFrom(sectionLines("## Before going public"), OWNERS_LEAD, "Set these in").filter((line) => /^[0-9]+[.] /.test(line));
    expect(owners.map((line) => line.slice(0, line.indexOf(" ")))).toEqual(OWNERS_TITLES.map((_, n) => `${n + 1}.`));
    for (const [n, title] of OWNERS_TITLES.entries()) expect(owners[n]!.startsWith(`${n + 1}. **${title}`), title).toBe(true);
  });

  test("every number of 3f's text stands in its sentence with the constant's value", () => {
    const parts = ordersParts();
    for (const row of ORDER_NUMBERS) expect(parts[row.part], `${row.constant}: ${row.phrase}`).toContain(row.phrase);
  });

  test("and no other number: every run of digits in it is a constant's, outside what names a reference", () => {
    const values = new Set<string>([...Object.values(O), ...Object.values(A)].filter((value) => typeof value === "number").map(String));
    const outside = REFERENCES.reduce((text, pattern) => text.replace(pattern, (_match: string, lead: unknown) => (typeof lead === "string" ? `${lead} ` : " ")), ordersText());
    expect((outside.match(/[0-9]+/g) ?? []).filter((digits) => !values.has(digits))).toEqual([]);
  });

  test("a setting is written as the operator sets it in infra/.env: an API setting with its prefix", () => {
    const withMarks = [sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Upgrading"), "Authorities' orders and the alert channel"), linesFrom(sectionLines("## Restoring"), "**Restoring with the keeper's copy**")]
      .flatMap((lines) => withoutFences(lines))
      .join("\n");
    for (const name of ["NOTIFY", "REPORT_HOLD", "MODERATION_RETENTION", "HOME_STATE", "CONTACT_POINT", "PUSH_ORIGIN", "APP_ORIGIN"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(`${CODE_MARK}${name}`), name).toBe(false);
    }
    for (const name of ["API_CONTACT_POINT", "API_HOME_STATE", "API_REPORT_HOLD", "API_MODERATION_RETENTION", "APP_SITE", "COMPOSE_PROFILES", "WEB_CONTACT_POINT", "WEB_HOME_STATE"]) {
      expect(withMarks.includes(name) || ordersText().includes(name), name).toBe(true);
    }
  });

  test("the hand-over's and the yearly counts' commands stand in the runbook as the operator types them", () => {
    const orders = ordersParts().orders;
    for (const words of [
      "docker compose --profile handover run --rm -T -v <directory>:/handover handover < list > digests",
      "handover-list",
      "handover-record",
      "handover-destroyed",
      "staff.js tco-counts <last year>",
      "docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js address-check --handle <handle> < address",
    ]) {
      expect(orders, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(readmeLines().join("\n")).toContain("docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm migrate node dist/staff.js tco-counts <year>");
  });

  test("3f's review: a sentence of Restoring or of the orders' runbook that sets APP_SITE recreates Caddy alone, and one that sets an API switch names the start that reads it", () => {
    // Caddy reads APP_SITE only when its container is created, and the API reads its switches only at its start: a
    // setting in infra/.env alone changes nothing. Without --no-deps Compose would start the API with Caddy.
    const sentences = [...sectionLines("## Restoring"), ...sectionLines(ORDERS_HEADING)].flatMap((line) => line.split(/(?<=[.;])\s+(?=[A-Z`(])/));
    const site = sentences.filter((sentence) => sentence.includes("`APP_SITE="));
    const api = sentences.filter((sentence) => /`API_[A-Z_]+=/.test(sentence));
    expect(site.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
    expect(api.length).toBeGreaterThanOrEqual(4);
    for (const sentence of site) expect(sentence, sentence).toContain("up -d --no-deps caddy");
    for (const sentence of api) expect(sentence, sentence).toContain("up -d api");
    // operations5: a message moved between the two folders is a second row; the runbook says not to, and what then.
    expect(ordersParts().orders).toContain("Never move a message between the inbox and the junk folder");
    expect(ordersParts().orders).toContain("close the second row on Contact point with the first row's word");
  });

  test("the lines 3f made false are gone, and the hard gate reads as W.10 words it", () => {
    const all = readmeLines().join("\n");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Until sub-project 3f's off-server copy of decisions");
    expect(all).not.toContain("take the app's public hostname off the tunnel and leave the console's on");
    expect(all).not.toContain("staff.js account-facts");
    expect(all).not.toContain("account-facts <handle>");
    expect(all).not.toContain("Authorities' orders before 3f.");
    expect(all).not.toContain("in their own records until sub-project 3f");
    expect(all).not.toContain("With sub-project 3f the authorities' contact address is published as well");
    // 3d Task 2 (W.11): the gate's first line reads 3d's quarantine and release; 3d Task 8: and the lists, now that 3d's
    // owner's list stands beside 3f's.
    expect(all).toContain("until sub-project 3f's order path and sub-project 3d's quarantine and release have shipped and the lists below are done");
  });
});

/**

/**
 * 3d Task 2 (design, sections 7.2, 7.3 and W.11): the release's runbook, "A release" under Quarantine, and the steps of
 * Restoring that replay releases. An assessment releases nothing; the leave is recorded with release-leave, withdrawn
 * at once when it was a mistake; release-show prints the record; the backups' day comes from RETENTION.backupDays. After
 * a restore, release-replay, the inventory, the lost leave and the lost withdrawal, and the site that opens only when no
 * gap is left. No line of the README says the software cannot release, and the R2 bullet no longer destroys by hand.
 */
describe("the README's release (3d design, W.11)", () => {
  test("A release stands under Quarantine: an assessment releases nothing, the leave is a fact of its own, a mistaken one is withdrawn, release-show prints the record", () => {
    const lines = readmeLines();
    const at = lines.indexOf("### A release");
    expect(at).toBeGreaterThan(lines.indexOf("## Quarantine"));
    const text = sectionLines("## Quarantine").slice(sectionLines("## Quarantine").indexOf("### A release")).join(" ");
    expect(text).toContain("An authority's assessment is not leave to destroy.");
    expect(text).toContain("staff.js release-leave <seal> --by <authority|court> --reference <text> --day <yyyy-mm-dd> --operator <name>");
    expect(text).toContain("`release-leave --end-untold <leave>`");
    expect(text).toContain("`release-leave --withdraw <leave> --operator <name>`");
    expect(text).toContain("a leave that a release already rests on cannot be withdrawn");
    expect(text).toContain("staff.js release-show <release>");
    expect(text).toContain("korbat promises nobody a destruction");
  });

  test("Restoring replays the releases: release-replay, the inventory first, the lost leave and withdrawal, and the site opens only with no gap left", () => {
    const text = sectionLines("## Restoring").join(" ");
    expect(text).toContain("**Restoring the releases** (sub-project 3d)");
    expect(text).toContain("cat <the keeper's files> | docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js release-replay");
    expect(text).toContain("beginning with step 6 (the inventory)");
    expect(text).toContain("`release-leave <seal> ... --gap <gap>`");
    expect(text).toContain("`release-leave --withdraw <leave> --operator <name> --gap <gap>`");
    expect(text).toContain('the class "Releases and held uploads to replay" included');
  });

  test("the lines 3d's release made false are gone", () => {
    const all = readmeLines().join(" ");
    expect(all).not.toContain("but nothing releases or erases them before 3d");
    expect(all).not.toContain("its software has no function yet to hand them over or to erase them");
    expect(all).not.toContain("before sub-project 3d, the operator copies out or destroys the files");
  });
});

    const kept = readmeLines().find((line) => line.startsWith("- **The kept head.**"))!;

    expect(kept).toContain("`API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL`");

  test("The yearly edition gains the daily value: the job, the keeper's mail and notes, the outside timestamp's settings and the alerts' titles", () => {
    const text = sectionLines("## The yearly edition").join(" ");
    expect(text).toContain("**The yearly edition, the monthly count and the daily value.**");
    for (const words of [
      "`API_HEAD_KEEPER_MAIL`",
      "`API_HEAD_WITNESS`",
      "`API_HEAD_WITNESS_URL`",
      "The keeper keeps each day's mail with the value, the place and the hash",
      `"${ALERT_TEXTS.head_missed.title}" is noted by the keeper`,
      `("${ALERT_TEXTS.head_unwitnessed.title}")`,
      "openssl ts -verify -digest <value> -in <day>.tsr -CAfile <certificates>",
      "docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api",
    ]) {
      expect(text, words).toContain(words);
    }
    expect(withoutCodeMarks(text)).toContain(`the last ${HEAD_RULES.shownDays} days`);
  });

  test("Restoring gains head-restore-mark with the keeper's values for the days after the backup, before the site opens", () => {
    const lines = sectionLines("## Restoring");
    const text = lines.join(" ");
    expect(text).toContain("docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js head-restore-mark <day>:<value> ...");

/**

 * starts while another is still pending is remembered: the writer must await each one.
 */
function memorySink() {
  const chunks: Uint8Array[] = [];
  let busy = false;
  let overlapped = false;
  return {
    async write(chunk: Uint8Array): Promise<void> {
      if (busy) overlapped = true;
      busy = true;
      await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 0));
      chunks.push(Uint8Array.from(chunk));
      busy = false;
    },

    },
    get count() {

  };

 * chunks of its length, failing once `failAfter` chunks were read when asked to. It records how many
 * chunks were read, whether the reading stopped and whether the handle was closed.
 */
function fakeFile(size: number, options: { failAfter?: number; chunk?: Uint8Array } = {}) {
  const chunk = options.chunk ?? new Uint8Array(KIB64);
  const state = { chunks: 0, stopped: false, closed: false };
  const handle = {
    createReadStream({ start = 0, end = size - 1 }: { start?: number; end?: number }): AsyncIterable<Uint8Array> {

            if (options.failAfter !== undefined && state.chunks >= options.failAfter) throw new Error("the disk failed in the middle of the file");
            state.chunks += 1;

interface CentralEntry {

/** Every central directory entry in archive order, found by its signature (none of the test data holds it). */
function centralDirectory(archive: Uint8Array, base = 0): CentralEntry[] {
  const bytes = Buffer.from(archive);
  const entries: CentralEntry[] = [];
  for (let i = 0; i + 46 <= bytes.length; i++) {
    if (bytes.readUInt32LE(i) !== 0x02014b50) continue;
    const nameLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(i + 28);
    const extraLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(i + 30);

      const length = bytes.readUInt16LE(at + 2);
      zip64 = Array.from({ length: length / 8 }, (_, k) => u64(bytes, at + 4 + 8 * k));
    }

      name: bytes.toString("utf8", i + 46, i + 46 + nameLength),
      method: bytes.readUInt16LE(i + 10),
      versionNeeded: bytes.readUInt16LE(i + 6),

      compressed: bytes.readUInt32LE(i + 20),
      size: bytes.readUInt32LE(i + 24),
      offset: bytes.readUInt32LE(i + 42),
      zip64,
    });
  }
  return entries;
}
