```ts
import { describe, expect, test } from "vitest";
import { AUTOMATION_RULES, STANDING_RULES } from "@korbat/contracts";
import { REDRESS_TEXTS, REDRESS_VERSION, RULEBOOKS, RULES, RULES_CHANGES, RULES_VERSION, getRedress, getRule, isRuleId, ORDER_NOTICE } from "../src/index";

const VERSIONS = [1, 2, 3, 4] as const;

describe("rulebook", () => {
  test("the current rulebook is version 4 (3d Task 8), and every version is kept: a decision renders with the rules it was made under", () => {
    expect(RULES_VERSION).toBe(4);
    expect(Object.keys(RULEBOOKS).map(Number)).toEqual([...VERSIONS]);
    expect(RULES).toBe(RULEBOOKS[RULES_VERSION]);
  });

  test.each(VERSIONS)("version %i has exactly six rules R1..R6 in order", (version) => {
    expect(RULEBOOKS[version].map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"]);
  });

  test.each(VERSIONS)("every rule of version %i has text and at least one example on each side", (version) => {
    for (const r of RULEBOOKS[version]) {
      expect(r.title.length, r.id).toBeGreaterThan(5);
      expect(r.text.length, r.id).toBeGreaterThan(40);
      expect(r.notAllowed.length, r.id).toBeGreaterThan(0);
      expect(r.allowed.length, r.id).toBeGreaterThan(0);
    }
  });

  test("version 1 is the six rules as they stood: only R2 fully automated, only R1 auto-withheld", () => {
    const v1 = RULEBOOKS[1];
    expect(v1.filter((r) => r.automation === "auto_remove").map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(["R2"]);
    expect(v1.filter((r) => r.automation === "withhold_for_review").map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(["R1"]);
    expect(v1.filter((r) => r.seniorQueue).map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(["R2", "R5"]);
    expect(getRule("R1", 1)?.text).toContain("Images that score high on the automated check are hidden from others until a person reviews them");
    expect(getRule("R2", 1)?.text).toContain("removed automatically on a hash match");
    expect(getRule("R5", 1)?.text).toContain("Cases go to the senior queue.");
    expect(getRule("R6", 1)?.title).toBe("No spam, scams, or impersonation");
  });

  test("version 2 automates nothing: a person decides every case, and R2 and R5 are an admin's", () => {
    const v2 = RULEBOOKS[2];
    expect(v2.filter((r) => r.automation !== "none").map((r) => r.id)).toEqual([]);
    expect(v2.filter((r) => r.seniorQueue).map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(["R2", "R5"]);
  });

  test("version 2's R1 no longer promises an automated check", () => {
    expect(getRule("R1", 2)?.text).toBe(
      "Images or text whose primary purpose is sexual arousal are not allowed. This includes nudity presented sexually, explicit sexual acts, and sexualised depictions of anyone.",
    );
  });

  test("version 2's R2 says that nobody opens reported images, who seals them and who decides", () => {
    expect(getRule("R2", 2)?.text).toBe(
      "Any sexualised depiction of a minor is not allowed. Nobody at korbat opens images that are reported or found as such material while the report is unanswered or the images are sealed. " +
        "After an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image. Whoever is on duty may seal them while an admin decides: sealed images are shown to nobody, their author included. " +
        "An admin either seals them for good, in which case they are kept only for the authorities and reported to them, or answers without a seal. " +
        "Every final decision on a report or finding under this rule, whether it acts or not, and every review of one, is taken by an admin. " +
        "Only an admin can lift a seal, and a seal for good only on the authorities' answer; an appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images.",
    );
  });

  test("version 2's R4 hides on a moderator's decision, never on the number of reports", () => {
    const text = getRule("R4", 2)!.text;
    expect(text.endsWith("When a moderator finds a report credible, the post is hidden from others while the moderator decides, because the harm is immediate. The number of reports never decides it.")).toBe(true);
    expect(text).not.toContain("When a report is credible the post is hidden");
    // Everything before its last sentence is version 1's.
    expect(text.startsWith(getRule("R4", 1)!.text.split(" When a report is credible")[0]!)).toBe(true);
  });

  test("version 2's R5 says who may hide a threat, who decides, and who reviews an appeal", () => {
    const text = getRule("R5", 2)!.text;
    expect(text).not.toContain("senior queue");
    expect(
      text.endsWith(
        "Any moderator may hide a reported threat from others at once while an admin decides, and may lift that again. " +
          "Every final decision on a report under this rule, whether it acts or not, is taken by an admin, and only an admin corrects one. " +
          "An appeal against a restriction under it is reviewed by a moderator who made none of the case's decisions and did not report it themselves, and waits while korbat has none.",
      ),
    ).toBe(true);
  });

  test("version 2's R6 names coordinated manipulation, with its examples on both sides", () => {
    const r6 = getRule("R6", 2)!;
    expect(r6.title).toBe("No spam, scams, impersonation or coordinated manipulation");
    expect(r6.text).toContain("Coordinating several accounts, your own or other people's, to like, repost or report together is not allowed.");
    expect(r6.notAllowed).toEqual(expect.arrayContaining(["A group of accounts liking each other's posts on cue to lift them in Explore", "Reporting someone together to get them removed"]));
    expect(r6.allowed).toContain("Asking your followers to read or share a post");
    // Version 1's examples are all still there.
    for (const example of getRule("R6", 1)!.notAllowed) expect(r6.notAllowed).toContain(example);
    for (const example of getRule("R6", 1)!.allowed) expect(r6.allowed).toContain(example);
  });

  test("version 3 is version 2 with one change, to R6: repeated plainly unfounded reports, after a warning; a notice of illegal content is never restricted", () => {
    const [v2, v3] = [RULEBOOKS[2], RULEBOOKS[3]];
    for (const id of ["R1", "R2", "R3", "R4", "R5"]) expect(getRule(id, 3), id).toEqual(getRule(id, 2));
    expect(v3.filter((r) => r.automation !== "none").map((r) => r.id)).toEqual([]);
    expect(v3.filter((r) => r.seniorQueue).map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(v2.filter((r) => r.seniorQueue).map((r) => r.id));
    const [r6v2, r6v3] = [getRule("R6", 2)!, getRule("R6", 3)!];
    expect(r6v3.title).toBe(r6v2.title);
    expect(r6v3.text).toBe(
      `${r6v2.text} Sending report after report that is plainly unfounded is not allowed either: after a warning, korbat may stop taking an account's reports under these rules for a limited time. A notice of illegal content is never restricted.`,
    );
    expect(r6v3.notAllowed).toEqual([...r6v2.notAllowed, "Reporting the same account again and again for posts that plainly break no rule"]);
    expect(r6v3.allowed).toEqual([...r6v2.allowed, "Reporting in good faith something that turns out to break no rule"]);
  });

  test("version 4 (3d design, W.4): version 3 with R1's and R2's texts grown by what a program may do, R2's sentence on staff's look gaining its exception, and the two new automation values; R3 to R6 unchanged", () => {
    const [v3, v4] = [RULEBOOKS[3], RULEBOOKS[4]];
    for (const id of ["R3", "R4", "R5", "R6"]) expect(getRule(id, 4), id).toEqual(getRule(id, 3));
    expect(v4.map((r) => [r.id, r.automation])).toEqual([
      ["R1", "flag_or_withhold"],
      ["R2", "seal_for_review"],
      ["R3", "none"],
      ["R4", "none"],
      ["R5", "none"],
      ["R6", "none"],
    ]);
    expect(v4.filter((r) => r.seniorQueue).map((r) => r.id)).toEqual(v3.filter((r) => r.seniorQueue).map((r) => r.id));
    const [r1v3, r1v4] = [getRule("R1", 3)!, getRule("R1", 4)!];
    expect({ ...r1v4, text: undefined, automation: undefined }).toEqual({ ...r1v3, text: undefined, automation: undefined });
    expect(r1v4.text).toBe(
      `${r1v3.text} korbat may let a program rate uploaded images against this rule. An image it rates as likely within the rule is put before a moderator, and korbat may hide that one image from other people until the moderator has decided; its author still sees it, is told at once and can ask for a person. No program removes anything or judges text. Whether a program runs and what runs today is stated under Automation on the rules page.`,
    );
    const [r2v3, r2v4] = [getRule("R2", 3)!, getRule("R2", 4)!];
    expect({ ...r2v4, text: undefined, automation: undefined }).toEqual({ ...r2v3, text: undefined, automation: undefined });
    const before = "After an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image.";
    expect(r2v3.text).toContain(before);
    expect(r2v4.text).toBe(
      `${r2v3.text.replace(before, "After an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image, except an image that an automated comparison matched: korbat's staff do not open such an image at any time.")} korbat may compare the fingerprint of an uploaded image with lists of images that a named body has classified as child sexual abuse material. An upload that the body reports as an exact match with such an entry is not accepted, now or later, and is held unseen until an admin has decided what happens to the file. When an image that is already on a post matches in that way, it is put before an admin at once, korbat keeps that post's images until the admin has answered, and korbat may seal them at once until then. A match with such an entry that the body does not report as exact refuses no upload and is never sealed by a program; on a post it is put before an admin in the same way, and korbat keeps that post's images until the admin has answered. A match is a comparison of fingerprints, not korbat's finding about an image; korbat's staff do not open an image that a match names; and nothing is removed by a program. Whether a comparison runs, with which body, and what runs today is stated under Automation on the rules page.`,
    );
    // The words of every text of 3d (section 18, rule 1): no text says what a match or a score does not show.
    for (const rule of v4) expect(rule.text, rule.id).not.toMatch(/is child sexual abuse material|confirmed|posted such/);
    // Versions 1 to 3 render as sent: their automation values are the old ones.
    expect(RULEBOOKS[3].map((r) => r.automation)).toEqual(["none", "none", "none", "none", "none", "none"]);
  });

  test("R3 reads the same in both versions", () => {
    expect(getRule("R3", 2)).toEqual(getRule("R3", 1));
  });

  test("getRule reads a rule of one version, the current one unless told, and isRuleId knows the six ids", () => {
    expect(getRule("R3")?.title).toMatch(/hatred/i);
    expect(getRule("R6")).toBe(getRule("R6", RULES_VERSION));
    expect(getRule("R6", 1)?.title).not.toBe(getRule("R6", 2)?.title);
    expect(getRule("R9")).toBeUndefined();
    expect(getRule("R1", 5)).toBeUndefined();
    expect(isRuleId("R6")).toBe(true);
    expect(isRuleId("x")).toBe(false);
  });
});

describe("redress", () => {
  const LAST = "You can also go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";

  test("the current redress version is 4 (3d Task 6); version 3 is version 2's nine texts word for word and the order's notice; versions 1 to 3 are kept as they were", () => {
    expect(REDRESS_VERSION).toBe(4);
    expect(Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS).map(Number)).toEqual([1, 2, 3, 4]);
    expect(Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[1])).toEqual(["appeal", "interim", "notAppealable"]);
    expect(Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[2])).toEqual(["appeal", "interim", "notAppealable", "strikeNext", "reply", "replyAtOnce", "replyAnswered", "warnNext", "appealNow"]);
    for (const key of ["appeal", "interim", "notAppealable"] as const) expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[2][key], key).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[1][key]);
    // 3f (design, section 10.7; W.3): version 3 adds the group `order` and changes no sentence of version 2.
    expect(Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[3])).toEqual([...Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[2]), "order"]);
    for (const key of Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[2]) as (keyof (typeof REDRESS_TEXTS)[2])[]) expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[3][key], key).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[2][key]);
    expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[3].order).toBe(ORDER_NOTICE);
    expect(getRedress(REDRESS_VERSION)).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[4]);
    expect(getRedress(3)).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[3]);
    expect(getRedress(2)).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[2]);
    expect(getRedress(1)).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[1]);
    expect(getRedress(5)).toBeUndefined();
  });

  test("version 4 (3d design, W.4): version 3's texts word for word, and the three of a program's measure and of a refused upload", () => {
    expect(Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[4])).toEqual([...Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[3]), "askPerson", "askAdmin", "uploadObject"]);
    for (const key of Object.keys(REDRESS_TEXTS[3]) as (keyof (typeof REDRESS_TEXTS)[3])[]) expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[4][key], key).toBe(REDRESS_TEXTS[3][key]);
    const v4 = REDRESS_TEXTS[4];
    expect(v4.askPerson).toBe(
      `You can ask for a person now: choose "Ask for a person" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and write anything a person should know. You can send one message. korbat's target is that a moderator answers within 24 hours; the measure does not end by itself before a person has decided. A measure a program takes cannot be appealed as such: ask for a person instead. The moderator's decision can be appealed, if it restricts your post. ${LAST}`,
    );
    expect(v4.askAdmin).toBe(
      `You can ask for a person now: choose "Ask for a person" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and write anything a person should know. You can send one message. korbat's target is that an admin answers within 24 hours; the measure does not end by itself before a person has decided. A measure a program takes cannot be appealed as such: ask for a person instead. The admin's decision can be appealed, if it seals the images for good; an appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images. ${LAST}`,
    );
    expect(v4.uploadObject).toBe(
      `You can object, free of charge: choose "Object" on this screen and write anything the admin should know. You can send one message, at any time before the hold is lifted or korbat has released the file, also after an admin has decided to report it. An admin, not a program, decides what happens to the file. Nobody at korbat can accept the image, since nobody opens it. ${LAST}`,
    );
  });

  test("the one number of version 4's texts is held to AUTOMATION_RULES: a changed target is a new version", () => {
    const numbers = (text: string) => [...text.matchAll(/[0-9]+/g)].map((match) => Number(match[0]));
    for (const key of ["askPerson", "askAdmin"] as const) expect(numbers(REDRESS_TEXTS[4][key]), key).toEqual([AUTOMATION_RULES.objectionTargetHours, 53]);
    expect(numbers(REDRESS_TEXTS[4].uploadObject)).toEqual([53]);
  });

  test("version 2's six new texts, word for word (3e design, section 18, W.3)", () => {
    const v2 = REDRESS_TEXTS[2];
    expect(v2.strikeNext).toBe(
      "A strike restricts nothing by itself. When an account has 3 active strikes, a moderator may decide to suspend it for a limited time or, after three suspensions in 365 days, an admin may decide to terminate it. You would be told first and could reply before anything is restricted.",
    );
    expect(v2.reply).toBe(
      `Before it starts you can reply: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and say anything you want the moderator to weigh. A reply sent before the start holds the start until a moderator has read it and answered you; if the decision is kept, it then starts with the answer, and never before the time you were given. A reply sent later is read and answered too, and can end this measure, but does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
    );
    expect(v2.replyAtOnce).toBe(
      `You can reply at any time while it runs: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator reads your reply and answers you, and can end this measure at once; the reply does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
    );
    expect(v2.replyAnswered).toBe(
      `This answer is not appealed by itself. The appeal is against the decision it keeps: once, free of charge, until {deadline}, with "Appeal" on that decision's screen under Settings, Cases. The six months for it count from this answer when you replied before the start, and otherwise from the day you were told of that decision. ${LAST}`,
    );
    expect(v2.warnNext).toBe("If 3 of the reports you send after this warning are marked that way while it counts, a moderator may restrict your reports under korbat's rules for up to 30 days.");
    expect(v2.appealNow).toBe("You can appeal from now; you do not have to wait for the start. An appeal does not hold the start: only a reply sent before the start does.");
  });

  test("every number in version 2's texts is held to STANDING_RULES: a changed number is a new version, so an old statement keeps its own", () => {
    const v2 = REDRESS_TEXTS[2];
    const words = ["zero", "one", "two", "three", "four", "five"];
    expect(v2.strikeNext).toContain(`When an account has ${STANDING_RULES.ladderStrikes} active strikes`);
    expect(v2.strikeNext).toContain(`after ${words[STANDING_RULES.ladderDays.length]} suspensions in ${STANDING_RULES.ladderMemoryDays} days`);
    expect(v2.warnNext).toContain(`If ${STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictMarks} of the reports`);
    expect(v2.warnNext).toContain(`for up to ${STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictDays} days`);
    // No other number is typed into them.
    const numbers = (text: string) => [...text.matchAll(/[0-9]+/g)].map((match) => Number(match[0]));
    expect(numbers(v2.strikeNext)).toEqual([STANDING_RULES.ladderStrikes, STANDING_RULES.ladderMemoryDays]);
    expect(numbers(v2.warnNext)).toEqual([STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictMarks, STANDING_RULES.reportRestrictDays]);
    for (const key of ["reply", "replyAtOnce", "appealNow"] as const) expect(numbers(v2[key]), key).toEqual([]);
    // Article 53 of the Digital Services Act is a law's number, not one of korbat's.
    expect(numbers(v2.replyAnswered)).toEqual([53]);
  });

  test("the appeal's text names its deadline, the courts and the Digital Services Coordinator", () => {
    // Version 1's text is fixed: a decision names the version it was made under, and its statement quotes this text for good.
    expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[1].appeal).toBe(
      `You can appeal this decision once, free of charge, within six months of being told, until {deadline}: choose "Appeal" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator who took no part in the case reviews it. ${LAST}`,
    );
  });

  test("the interim text is the one of a decision taken while deciding", () => {
    expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[1].interim).toBe(
      `This applies while korbat decides, and ends with its decision. If korbat's decision restricts your post or profile, you can appeal it. ${LAST}`,
    );
  });

  test("the third text is the one of a decision its author cannot appeal", () => {
    expect(REDRESS_TEXTS[1].notAppealable).toBe(
      "korbat's appeal does not apply to this decision. Where an earlier decision about this content still stands in part, its own screen in korbat says whether you can still appeal it. " +
        "You can go to court, or complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).",
    );
  });
});

describe("the rulebook's change log", () => {
  test("RULES_CHANGES has one entry a version of RULEBOOKS, oldest first, each with a day and W.1's sentence", () => {
    expect(RULES_CHANGES.map((change) => change.version)).toEqual(Object.keys(RULEBOOKS).map(Number));
    expect(RULES_CHANGES.at(-1)!.version).toBe(RULES_VERSION);
    expect(RULES_CHANGES).toEqual([
      { version: 1, date: "2026-09-14", summary: "The six rules as first published." },
      {
        version: 2,
        date: "2026-10-04",
        summary:
          "A person decides every case; the automated checks that R1 and R2 named are withdrawn until they exist. R2 says how reported images are handled without anyone opening them. R4 and R5 say who may hide content while a case is decided and who decides it. R6 names coordinated manipulation.",
      },
      { version: 3, date: "2026-10-12", summary: "R6 names repeated, plainly unfounded reporting." },
      // 3d Task 8 (W.1, W.4): the day the version came into force, a literal written by the task that ships it.
      { version: 4, date: "2026-10-19", summary: "R1 and R2 say what an automated tool may do when one is switched on, and point to the list of what runs today." },
    ]);
    const days = RULES_CHANGES.map((change) => change.date);
    expect([...days].sort()).toEqual(days);
  });
});
```

### Create `packages/db/migrations/0040_signals_and_retention.sql`

```sql
-- Written by hand (3d design, sections 2 rows 33, 37 and 47, 6.8, 6.9, 6.10, 7.13 and 7.14; Task 8), through
-- generate:custom: it changes no table, so a second generate prints "No schema changes". The design numbers this migration
-- 0037; earlier tasks of 3d added migrations the design did not foresee (3f ended at 0032), so it is 0040.
-- As in 0016 to 0039: every function is owned by the migrator, pins its search path to public and pg_temp, names every
-- object schema-qualified and has EXECUTE taken from PUBLIC; an error carries its code as the message under SQLSTATE
-- P0001. Neither function names a value that 0038 added to intake_kind or intake_channel, as an enum literal or as text
-- (the stricter form of the enum-literal rule, which enum-literals.test.ts reads this file under), and neither holds an
-- interval literal or a number of automation_rules(): case_flag's four numbers are its own, and erase_automation_records
-- reads match_keep_days from automation_rules().

-- 1. case_flag(case_id): the flag "possible coordinated reporting" (row 47, 7.13), computed at read from rows 3c already
-- keeps, STABLE, a definer, EXECUTE to the API's role alone. In this order:
--   1. the case's unanswered items of signed-in reporters (intake_items with answered_by null and reporter_account_id not
--      null), each with its created_at. An item whose reporter retention forgot (forget_reporter, C 6.4) has none, and a
--      signed-out notice never had one, so neither counts: the flag goes dark by itself;
--   2. among the windows of window_minutes that begin at one of those items (from the item's time, up to but not
--      including the window's end), the one with the most distinct reporters, then the most items, then the earliest;
--      `items` and `reporters` are its two counts (0 and 0 when there is none);
--   3. `coordinated` is true when items is at least min_items, reporters is at least min_reporters, and at least
--      linked_share of those reporters follow, or are followed by, another of them (public.follows).
-- Its four numbers are constants of this function, in the CTE `rules`, mirrored by the contracts' SIGNAL_RULES (a test
-- reads them from the function's text and holds them to it). It answers counts and never a reporter: the reporters'
-- array never leaves the statement. It keeps nothing, and no function, view, index or decision names it: the API calls
-- it from the queue's read and the case answer's read alone (row 48).
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."case_flag"(case_id uuid) RETURNS TABLE (coordinated boolean, items integer, reporters integer)
LANGUAGE sql STABLE SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
  WITH rules AS (
    SELECT 5 AS min_items, 5 AS min_reporters, 60 AS window_minutes, 0.5::numeric AS linked_share
  ), open_items AS (
    SELECT i.reporter_account_id AS reporter, i.created_at
      FROM public.intake_items i
     WHERE i.case_id = case_flag.case_id AND i.answered_by IS NULL AND i.reporter_account_id IS NOT NULL
  ), windows AS (
    SELECT w.start, count(*)::integer AS items, count(DISTINCT o.reporter)::integer AS reporters, array_agg(DISTINCT o.reporter) AS who
      FROM (SELECT DISTINCT x.created_at AS start FROM open_items x) w
      CROSS JOIN rules r
      JOIN open_items o ON o.created_at >= w.start AND o.created_at < w.start + make_interval(mins => r.window_minutes)
     GROUP BY w.start
  ), best AS (
    SELECT b.items, b.reporters, b.who FROM windows b ORDER BY b.reporters DESC, b.items DESC, b.start LIMIT 1
  ), linked AS (
    SELECT count(*)::integer AS n
      FROM best b CROSS JOIN LATERAL unnest(b.who) AS r(id)
     WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.follows f
                    WHERE (f.follower_id = r.id AND f.followee_id = ANY (b.who) AND f.followee_id <> r.id)
                       OR (f.followee_id = r.id AND f.follower_id = ANY (b.who) AND f.follower_id <> r.id))
  )
  SELECT coalesce(b.items >= r.min_items AND b.reporters >= r.min_reporters AND l.n >= r.linked_share * b.reporters, false),
         coalesce(b.items, 0),
         coalesce(b.reporters, 0)
    FROM rules r LEFT JOIN best b ON true LEFT JOIN linked l ON true
$$;--> statement-breakpoint

-- 2. erase_automation_records(): the retention job's step automation_records (6.8, 6.10, 7.14), called in every round,
-- a definer, EXECUTE to the API's role alone. It answers how many rows it changed. The guards of media_matches and
-- upload_refusals let the migrator through (0039), which is who this function runs as. In this order:
--   1. Match records. A record of media_matches gets hash and classification null and erased_at when match_keep_days
--      have passed since its anchor: for a refusal's record, the release of the refusal or its end as no_report (an
--      unended hold, or one ended as report and not released, keeps it); for a record with a case, the release of the
--      case's post when it is in release_posts, else the case's closing, and never while a seal for good in force lists a
--      post of the case, or the case's own post, that is not in release_posts; and with neither (a flagged upload that
--      was never posted), its queried_at. So a post's record and an upload's end the same way: the hash of a file korbat
--      released goes match_keep_days after the release, as the terms' list says. Then every refusal whose record is
--      erased loses its owner_id and its objection (review ruling 6): its row stays with its times, its end and its
--      release, and names nobody.
--   2. Objections. An automated_objections row gets text null and erased_at once its decision's texts are due by 3c's
--      schedule: the test of erase_statement_texts (0018), applied by calling it, which raises not_due until the
--      decision's subject account has been deleted for 3c's months. A decision without a decider has no text of its own,
--      so the call erases nothing and only answers whether the decision's texts are due. Only an objection whose subject
--      is deleted at all is tried.
--   3. Signals, once handled. A signal that no statement reads (one handled as gone, which has neither an item nor a
--      decision) is deleted: a match's once its record is erased, a score's match_keep_days after it was handled. A
--      signal that a statement reads (it names a decision, or its finding's item) is the record of the automated means
--      that decision's statement prints, and the statement reads it at every render (DecisionStatement.signal): it is
--      deleted under the same conditions (a match's record erased; a score's intake erased) and only once the texts of
--      its case's decisions are due, by the same test as the objections. The sweep reads a match's handled mark on the
--      record itself (review ruling 8), so no deletion here can make it act twice.
-- It never touches releases, release_posts, release_leaves, release_notices or quarantine_files: it reads the first two
-- for a release's time and writes none of them. The forgetting of hashes and scores once a tool is off is not here: it is
-- the media module's two statements in the same round (section 5).
CREATE FUNCTION "public"."erase_automation_records"() RETURNS integer
LANGUAGE plpgsql SECURITY DEFINER SET search_path = public, pg_temp AS $$
DECLARE
  v_keep interval;
  v_changed integer := 0;
  v_rows integer;
  v_id uuid;
  v_decision uuid;
  v_due boolean;
BEGIN
  SELECT make_interval(days => a.match_keep_days) INTO v_keep FROM public.automation_rules() a;

  -- 1. Match records, then the refusals whose record is erased.
  UPDATE public.media_matches m SET hash = NULL, classification = NULL, erased_at = now()
   WHERE m.erased_at IS NULL
     AND CASE
           WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.upload_refusals u WHERE u.match_id = m.id) THEN
             (SELECT coalesce((SELECT r.released_at FROM public.releases r WHERE r.id = u.release_id),
                              CASE WHEN u.end_as = 'no_report' THEN u.ended_at END)
                FROM public.upload_refusals u WHERE u.match_id = m.id ORDER BY u.refused_at DESC LIMIT 1) <= now() - v_keep
           WHEN m.case_id IS NOT NULL THEN
             (SELECT coalesce((SELECT r.released_at FROM public.release_posts p JOIN public.releases r ON r.id = p.release_id
                                WHERE c.target_type = 'post' AND p.post_id = c.target_id),
                              c.closed_at)
                FROM public.cases c WHERE c.id = m.case_id) <= now() - v_keep
             AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.seal_posts s JOIN public.measures_in_force f ON f.id = s.action_id
                              WHERE f.kind = 'seal_media' AND f.decision_kind <> 'interim'
                                AND (f.case_id = m.case_id
                                     OR s.post_id = (SELECT c.target_id FROM public.cases c WHERE c.id = m.case_id AND c.target_type = 'post'))
                                AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.release_posts p WHERE p.post_id = s.post_id))
           ELSE m.queried_at <= now() - v_keep
         END;
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_changed := v_changed + v_rows;
  UPDATE public.upload_refusals u SET owner_id = NULL, objection = NULL
   WHERE (u.owner_id IS NOT NULL OR u.objection IS NOT NULL)
     AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.media_matches m WHERE m.id = u.match_id AND m.erased_at IS NOT NULL);
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_changed := v_changed + v_rows;

  -- 2. Objections whose decision's texts are due.
  FOR v_decision IN
    SELECT o.decision_id
      FROM public.automated_objections o
      JOIN public.decisions d ON d.id = o.decision_id
      JOIN public.cases k ON k.id = d.case_id
      JOIN auth.users u ON u.id = CASE WHEN k.target_type = 'post' THEN (SELECT p.author_id FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = k.target_id) ELSE k.target_id END
     WHERE o.erased_at IS NULL AND u.deleted_at IS NOT NULL
     ORDER BY o.decision_id
  LOOP
    v_due := true;
    BEGIN
      PERFORM public.erase_statement_texts(v_decision);
    EXCEPTION WHEN raise_exception THEN
      IF SQLERRM <> 'not_due' THEN
        RAISE;
      END IF;
      v_due := false;
    END;
    IF v_due THEN
      UPDATE public.automated_objections o SET text = NULL, erased_at = now() WHERE o.decision_id = v_decision AND o.erased_at IS NULL;
      GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
      v_changed := v_changed + v_rows;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;

  -- 3. Signals. First those no statement reads: handled as gone, with neither an item nor a decision.
  DELETE FROM public.automated_signals s
   WHERE s.handled_at IS NOT NULL AND s.intake_item_id IS NULL AND s.decision_id IS NULL
     AND ((s.kind = 'known_match' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.media_matches m WHERE m.id = s.match_id AND m.erased_at IS NOT NULL))
          OR (s.kind = 'r1_score' AND s.handled = 'gone' AND s.handled_at <= now() - v_keep));
  GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
  v_changed := v_changed + v_rows;
  -- Then those a statement reads, once the texts of their case's decisions are due: one decision of the case is tested
  -- (the signal's own, else the case's first), since every decision of a case has the case's subject.
  FOR v_id, v_decision IN
    SELECT s.id, coalesce(s.decision_id, (SELECT d.id FROM public.decisions d WHERE d.case_id = x.case_id ORDER BY d.decided_at, d.id LIMIT 1))
      FROM public.automated_signals s
      LEFT JOIN public.intake_items i ON i.id = s.intake_item_id
      CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT coalesce(i.case_id, (SELECT d.case_id FROM public.decisions d WHERE d.id = s.decision_id)) AS case_id) x
      JOIN public.cases k ON k.id = x.case_id
      JOIN auth.users u ON u.id = CASE WHEN k.target_type = 'post' THEN (SELECT p.author_id FROM public.posts p WHERE p.id = k.target_id) ELSE k.target_id END
     WHERE s.handled_at IS NOT NULL AND (s.intake_item_id IS NOT NULL OR s.decision_id IS NOT NULL) AND u.deleted_at IS NOT NULL
       AND ((s.kind = 'known_match' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.media_matches m WHERE m.id = s.match_id AND m.erased_at IS NOT NULL))
            OR (s.kind = 'r1_score' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.intakes n WHERE n.id = i.intake_id AND n.erased_at IS NOT NULL)))
     ORDER BY s.id
  LOOP
    -- A case without a decision has no statement to test by; its signal waits.
    IF v_decision IS NULL THEN
      CONTINUE;
    END IF;
    v_due := true;
    BEGIN
      PERFORM public.erase_statement_texts(v_decision);
    EXCEPTION WHEN raise_exception THEN
      IF SQLERRM <> 'not_due' THEN
        RAISE;
      END IF;
      v_due := false;
    END;
    IF v_due THEN
      DELETE FROM public.automated_signals s WHERE s.id = v_id;
      GET DIAGNOSTICS v_rows = ROW_COUNT;
      v_changed := v_changed + v_rows;
    END IF;
  END LOOP;

  RETURN v_changed;
END $$;--> statement-breakpoint
REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_automation_records"() FROM PUBLIC;--> statement-breakpoint
GRANT EXECUTE ON FUNCTION "public"."erase_automation_records"() TO korbat_api;
```

```json
        },
        "decisions_category": {
          "name": "decisions_category",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "decisions_category_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_TERRORIST_CONTENT')"
        },
        "decisions_automated_decision": {
          "name": "decisions_automated_decision",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" in ('fully', 'partially', 'not_automated')"
        },
        "decisions_territorial_scope": {
          "name": "decisions_territorial_scope",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"territorial_scope\" = 'worldwide'"
        },
        "decisions_review_target": {
          "name": "decisions_review_target",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"kind\" in ('review', 'correction')) = (\"decisions\".\"reviews_decision_id\" is not null) and (\"decisions\".\"kind\" = 'review') = (\"decisions\".\"appeal_id\" is not null)"
        },
        "decisions_interim": {
          "name": "decisions_interim",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" <> 'interim' or \"decisions\".\"through_seq\" = 0"
        },
        "decisions_ground_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'incompatible' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is not null"
        },
        "decisions_ground_law": {
          "name": "decisions_ground_law",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_restricted": {
          "name": "decisions_restricted",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"outcome\" <> 'restricted' or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is not null and ((\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is not null and \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is not null) or \"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is null)) or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'order'"
        },
        "decisions_decider": {
          "name": "decisions_decider",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is null) = (\"decisions\".\"automated_decision\" = 'fully') and (\"decisions\".\"decided_by\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"kind\"::text = 'interim')"
        },
        "decisions_match_answer_reason": {
          "name": "decisions_match_answer_reason",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"match_answer_reason\" in ('source_withdrew', 'counsel', 'other')"
        },
        "decisions_informed": {
          "name": "decisions_informed",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"informed_at\" is not null or \"decisions\".\"author_mail\"::text = 'none'"
        },
        "decisions_digests": {
          "name": "decisions_digests",
          "value": "(\"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"reason_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$') and (\"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null or \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$')"
        },
        "decisions_keyword": {
          "name": "decisions_keyword",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null or \"decisions\".\"ground\" is not distinct from 'illegal'"
        },
        "decisions_law_no_rule": {
          "name": "decisions_law_no_rule",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"ground\" is distinct from 'illegal' or \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null"
        },
        "decisions_reversal_plain": {
          "name": "decisions_reversal_plain",
          "value": "\"decisions\".\"kind\" not in ('review', 'correction') or (\"decisions\".\"ground\" is null and \"decisions\".\"rule_id\" is null and \"decisions\".\"category_keyword\" is null and \"decisions\".\"facts_digest\" is null and \"decisions\".\"legal_reference_digest\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

        }

      "checkConstraints": {
        "intakes_ref": {
          "name": "intakes_ref",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"ref\" ~ '^N-[A-Z2-7]{10}$'"
        },
        "intakes_rule_id": {
          "name": "intakes_rule_id",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2', 'R3', 'R4', 'R5', 'R6')"
        },
        "intakes_category": {
          "name": "intakes_category",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category\" in ('STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ANIMAL_WELFARE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CONSUMER_INFORMATION', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_CYBER_VIOLENCE_AGAINST_WOMEN', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_DATA_PROTECTION_AND_PRIVACY_VIOLATIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_ILLEGAL_OR_HARMFUL_SPEECH', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_INTELLECTUAL_PROPERTY_INFRINGEMENTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NEGATIVE_EFFECTS_ON_CIVIC_DISCOURSE_OR_ELECTIONS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_NOT_SPECIFIED_NOTICE', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_RISK_FOR_PUBLIC_SECURITY', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SCAMS_AND_FRAUD', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_SELF_HARM', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_UNSAFE_AND_PROHIBITED_PRODUCTS', 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_VIOLENCE')"
        },
        "intakes_category_keyword": {
          "name": "intakes_category_keyword",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"category_keyword\" in ('KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL', 'KEYWORD_CHILD_SEXUAL_ABUSE_MATERIAL_DEEPFAKE', 'KEYWORD_GROOMING_SEXUAL_ENTICEMENT_MINORS')"
        },
        "intakes_cited_law_len": {
          "name": "intakes_cited_law_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"cited_law\") <= 300"
        },
        "intakes_explanation_len": {
          "name": "intakes_explanation_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"intakes\".\"explanation\") <= 2000"
        },
        "intakes_has_ground": {
          "name": "intakes_has_ground",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or \"intakes\".\"kind\"::text = 'automated'"
        },
        "intakes_illegal_elements": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_elements",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'user' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"bona_fide\" and (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is not null or \"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is not null))"
        },
        "intakes_finding_legal": {
          "name": "intakes_finding_legal",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\" <> 'finding' or not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\""
        },
        "intakes_illegal_not_tc": {
          "name": "intakes_illegal_not_tc",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" or \"intakes\".\"category\" <> 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_OTHER_VIOLATION_TC'"
        },
        "intakes_csam": {
          "name": "intakes_csam",
          "value": "not \"intakes\".\"csam\" or (\"intakes\".\"category\" = 'STATEMENT_CATEGORY_PROTECTION_OF_MINORS' and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_contact_signed_out": {
          "name": "intakes_contact_signed_out",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out'"
        },
        "intakes_reporter_signed_in": {
          "name": "intakes_reporter_signed_in",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_in'"
        },
        "intakes_finding": {
          "name": "intakes_finding",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is not null) and (\"intakes\".\"kind\" = 'finding') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'staff') and (\"intakes\".\"kind\"::text = 'automated') = (\"intakes\".\"channel\"::text = 'system')"
        },
        "intakes_lookup": {
          "name": "intakes_lookup",
          "value": "(\"intakes\".\"lookup_hash\" is not null) = (\"intakes\".\"channel\" = 'signed_out' or \"intakes\".\"csam\")"
        },
        "intakes_erased": {
          "name": "intakes_erased",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"erased_at\" is null or (\"intakes\".\"explanation\" is null and \"intakes\".\"cited_law\" is null)"
        },
        "intakes_r2_finding_only": {
          "name": "intakes_r2_finding_only",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is distinct from 'R2' or \"intakes\".\"kind\"::text in ('finding', 'automated')"
        },
        "intakes_automated": {
          "name": "intakes_automated",
          "value": "\"intakes\".\"kind\"::text <> 'automated' or (\"intakes\".\"automated_processing\" and (\"intakes\".\"rule_id\" is null or \"intakes\".\"rule_id\" in ('R1', 'R2')) and not \"intakes\".\"alleges_illegal\" and not \"intakes\".\"csam\" and \"intakes\".\"reporter_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"contact_id\" is null and \"intakes\".\"finding_by\" is null)"
        }
      },
      "isRLSEnabled": true
    },

        },
        "legal_orders_member_state": {
          "name": "legal_orders_member_state",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"member_state\" ~ '^[A-Z]{2}$'"
        },
        "legal_orders_names": {
          "name": "legal_orders_names",
          "value": "char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"authority\") between 1 and 200 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"reference\") between 1 and 200"

          "name": "legal_orders_channel",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"channel\" in ('mailbox', 'portal', 'post', 'other')"
        },
        "legal_orders_opened_via": {
          "name": "legal_orders_opened_via",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"opened_via\" in ('console', 'cli')"
        },
        "legal_orders_received": {
          "name": "legal_orders_received",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"received_at\" <= \"legal_orders\".\"opened_at\" and \"legal_orders\".\"sent_at\" <= \"legal_orders\".\"opened_at\""
        },
        "legal_orders_issued": {
          "name": "legal_orders_issued",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"issued_at\" <= coalesce(\"legal_orders\".\"received_at\", \"legal_orders\".\"opened_at\")"
        },
        "legal_orders_tco": {
          "name": "legal_orders_tco",
          "value": "((\"legal_orders\".\"kind\" <> 'tco_removal' and not \"legal_orders\".\"section_c\") or \"legal_orders\".\"withhold_from_author\") and (\"legal_orders\".\"kind\" <> 'tco_removal' or \"legal_orders\".\"preserve\")"
        },

          "value": "(\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person\" is null or (\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person\" in ('at_effect', 'at_instant', 'never') and \"legal_orders\".\"kind\" = 'dsa_art10')) and (\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person_at\" is not null) = (\"legal_orders\".\"tell_person\" is not distinct from 'at_instant')"
        },
        "legal_orders_hold_end": {
          "name": "legal_orders_hold_end",
          "value": "(\"legal_orders\".\"hold_ended_at\" is null) = (\"legal_orders\".\"hold_end_reason\" is null) and \"legal_orders\".\"hold_end_reason\" in ('not_authentic', 'annulled', 'released_by_authority', 'not_ordered')"
        },
        "legal_orders_texts_len": {
          "name": "legal_orders_texts_len",
          "value": "char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"verified_how\") <= 500 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"hold_basis\") <= 500 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"scope\") <= 500 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"reasons\") <= 4000 and char_length(\"legal_orders\".\"redress\") <= 4000"
        },
        "legal_orders_document": {
          "name": "legal_orders_document",
          "value": "\"legal_orders\".\"document_sha256\" ~ '^[0-9a-f]{64}$' and \"legal_orders\".\"document_bytes\" >= 0"

      },

    },

          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"duties\" <@ array['dsa18_1', 'dsa18_2', 'tco14_5', 'voluntary']::text[]"
        },
        "authority_notifications_sent_kinds": {

        },

          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"answer\" in ('not_illegal', 'illegal', 'no_assessment', 'other')"
        },

        },
        "authority_notifications_closed": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_closed",
          "value": "(\"authority_notifications\".\"state\" = 'owed') = (\"authority_notifications\".\"closed_at\" is null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_declined": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_declined",
          "value": "(\"authority_notifications\".\"state\" = 'declined') = (\"authority_notifications\".\"declined_reason\" is not null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_sent": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_sent",
          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"state\" <> 'sent' or (\"authority_notifications\".\"sent_at\" is not null and \"authority_notifications\".\"authority\" is not null and \"authority_notifications\".\"channel\" is not null and \"authority_notifications\".\"sent_kinds\" is not null and cardinality(\"authority_notifications\".\"duties\") > 0 and \"authority_notifications\".\"not_kept_version\" is not null)"
        },
        "authority_notifications_answered": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_answered",
          "value": "\"authority_notifications\".\"answer\" is null or \"authority_notifications\".\"answered_at\" is not null"
        },
        "authority_notifications_texts": {
          "name": "authority_notifications_texts",
          "value": "char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"check_reason\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"state_basis\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"declined_reason\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"checked_by\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"sent_by\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"authority\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"channel\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"receipt\") <= 500 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"own_reference\") <= 200 and char_length(\"authority_notifications\".\"their_reference\") <= 200"
        }
```

### Replace `README.md` (whole file)

````markdown
# korbat

Pseudonymous social platform with a narrow public rulebook and transparent moderation. Self-hosted.

- Design spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-03-korbat-design.md`
- Accounts and sessions (sub-project 1a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-14-identity-auth-1a-design.md`
- Posting and feed (sub-project 2a): `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-17-posting-feed-2a-design.md`
- Plans: `docs/superpowers/plans/`

## Dev quick start
```bash
pnpm install
node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs                # creates or completes infra/.env, apps/api/.env, apps/app/.env and apps/worker/.env, and derives apps/api/.env.test; values are random and never printed
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d postgres redis mailpit   # dev host ports 55432, 56379, 51025, 58025 (movable: DEV_*_PORT in infra/.env)
pnpm --filter @korbat/api dev               # http://localhost:3000/api/health; reads apps/api/.env
pnpm --filter @korbat/worker dev            # the image worker; reads apps/worker/.env and works on .data/media
pnpm --filter @korbat/app web               # http://localhost:8081
pnpm --filter @korbat/admin dev             # the staff console at http://localhost:8090 (never 127.0.0.1); forwards /api/staff/* to the API above
```

Emails sent in development (sign-in codes, new-device alerts, lockout notices) land in Mailpit at http://localhost:58025. Locally the web app uses Cloudflare's always-pass Turnstile test key, so the human check never blocks you.

The data services are PostgreSQL 18 and Valkey (the BSD-licensed fork of Redis, still under the service name `redis`, on its own volume `valkeydata`: Valkey 9 cannot read the RDB format 12 that Redis 7.4 wrote into the old `redisdata` volume, which held only transient state and can be removed with `docker volume rm`). Valkey needs the password from `infra/.env`; `gen-dev-env` writes it into the API's `REDIS_URL` too, so an older `.env` is fixed by running it again.

korbat once ran MinIO and never used it. Images live on two Docker volumes instead, `media-uploads` and `media-store`. If an old stack left a `korbat_miniodata` volume behind, `docker volume rm korbat_miniodata` removes it.

## Tests
```bash
pnpm test                                     # unit tests of every package
node scripts/test-db.mjs                      # creates or migrates the korbat_test database; run it again after adding a migration
pnpm --filter @korbat/api test:integration    # needs postgres, redis and mailpit up
```

Integration tests have their own database, `korbat_test`, and their own Redis database, 15. Both are named in `apps/api/.env.test`, which `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` derives from `apps/api/.env`. Every run starts by emptying them, and refuses to start if a URL points anywhere else, so tests never touch development data.

Before they had their own database, the integration suites left accounts, profiles and posts in the development database, and the smoke test still leaves its first account per run, by then a moderator, with one open moderation case on that account's post. To see and remove them:

```bash
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs          # lists test accounts and profiles without an account; deletes nothing
node scripts/clean-dev-fixtures.mjs --yes    # deletes them with everything they made
```

It only matches emails of the tests' shape, `<word>-<uuid>@korbat.local`, recomputes the counters of kept profiles and posts they touched, and refuses to run unless `API_APP_ORIGIN` in `infra/.env` is a localhost origin. It keeps an account that holds a staff key or that the moderation record names (one that decided anything, one on either side of a staff link, the subject of a case that a decision or a reveal names), and counts it as kept; every other case about a deleted account or one of its posts is deleted with it, the smoke test's open case included.

## Full stack
```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml up -d --build   # http://localhost:8080, and the staff console at http://localhost:8090
node scripts/smoke-auth-stack.mjs --base http://localhost:8080 --console http://localhost:8090 --mailpit http://localhost:58025 --terms draft-2026-09 -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

The smoke test first checks the staff console's site: its page carries the console's own policy and is never stored, and the staff API answers there (401 without a session) and nowhere else (Caddy's own 404 on the app's site); the console's case routes (the overview, the queue, a case, the appeals) answer the same two ways, and the console's site refuses the app's own moderation routes with a 404 of its own. It then signs up a throwaway account through Caddy, reads its code from Mailpit, posts and reads the post back from the public Latest timeline. It uploads a JPEG carrying a GPS position, posts it, and checks that the served file is a fresh WebP without metadata, that a symlink planted in the store from inside the worker gets a 404, and that deleting the post removes the image from disk. It checks the worker's isolation, then grants the account a staff role with the CLI and checks that its session was revoked. A second throwaway account edits its bio, changes its handle, reports the first account's post under a rule, finds that report undecided in its own list and as the last member, `moderation`, of its export, and deletes itself. Last, signed out, a notice that the same post is illegal is taken with the human check: it answers a reference and a token, the status page opens with that token, the receipt arrives in Mailpit, and the token in the receipt's link opens the same page. Nothing in it decides the case, since a decision needs a staff key: every run leaves one open case in lane 2 on the first account's post. One network can run it five times an hour and twenty times a day, since its two sign-ups count against the hourly sign-up limit and its signed-out notice against the limits of reports sent without an account.

After every sharp upgrade, add `--worst-case`: it also uploads flat-colour files at the pixel caps (48 MP 16-bit interlaced PNG, 48 MP progressive JPEG, 48 MP GIF, 16 MP AVIF), expects each to be ready without the worker being OOM-killed or restarted, and prints the worker's memory peak.

Caddy listens on 8080 inside its container as its own user, proxies `/api` to the API and serves the web app with the page's security headers; `index.html` is revalidated on every load and the hashed bundles are cached for a year. On 8090 it serves the staff console under the console's own policy and proxies only `/api/staff/*`, which the app's site refuses. On 8091 it serves the phones' push site: only the two alert topics' subscriptions reach ntfy, and every other path is Caddy's own 404. The compose file keeps cloudflared, Caddy, the API and the data services on separate networks, so cloudflared reaches only Caddy and Caddy only the API and ntfy. Under the Compose profile `notify`, the contact point's watcher (`notify`) and the push server (ntfy) join two networks of their own: `push`, which has no route out and whose clients the app's and the console's sites refuse with 403, and `watch`, which holds the watcher and PostgreSQL and nothing else. With the profile on, add `--push http://localhost:8091` to the smoke test: it checks that the push site answers ntfy's own API with 404 and hands a subscription to ntfy, and that from the push network the app's and the console's sites answer 403.

## Upgrading PostgreSQL

The stack runs PostgreSQL 18 on the `pgdata18` volume. A database from the earlier PostgreSQL 16 volume (`pgdata`) is moved by:

```bash
node scripts/pg-major-upgrade.mjs -- docker compose -f infra/compose.yml -f infra/compose.dev.yml
```

It dumps the old cluster with the old image in a throwaway container, starts the new server, restores the dump with every owner kept, and compares the row counts. The old volume stays until you remove it; the test database is created again by `node scripts/test-db.mjs`. Run `staff.js audit-verify` with every kept place before and after a major upgrade; Before going public says why.

## Upgrading

Authorities' orders and the alert channel (sub-project 3f) add a database role for the contact point's watcher, two services under a Compose profile, the hand-over's service under another, the report hold, and two arguments of the web build.

- On a database that exists, give the role its password and create it, with its USAGE on the schema `public`, once, as the superuser and against korbat's own database, before the first 3f migration: set `KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD` in `infra/.env` (`node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` does in development), run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d postgres`, which passes it to the database's container, then the command below. Run twice, it changes nothing. The grant cannot be made by the migration: the migrator does not own the schema, and its grant would be a warning and nothing more. The migration checks both and stops with "create the role korbat_notify first" when either is missing, so a half-done upgrade stops there and not at a watcher that cannot read a row. A new data directory gets both from `infra/postgres/init/01-roles.sh`.

```bash
docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T postgres sh -c 'psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB" -v pw="$KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD"' <<'SQL'
SET korbat.notify_pw = :'pw';
DO $$ BEGIN IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pg_roles WHERE rolname = 'korbat_notify') THEN
  IF current_setting('korbat.notify_pw') = '' THEN RAISE EXCEPTION 'KORBAT_NOTIFY_DB_PASSWORD is empty in the postgres container: set it in infra/.env, then up -d postgres'; END IF;
  EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE korbat_notify LOGIN PASSWORD %L', current_setting('korbat.notify_pw'));
END IF; END $$;
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA public TO korbat_notify;
SQL
```

- `notify` and ntfy run under the Compose profile `notify`. Switch it on in one place, `COMPOSE_PROFILES=notify` in `infra/.env`, which Compose reads for every command: the README's commands stay as they are, and an upgrade then recreates the two services with the rest. Without that line they are never started, or keep running an old image against a migrated database.
- Until the contact-point mailbox exists, leave the profile off and set `API_NOTIFY=off`: korbat then says on the console's home screen that phone alerts are switched off on this server, and mails no "Phone alerts are down". No setting of `notify`, ntfy or the hand-over is needed for the stack to start.
- The quarantine's service (`quarantine`, sub-project 3d) runs under the Compose profile `quarantine`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand with the steps under Quarantine. Its volume `media-quarantine` is created by its first run, owned by the API image's user; the hand-over's service now mounts it too, read-only. It needs no setting, and nothing of it is backed up.
- The hand-over's service (`handover`) runs under the Compose profile `handover`, which stays off: the operator starts it by hand for one hand-over, with the directory on its command line (Authorities' orders, Notifications and hand-overs). It needs no setting.
- The report hold is on from the upgrade: while a report of sealed images to the authorities is owed, the deletion of the account keeps its address, and nothing else, for at most 7 days. `API_REPORT_HOLD=off` in `infra/.env` ends the practice for everyone and deletes as before; set it only on counsel's advice.
- The web build takes `WEB_CONTACT_POINT` and `WEB_HOME_STATE` from `infra/.env` for the terms (the contact point for authorities and korbat's Member State). Neither is required, and both stay empty, or the state alone set, until the last step of Before going public; `node scripts/gen-dev-env.mjs` adds the two lines to an existing file without changing a value. Rebuild the caddy image after a change of either.

## Backups

The backup of `media-store` is deleted 30 days after it was taken (`RETENTION.backupDays`, which the terms publish), without exception but an authority's written demand. `media-quarantine` is never backed up (Quarantine, step 4).

## Restoring

Restore the database and the `media-store` volume from the same moment. The API's sweeper deletes images that have no row: after a database restored from an older snapshot it would delete every image posted since. It refuses when there are many such images, but for a restore window set `MEDIA_RECONCILE=off` in `infra/.env` before starting the API, and put it back to `on` once the store matches the database. `force` makes one pass delete them anyway, for when they really are orphans.

Keep no backup of the database or of `media-store` more than 30 days after it was taken (`RETENTION.backupDays`, which the terms publish), and delete older ones, except a backup that korbat must keep for the authorities (step 5), which you keep until they have answered. A backup holds what korbat erased after it was taken, among it content erased under rule R4.

The staff steps run with the api service stopped (`docker compose -f infra/compose.yml stop api`), before it starts again, with the commands under Staff console and Moderation; step 5 says which of its parts wait until the API runs again:

1. Run `staff.js audit-head` on the restored database. Its place and hash go to the keeper with the restore's date: new rows will take the places lost with the backup's later rows, with other hashes, so every place kept after the backup would fail as a rewrite does. The keeper retires those places with that note, `audit-verify` runs from then on with the places at or before the restored one, and a failing place that no announced restore explains is a rewrite.
2. Run `staff.js revoke <email> all` for every account `staff.js keys` lists, since the restore brings back every staff key, staff session and enrolment link revoked or cancelled after the backup, and the auth events and audit rows that recorded those revocations are gone with it.
3. Run grant-role for every staff account with the role on your own list, and `user` for any other account `staff.js keys` lists, as after an API incident: it sets back any role changed after the backup and ends every session and staff session of the account, app sessions revoked after the backup included. Then compare the accounts `staff.js keys` lists with that list.
4. Each person enrols again, two keys each.
5. Moderation. Every decision, review and seal confirmed after the backup is gone with its audit rows, and what it restricted is back: sealed images are served again, and a removed post is public again. Reports, notices and re-examinations received after the backup are gone too, and so is everything `staff.js` wrote since: links and unlinks and limits. So are the stops that people pressed on a report's page after the backup, and the report mail that accounts resumed in Settings since; korbat may mail such an address about reports again, though its holder asked it to stop, until they press stop again, and an account that resumed its report mail gets none until it resumes again. Nothing on the server or in your records names them, so none can be applied again. Nothing on the restored server names the lost decisions either: the keeper's daily copy names them, and the orders and records to authorities, up to the keeper's last download, and Restoring with the keeper's copy below takes each lost measure again from it. So before the api service starts again after step 3, set `APP_SITE=closed` in `infra/.env` and recreate Caddy alone with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy` (Caddy reads the setting only when it is created, and without `--no-deps` Compose would start the API with it), which closes the app's site and leaves the console's open, as that block's first step says; check from outside that the app's hostname answers 503. Before it starts, also delete the moderation dispatch's daily markers, which live in Valkey and are not restored with the database: `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml exec -T redis sh -c 'export VALKEYCLI_AUTH="$REDIS_PASSWORD"; valkey-cli --scan --pattern "*moderation-dispatched:*" | while read -r k; do valkey-cli del "$k"; done'`. The dispatch's first round then releases again every outcome and changed outcome that was answered before the day's dispatch hour and not yet released at the backup, so the status pages, the re-examination windows and the mails agree again; a person whose outcome mail or statement went out after the backup's time gets it a second time. Before it starts, also set `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=off` in `infra/.env`, which the API reads when `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api` starts it. The restored database no longer holds the cases, freezes and seals made after the backup. From its first round, 10 minutes after the start, the retention job would make R4 redactions final, erase case evidence and delete the images that these cases, freezes and seals no longer protect. That includes images sealed and reported to the police since the backup, long before an admin has enrolled and sealed them again. While the switch is off nothing is erased or deleted but the fingerprints and ratings of an automated tool that is off (Automated tools), and the console's count of late erasures rises. Before anyone decides anything, run `staff.js link` and `staff.js unlink` until the links match your records, and check that the count `staff.js keys` prints for each staff account equals your records'; then run `staff.js limits` with the numbers you last set. Once the staff have enrolled again, an admin first opens a finding citing R2 on every post or account that your R2 records show was sealed after the backup's time, unless its case is open in the restored database, and seals its images again. Only then, once every such seal has been applied again, set `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on` in `infra/.env` and run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`, which recreates the API with it, and open the app's site again when the console's After a restore screen says so (`APP_SITE=open`, then `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy`). Its next rounds make up the erasures that fell due meanwhile. Then tell the authority each of these was reported to what was lost and when it was sealed again, and keep the backup you restored from until that authority has answered, also past the 30 days. Sub-project 3d adds the release of sealed images and its replay after a restore. Then the cases that were open at the backup are open again in the queue: decide them again at once, lane 0 first. Each moderator also opens a finding on any other target they remember restricting since the backup's time.

**Restoring with the keeper's copy** (sub-project 3f). The keeper's daily copy of the audit log's tail (Staff console, the audit log's "Download since my last copy") names the orders, the records to authorities and the decisions the backup lacks, up to the keeper's last download. These steps come after the staff steps above; where they and step 5 differ, these hold.

1. Before the API starts: `API_MODERATION_RETENTION=off`, `MEDIA_RECONCILE=off` and `APP_SITE=closed` in `infra/.env`, which the API reads when `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api` starts it in step 5; then recreate Caddy alone with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy`, since Caddy reads `APP_SITE` only when it is created, and check from outside that the app's hostname answers 503 to every path (`curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' https://<app hostname>/`); the console's site is unchanged.
2. Feed the import every keeper's file from the one that holds the restored head's place onward, oldest first, concatenated on standard input: `cat <files> | docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js restore-import <kept places>` (`-T`: without it Compose attaches a terminal and the redirect fails). The files need not start at the head: the import checks the earlier lines and skips them. A changed file is refused whole and nothing is written; a hole between two files is printed, and what lies behind it is not imported. Read what it prints, a hole among it.
3. Compare the contact-point mailbox since the keeper's last download with the orders it lists; open what is missing with `order-open --received`. An imported item whose link named no post shows `sha256:` and a digest in place of the link, since the copy holds no link's text: read the address from the order in the mailbox. Enter the records of class "record" again from the authority's letters, each with its command and `--gap <gap>`, which closes that gap. Until the last of them is entered, answer no data request: `access-request` cannot print an authority's "not to the person" mark for a record that is still lost.
4. Before any order's disabling is taken again: compare each held notice the import lists with the mailbox since the keeper's last download. An extension or a later time that was recorded after that download is lost with the restore; record it again first (`order-hold-extend`, `order-hold-until`), or the disabling taken again would tell the author at the old end.
5. Start the API with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`; everyone enrols new keys.
6. On the console's After a restore screen, take every measure again, from the top. An order's disabling first: its hour, its preservation and its hold are the old ones. A gap that needs nothing is closed by an admin as "Not needed", with the key.
7. When the screen says so, set `APP_SITE=open` and recreate Caddy alone with `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d --no-deps caddy`, then check from outside that the app's hostname no longer answers 503; when it says so, switch retention and the sweep back on (`API_MODERATION_RETENTION=on`, `MEDIA_RECONCILE=on`) and run `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml up -d api`, since the API reads both only when it starts.

The keeper's file holds no post and no statement, but it names authorities and references, held orders' among them, and a reference may itself name a person: keep it like the head, not like a log.

**Restoring the releases** (sub-project 3d). While the app's site stays closed (step 1 above), after `restore-import` (step 2 above), which writes a gap of the class "Releases and held uploads to replay" for every release, every leave recorded and every leave withdrawn that the backup lacks:

1. `cat <the keeper's files> | docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js release-replay`. Every release recorded after the backup is marked again, for sealed posts and for held uploads: its posts are released and their image rows erased, a seal for good taken again afterwards freezes nothing, and a held upload whose refusal the backup does not hold is kept from every post. A replay whose author must not be told yet, or whose leave the restore lost, waits until it may be told.
2. The Quarantine steps, beginning with step 6 (the inventory): the destroy lines name every released file that the restored store or the quarantine holds again. An `operator` line is a file the quarantine holds for an image the restored database does not know: never destroy it on that line alone; find the row of the keeper's files that names the image (`upload_hold_ended`, `upload_released`, `seal_released`). If it is held for a report, it stays where it is, and the operator's R2 records say so. If it was released, no list will ever print a `destroy` line for it, since the database cannot tie the file to its release: write that one line by hand (the `operator` line with `destroy` as its direction), run steps 2 and 3 with it, and note it.
3. On After a restore, a person closes what no command can: a lost end of a hold whose refusal is there is ended again by an admin, the same way (do not run `upload-report` a second time before the keeper's files have been checked for the record of the report); a measure a program had taken is taken again by a person, as 3f's classes say. A lost leave is recorded again from what korbat holds in writing, with `release-leave <seal> ... --gap <gap>`, which records it under the id the gap names and closes the gap. A lost withdrawal of a leave comes before anything else on its case: the restored database shows the mistaken leave as standing, so withdraw it again with `release-leave --withdraw <leave> --operator <name> --gap <gap>` before an admin reads the case.
4. `docker compose -f infra/compose.yml run --rm -T migrate node dist/staff.js head-restore-mark <day>:<value> ...`, with the values of the keeper's mails for the days after the backup, each a day and its value as the mail gives them. Each is shown on `/transparency` as retired, every published value that the restored log no longer gives is retired too, none is deleted, and today's row says that korbat restored its database from a backup and which value is the last that still fits. The site opens only when After a restore shows no gap, the class "Releases and held uploads to replay" included.

**The public figures after a restore** (sub-project 3d). A backup holds the yearly editions published and the months of the readers' count closed until it was taken, and nothing after. `restore-import` prints one line for each published version of an edition that the restored database lacks ("edition <year> version <n>, published <time>, is not in the restored database"), and writes nothing for it: `/transparency` no longer shows that version. The job publishes a year's first version again in its next daily round, computed from the restored database as of the same 1 March, which lacks what the backup lacked, and a version for an order whose hold ended again when it finds that order; a lost correction comes back only with `staff.js edition <year> --correct`. Note in the operator's notes each lost version, its day and, if you kept the page, how the new one differs, and say so to anyone who asks about it. A month closed after the backup is lost the same way, its two numbers with it (`recipient_months`), and no line or audit row records that it was: it reads "not recorded" in `staff.js recipients` and in the recipients' line of the next edition. Note the months between the backup and the restore.

A suspect or revoked staff key is never cleared or revived.

## Posting and feed
Text posts up to 1000 characters, replies, quotes, likes, reposts and bookmarks; follows, blocks and mutes; a chronological Following timeline and a public Latest timeline; threads and profile pages. The web app's home is the timeline; sign-in lives at `/signin`.

- **Reading signed out:** Latest, threads and profiles are public. Following, bookmarks, likes, follower lists and privacy settings need a session.
- **Blocks** are enforced in every query, not just the interface: neither account sees the other while signed in, follows are removed both ways, and the blocked side gets `not_found` so nothing is revealed. Posts are public, so a block does not hide them from someone who signs out; the interface says so.
- **Mutes** are one-way and silent, and hide an account from your timelines only.
- **Liker lists are never exposed.** Counts are public; likes and bookmarks are private to their owner.
- **Write limits** per account, tiered by account age: in the first 24 hours 5 posts and 20 replies an hour and no reposts or quotes for 48 hours; afterwards 30 posts and 60 replies an hour. Everyone: 100 likes an hour, 50 follows an hour and 400 a day, 30 blocks or mutes an hour. Undo actions are never limited.
- **Deleting** blanks the text in the database and leaves a tombstone only where a thread or a quote needs it. There is no editing. A post that a report or a moderator's finding named before it was deleted keeps a copy with its case, read by staff only, for as long as the case needs it (Moderation, Evidence and retention).
- **Moderation states.** A post is `visible`, `withheld` (while a case about it is being decided) or `removed`, as the database derives it from the measures that moderators' decisions recorded; nothing else writes the state, and the API's role cannot. A withheld or removed post is shown to its author alone, with a chip ("Under review" in amber, "Removed" in red) that names the rule or says "illegal content" and links to the decision's statement under Settings, Cases; everyone else finds it in no list and gets `not_found` for it.

## Images
Posts, replies and quotes can carry up to four images, and every image needs a description of up to 1000 characters. The web composer takes JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF and still GIF files up to 20 MB, and refuses HEIC with advice to export a JPEG.

- **Nothing of the original is kept**, but, while the known material check is switched on, three hashes of the file as received, deleted with the image or when the check is switched off; a match record keeps one of them for 180 days (Automated tools). The upload goes to the `media-uploads` volume, a separate worker container decodes it and writes fresh WebP files in two sizes (1024 and 2048 pixels on the long side) without any metadata to `media-store`, and the original is deleted once the image is ready.
- **The worker is boxed in**, and while the R1 check is switched on it also rates the decoded pixels, still without a network; this build computes no perceptual fingerprint. It has no network, no credentials and no capabilities, runs as a non-root user on a read-only file system within 768 MiB, one CPU and 64 processes, and only reads `media-uploads`. Decoders outside the allowlist are blocked, and the pixel count is checked from the header before decoding: 50 MP, 16 MP for AVIF, 16383 pixels on a side.
- **Formats can be switched off** without a deploy, for example while a codec advisory is open: remove it from `MEDIA_FORMATS` in `infra/.env` and restart `api` and `worker`.
- **Who sees an image** follows its post and, since moderation cases, its own state: anyone when the post and the image are both visible, cached publicly for at most a minute in a browser and five minutes at the edge (The edge); only the author when either is withheld or removed, never cached, while everyone else reads "Image hidden by korbat moderation" in its place on a visible post; nobody when the image is sealed (reported as child sexual abuse material, Moderation), its author included, who reads "Sealed: not shown to anyone, you included" in its place; nobody once its content or its post's was erased or the post is deleted. A deleted post's files leave the disk at once, except images that a moderation case holds as evidence or that an unanswered report of child sexual abuse material or a seal freezes: their rows and files are kept, served and listed to nobody and exported to nobody, and the retention job deletes them once nothing retains them.
````
