```ts
         where m.post_id = ${postId}::uuid and m.status = 'ready' and m.erased_at is null
         order by m.position, m.id`)) as unknown as { id: string; nsfw_score: number | null }[];
      return rows.map((row) => ({ mediaId: row.id, score: row.nsfw_score === null ? null : Number(row.nsfw_score) }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 5 and 7.9, MediaForCases.unsignalled): the sweep's read of images that should have a
     * signal and have none: every ready, unerased image of a post created in the last `hours` hours, the post not deleted
     * by its author, whose score is at or over `threshold` and that no r1_score signal names. The media repository names
     * automated_signals for this one read. At most `limit`, the oldest posts first. Task 7 adds the posted images with a
     * match record not marked handled.
     */
    async unsignalledScores(limit: number, hours: number, threshold: number): Promise<{ mediaId: string; postId: string; score: number }[]> {
      const rows = (await db.execute(sql`
        select m.id, m.post_id, m.nsfw_score from public.post_media m join public.posts p on p.id = m.post_id
         where p.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => ${hours}::int) and p.state <> 'deleted_by_author'
           and m.status = 'ready' and m.erased_at is null and m.nsfw_score >= ${threshold}::real
           and not exists (select 1 from public.automated_signals s where s.media_id = m.id and s.kind = 'r1_score')
         order by p.created_at, m.id
         limit ${limit}::int`)) as unknown as { id: string; post_id: string; nsfw_score: number }[];
      return rows.map((row) => ({ mediaId: row.id, postId: row.post_id, score: Number(row.nsfw_score) }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 8 (design, sections 2 row 33, 5 and 7.14, the retention job's step tools_off): while the R1 check is off,
     * every stored rating is set null in the caller's transaction, but the rating of an image that an unhandled signal
     * names, which the sweep still puts before a person. The API's role holds UPDATE of the column (0015); answers how many
     * images it changed. The step runs only while R1_CLASSIFIER is off, so "korbat keeps no rating from a time when one
     * did" is true once it has run.
     */
    async forgetScores(tx: Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
        update public.post_media m set nsfw_score = null
         where m.nsfw_score is not null
           and not exists (select 1 from public.automated_signals s where s.media_id = m.id and s.handled_at is null)
        returning m.id`);
      return rows.length;
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 8 (design, sections 6.3, 6.10 and 7.14, the retention job's step edge_purges): the outbox rows of the edge
     * done more than EDGE_RULES.keepDays ago, deleted in the caller's transaction; answers how many. A row without an
     * outcome is never taken: the job edge-purge has not finished with it.
     */
    async forgetPurges(tx: Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<number> {
      const rows = await tx.execute<{ id: string }>(sql`
        delete from public.edge_purges e
         where e.done_at is not null and e.done_at < now() - make_interval(days => ${EDGE_RULES.keepDays}::int)
        returning e.id`);
      return rows.length;
    },

    /**
     * Removes an upload of this account that is not on a post. 3d Task 7 (design, sections 5 and 7.8 step 5): with
     * `keepChecking` (the comparison is on), a row still processing whose check is pending or capped is kept and answered
     * `kept`; the sweeper deletes it once finalize gave it a verdict. A row gate K keeps (a held upload) is `none`.
     */
    async deleteUnattached(id: string, ownerId: string, keepChecking = false): Promise<"deleted" | "kept" | "none"> {
      if (keepChecking) {
        const checking = (await db.execute(sql`
          select 1 from post_media m join public.media_hashes h on h.media_id = m.id
           where m.id = ${id}::uuid and m.owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid and m.post_id is null and m.status = 'processing'
             and h.check_state in ('pending', 'capped')`)) as unknown as unknown[];
        if (checking.length === 1) return "kept";
      }
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.length === 1 ? "deleted" : "none";
    },

    /**
     * What serving an image file depends on: whether it is ready, its own moderation state, its post's state and author,
     * and whether its content or its post's was erased.
     */
    async fileAccess(id: string): Promise<{ status: MediaRow["status"]; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; postState: string | null; authorId: string | null; erased: boolean } | null> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ status: postMedia.status, mediaState: postMedia.moderationState, postState: posts.state, authorId: posts.authorId, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt, postErasedAt: posts.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(eq(postMedia.id, id))
        .limit(1);
      const found = rows[0];
      if (!found) return null;
      return { status: found.status, mediaState: found.mediaState, postState: found.postState, authorId: found.authorId, erased: found.erasedAt !== null || found.postErasedAt !== null };
    },

    /**
     * Puts images on a post, inside the transaction that creates it. Each must belong to the author,
     * be ready and be on no post yet; anything else rolls the post back.
     */
    async attach(tx: DbTx, input: { postId: string; ownerId: string; items: readonly { id: string; alt: string }[] }): Promise<void> {
      for (const [position, item] of input.items.entries()) {
        let rows: { id: string }[];
        try {
          rows = await tx
            .update(postMedia)
            .set({ postId: input.postId, position, altText: item.alt })
            .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, item.id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, input.ownerId), isNull(postMedia.postId), eq(postMedia.status, "ready")))
            .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
        } catch (err) {
          // 3d Task 7 (design, section 7.8 step 5): post_media_refused refuses a refused upload, an erased one and one held
          // for good; the post's transaction rolls back with the media error of that code.
          if (raisedCode(err) === "upload_refused") throw new MediaError("upload_refused", 422);
          throw err;
        }
        if (rows.length !== 1) throw new MediaError("media_unavailable", 400);
      }
    },

    /**
     * Removes a post's images, inside the transaction that deletes it, and says which files to delete afterwards. The
     * rows are taken in id order, under row locks, with no filter of its own: the keep trigger skips every row a case
     * holds and every row of a frozen post, and RETURNING omits them, so no file of a kept row is asked for. A plain
     * delete by post takes the rows in its scan's order, and deadlocked with an intake that locks the same rows by id.
     */
    async detachAll(tx: DbTx, postId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where post_id = ${postId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Removes every image row of the owner, on a post or not, whatever its state, inside the transaction
     * that purges the account, and says which files to delete afterwards (1b design, section 7.6). In id order under
     * row locks and with no filter, as detachAll: the keep trigger decides which rows stay.
     */
    async purgeOwner(tx: DbTx, ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(
        sql`delete from post_media where id in (select id from post_media where owner_id = ${ownerId}::uuid order by id for update) returning id`,
      )) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * The images of a page of posts, in one query, in their order on each post, each with its own moderation state:
     * what the state means for a reader is the view builder's to say. A sealed image is its id and its state only:
     * nobody is given its size, its blurhash, its alt text or a path. An image of a deleted post, and one whose content
     * or whose post's was erased, is given to nobody, its owner included, so no view and no export names a row that a
     * case or a freeze kept. A state this reader has not been taught is left out.
     */
    async forPosts(postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostImage[]>> {
      const byPost = new Map<string, PostImage[]>();
      if (postIds.length === 0) return byPost;
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, width: postMedia.width, height: postMedia.height, blurhash: postMedia.blurhash, altText: postMedia.altText, state: postMedia.moderationState })
        .from(postMedia)
        .innerJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]), eq(postMedia.status, "ready"), ne(posts.state, "deleted_by_author"), isNull(postMedia.erasedAt), isNull(posts.erasedAt)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.postId, postMedia.position);
      for (const row of rows) {
        if (!row.postId) continue;
        let image: PostImage;
        if (row.state === "sealed") image = { id: row.id, state: "sealed" };
        else if (row.state === "visible" || row.state === "withheld" || row.state === "removed") {
          if (row.width === null || row.height === null || row.blurhash === null) continue;
          image = { id: row.id, state: row.state, width: row.width, height: row.height, blurhash: row.blurhash, alt: row.altText ?? "", small: mediaPath(row.id, "small"), large: mediaPath(row.id, "large") };
        } else {
          // A state added later does not compile until this reader says who is given it.
          const unknown: never = row.state;
          void unknown;
          continue;
        }
        byPost.set(row.postId, [...(byPost.get(row.postId) ?? []), image]);
      }
      return byPost;
    },

    /**
     * Every image of the account that the data export takes a file for, on a post or not, oldest first: the ready ones
     * the account still sees (EXPORTABLE). A withheld or removed image stays with its author; a sealed image, an image
     * of a deleted post and an erased one are exported to nobody.
     */
    async readyImages(ownerId: string): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .orderBy(postMedia.createdAt, postMedia.id);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Whether readyImages would still list this image of the owner: the export reads the row again when it opens each
     * file, so an image that was sealed, erased or deleted with its post while the archive streams is left out of it.
     */
    async isExportable(ownerId: string, id: string): Promise<boolean> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .leftJoin(posts, eq(posts.id, postMedia.postId))
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.id, id), eq(postMedia.ownerId, ownerId), EXPORTABLE))
        .limit(1);
      return rows.length === 1;
    },

    /**
     * Uploads that still wait for the worker's verdict. 3d Task 7: not one whose check is capped, which waits for
     * match-retry to ask the source again, so the sweeper's round never asks it every thirty seconds.
     */
    async processingIds(): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(eq(postMedia.status, "processing"), sql`not exists (select 1 from public.media_hashes h where h.media_id = ${postMedia.id} and h.check_state = 'capped')`))
        .orderBy(postMedia.createdAt);
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Fails uploads the worker has not answered since `before`, and says which. 3d Task 7 (design, section 7.8 step 3): a
     * capped upload is exempt while it is younger than AUTOMATION_RULES.matchRetryHours; after that it fails as any.
     */
    async failStale(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db
        .update(postMedia)
        .set({ status: "failed", error: "processing_failed" })
        .where(
          and(
            eq(postMedia.status, "processing"),
            lt(postMedia.createdAt, before),
            sql`not exists (select 1 from public.media_hashes h where h.media_id = ${postMedia.id} and h.check_state = 'capped'
                                and ${postMedia.createdAt} > now() - make_interval(hours => ${AUTOMATION_RULES.matchRetryHours}::int))`,
          ),
        )
        .returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /** Removes uploads made before `before` that were never put on a post, whatever their state, and says which. */
    async deleteUnattachedBefore(before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = await db.delete(postMedia).where(and(isNull(postMedia.postId), lt(postMedia.createdAt, before))).returning({ id: postMedia.id });
      return rows.map((row) => row.id);
    },

    /**
     * Which of these ids have a row, whatever the row's state: the reconcile pass asks it which stored files belong to
     * no row, so a row that a hold or a freeze keeps must be seen here, or its files would be swept as orphans.
     */
    async existing(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
      if (ids.length === 0) return new Set();
      const rows = await db.select({ id: postMedia.id }).from(postMedia).where(inArray(postMedia.id, [...ids]));
      return new Set(rows.map((row) => row.id));
    },

    /** Removes a row whatever its state. Used when an upload could not be handed to the worker. */
    async deleteRow(id: string): Promise<void> {
      await db.delete(postMedia).where(eq(postMedia.id, id));
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ what moderation cases need

    /**
     * An intake's holds (3c design, sections 5 and 7.1, step 4), inside the intake's transaction. First one statement
     * locks, FOR KEY SHARE and in one id order, every image row the pairs name: the rows of each post and, for an owner
     * pair, every row of that owner that is on a post (an attached row's owner is its post's author, so those are the
     * images of the account's posts). The posts are read there, never locked. The lock is what makes a delete that races
     * the intake wait and then read the intake's committed item; a row whose delete committed first is not returned.
     * Then, for the post pairs only, the case's hold goes on each returned row that has no unreleased hold from that case
     * and is not erased, in id order, which is the order the holds are released in: an owner pair gets no hold, since the
     * images of a frozen post are kept whether a hold stands or not. It answers, for each post pair, the post's images
     * in position order, an erased one without its alt text; an empty list means the images are gone.
     */
    async hold(tx: DbTx, pairs: readonly HoldPair[]): Promise<Map<string, HeldImage[]>> {
      const caseOf = new Map<string, string>();
      const owners: string[] = [];
      for (const pair of pairs) {
        if ("postId" in pair) caseOf.set(pair.postId, pair.caseId);
        else owners.push(pair.ownerId);
      }
      const held = new Map<string, HeldImage[]>([...caseOf.keys()].map((postId) => [postId, []]));
      if (caseOf.size === 0 && owners.length === 0) return held;

      const locked = (await tx.execute(sql`
        select m.id, m.post_id, m.position, m.width, m.height, m.alt_text, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.post_id = any(${uuidArray([...caseOf.keys()])}) or m.owner_id = any(${uuidArray(owners)})
        order by m.id for key share of m`)) as unknown as { id: string; post_id: string; position: number; width: number; height: number; alt_text: string | null; erased: boolean }[];

      // The rows came back in id order; the holds are placed in that order too.
      const toHold = locked.filter((row) => caseOf.has(row.post_id) && !row.erased);
      if (toHold.length > 0) {
        await tx.execute(sql`
          insert into media_holds (media_id, case_id)
          select v.media_id, v.case_id
          from unnest(${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => row.id))}, ${uuidArray(toHold.map((row) => caseOf.get(row.post_id)!))}) as v(media_id, case_id)
          where not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = v.media_id and h.case_id = v.case_id and h.released_at is null)
          order by v.media_id`);
      }

      for (const row of [...locked].sort((a, b) => a.position - b.position)) {
        held.get(row.post_id)?.push({ id: row.id, alt: row.erased ? null : (row.alt_text ?? ""), width: row.width, height: row.height });
      }
      return held;
    },

    /**
     * What a case about this post or this account reaches (3c design, section 6.1): the post itself, or every post
     * whose author is the account, whatever its state. One statement that locks nothing.
     */
    async reach(target: { type: "post" | "account"; id: string }): Promise<CaseReach> {
      // 3f (design, section 7.10): no reader serves an image of a post disabled for an order, whatever the image's own state.
      const served = sql`m.moderation_state <> 'sealed' and p.state <> 'deleted_by_author' and p.state::text <> 'disabled' and m.erased_at is null and p.erased_at is null`;
      const reached = target.type === "post" ? sql`m.post_id = ${target.id}::uuid` : sql`p.author_id = ${target.id}::uuid`;
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(distinct m.post_id)::int as posts,
               count(*)::int as images,
               (count(*) filter (where m.moderation_state = 'sealed'))::int as sealed,
               (count(*) filter (where ${served}))::int as served,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD') as newest_post_on,
               to_char(max(p.created_at) filter (where ${served}) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as newest_served_at
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${reached}`)) as unknown as { posts: number; images: number; sealed: number; served: number; newest_post_on: string | null; newest_served_at: string | null }[];
      return {
        posts: row!.posts,
        images: row!.images,
        sealed: row!.sealed,
        served: row!.served,
        newestPostOn: row!.newest_post_on,
        newestServedAt: row!.newest_served_at === null ? null : new Date(row!.newest_served_at),
      };
    },

    /**
     * What opening an image for staff depends on, in one query: the row with its post, its size and its own state,
     * whether its content or its post's was erased, and whether its post is frozen now. Null when no row has the id or
     * the image is on no post.
     */
    async staffAccess(id: string): Promise<{ postId: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; mediaState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean; matched: boolean } | null> {
      // 3d Task 7 (design, sections 5 and 7.11; review ruling 2): also whether an unerased match record names the image,
      // an acting match or a flag, which shuts gate V for it on every case, whatever was answered.
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select m.post_id, m.status, m.width, m.height, m.moderation_state, (m.erased_at is not null or p.erased_at is not null) as erased, public.post_frozen(m.post_id) as frozen,
               exists (select 1 from public.media_matches x where x.media_id = m.id and x.erased_at is null) as matched
        from post_media m join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where m.id = ${id}::uuid`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; status: MediaRow["status"]; width: number | null; height: number | null; moderation_state: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erased: boolean; frozen: boolean; matched: boolean }[];
      if (!row) return null;
      return { postId: row.post_id, status: row.status, width: row.width, height: row.height, mediaState: row.moderation_state, erased: row.erased, frozen: row.frozen, matched: row.matched };
    },

    /**
     * A page of the image rows that are on a post, in id order after `afterId` (from the start when it is null): each
     * one's id, its post, its stored moderation state and when its content was erased. It locks nothing and gives nothing
     * of an image itself. The staff command line's text-verify reads every such row through it, a page at a time, to
     * hold the stored states to what the ledger of measures says they must be.
     */
    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.4): the post an image's address belongs to, or null when no attached image row has the id. An
     * order that names a picture's address names its post; this is a read, and it holds no row.
     */
    async imagePost(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, mediaId: string): Promise<string | null> {
      const [row] = await q.select({ postId: postMedia.postId }).from(postMedia).where(and(eq(postMedia.id, mediaId), isNotNull(postMedia.postId))).limit(1);
      return row?.postId ?? null;
    },

    /** 3f (design, section 7.5): how many image rows each of these posts holds, for an order's screen; a post with none is left out. */
    async imageCounts(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, number>> {
      if (postIds.length === 0) return new Map();
      const found = await q
        .select({ postId: postMedia.postId, count: sql<number>`count(*)::int` })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(inArray(postMedia.postId, [...postIds]))
        .groupBy(postMedia.postId);
      return new Map(found.map((row) => [row.postId!, row.count]));
    },

    /**
     * 3f (design, sections 5 and 7.11): a post's image rows as staff.js order-access prints them for a preserved post: the
     * id, the pixel size and when the row was made, in position order. The table holds no digest of a file, and no file
     * is opened here.
     */
    async preservedImages(q: Pick<Db, "select"> | Pick<DbTx, "select">, postId: string): Promise<{ id: string; width: number | null; height: number | null; createdAt: Date }[]> {
      return q
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, width: postMedia.width, height: postMedia.height, createdAt: postMedia.createdAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(eq(postMedia.postId, postId))
        .orderBy(postMedia.position, postMedia.id);
    },

    /**
     * 3f (design, section 7.14): for each post a seal lists (seal_posts), the ids of its image rows now, in their order.
     * Read-only, through the caller's transaction; handover-list compares their number with what the seal recorded.
     */
    async sealImageRows(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">, sealActionId: string): Promise<{ postId: string; mediaIds: string[] }[]> {
      const found = await q.execute<{ post_id: string; media_id: string | null }>(
        sql`select s.post_id, m.id as media_id from public.seal_posts s left join public.post_media m on m.post_id = s.post_id
             where s.action_id = ${sealActionId}::uuid order by s.post_id, m.position, m.id`,
      );
      const byPost = new Map<string, string[]>();
      for (const row of found) {
        const ids = byPost.get(row.post_id) ?? [];
        if (row.media_id !== null) ids.push(row.media_id);
        byPost.set(row.post_id, ids);
      }
      return [...byPost].map(([postId, mediaIds]) => ({ postId, mediaIds }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d (design, sections 6.1 and 7.1): whether a file of the image is in the quarantine without an end (it is being
     * restored), and whether one is recorded as lost, through the two functions the API's role may call; the table itself
     * is closed to it. Asked only for a visible image whose file is missing from the store.
     */
    async custody(id: string): Promise<{ quarantined: boolean; lost: boolean }> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`select public.media_quarantined(${id}::uuid) as quarantined, public.media_lost(${id}::uuid) as lost`)) as unknown as { quarantined: boolean; lost: boolean }[];
      return { quarantined: row!.quarantined, lost: row!.lost };
    },

    /**
     * 3d: up to `limit` images whose files the quarantine's record says are lost and whose author is owed the notice
     * (lost_untold), the earliest first, each with its owner and its post's creation time when the image row and the post
     * are still there (null otherwise: nobody is left to tell).
     */
    async lostUntold(limit: number): Promise<{ mediaId: string; lostAt: Date; ownerId: string | null; postCreatedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      const found = (await db.execute(sql`
        select l.media_id, l.lost_at, m.owner_id, p.created_at as post_created_at
          from public.lost_untold(${limit}) l
          left join post_media m on m.id = l.media_id
          left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
         order by l.lost_at, l.media_id`)) as unknown as { media_id: string; lost_at: Date | string; owner_id: string | null; post_created_at: Date | string | null }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ mediaId: row.media_id, lostAt: new Date(row.lost_at), ownerId: row.owner_id, postCreatedAt: row.post_created_at === null ? null : new Date(row.post_created_at) }));
    },

    /** 3d: records the outcome of a lost image's notice (lost_told), which changes the image's rows only from pending. */
    async lostTold(mediaId: string, outcome: "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "none" | "failed"): Promise<void> {
      await db.execute(sql`select public.lost_told(${mediaId}::uuid, ${outcome}::delivery_state)`);
    },

    /**
     * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 7.1 and 8.10): quarantine_plan() as staff.js quarantine-list reads it, through the caller's
     * transaction, which reads as the migrator (the function is executable by nobody else). For each image of the plan:
     * its direction, its post (the image row's, or for an image row that is gone the post its quarantine rows recorded),
     * the names of its files whose rows have no end, and of those whose rows are neither returned nor destroyed (a lost
     * file is among them: there is nothing of it to move).
     */
    async quarantinePlan(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ direction: string; mediaId: string; postId: string | null; open: string[]; kept: string[] }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select p.direction, p.media_id,
               coalesce(m.post_id, (select min(f.post_id::text)::uuid from public.quarantine_files f where f.media_id = p.media_id)) as post_id,
               coalesce((select array_agg(f.file order by f.file) from public.quarantine_files f
                          where f.media_id = p.media_id and f.returned_at is null and f.destroyed_at is null and f.lost_at is null), '{}') as open,
               coalesce((select array_agg(f.file order by f.file) from public.quarantine_files f
                          where f.media_id = p.media_id and f.returned_at is null and f.destroyed_at is null), '{}') as kept
          from public.quarantine_plan() p
          left join post_media m on m.id = p.media_id
         order by p.direction, p.media_id`)) as unknown as { direction: string; media_id: string; post_id: string | null; open: string[]; kept: string[] }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ direction: row.direction, mediaId: row.media_id, postId: row.post_id, open: row.open, kept: row.kept }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d: for every post sealed for good (a seal_media in force whose decision is not interim) and not released (Task 2:
     * a released post's rows are erased and then dropped by the disposal, while its seal still lists it), its image rows
     * now, erased or not, and the counts that each such seal recorded for it in seal_posts, which quarantine-list compares.
     * Through the caller's transaction.
     */
    async sealedForGoodCounts(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ postId: string; rows: number; images: number[] }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select s.post_id, array_agg(distinct s.images::int) as images,
               (select count(*)::int from post_media m where m.post_id = s.post_id) as rows
          from public.seal_posts s join public.measures_in_force f on f.id = s.action_id
         where f.kind = 'seal_media' and f.decision_kind <> 'interim'
           and not exists (select 1 from public.release_posts r where r.post_id = s.post_id)
         group by s.post_id
         order by s.post_id`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; rows: number; images: number[] }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ postId: row.post_id, rows: row.rows, images: row.images }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 2 (sections 5 and 8.10): text-verify's first read of the release. The images of the quarantine whose file
     * still lies there (a row without an end), not marked unknown, whose image row is gone and whose post is not released:
     * a file korbat holds of an image it no longer has, which no release accounts for. Through the caller's transaction,
     * which reads as the migrator: quarantine_files is closed to the API's role.
     */
    async quarantineOrphans(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ mediaId: string; postId: string | null }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select f.media_id, min(f.post_id::text)::uuid as post_id from public.quarantine_files f
         where f.returned_at is null and f.destroyed_at is null and f.lost_at is null and not f.unknown and f.release_id is null
           and not exists (select 1 from post_media m where m.id = f.media_id)
           and not exists (select 1 from public.release_posts r where r.post_id = f.post_id)
         group by f.media_id order by f.media_id`)) as unknown as { media_id: string; post_id: string | null }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ mediaId: row.media_id, postId: row.post_id }));
    },

    /**
     * 3d Task 2: text-verify's second read. The released posts that still hold an image row without erased_at: the release
     * erases every row of its posts in its own transaction, and a replay does the same, so such a row means a write around
     * them. Through the caller's transaction; the API's role reads both tables.
     */
    async releasedUnerased(q: Pick<Db, "execute"> | Pick<DbTx, "execute">): Promise<{ postId: string; images: number }[]> {
      const found = (await q.execute(sql`
        select r.post_id, count(*)::int as images from public.release_posts r join post_media m on m.post_id = r.post_id
         where m.erased_at is null group by r.post_id order by r.post_id`)) as unknown as { post_id: string; images: number }[];
      return found.map((row) => ({ postId: row.post_id, images: row.images }));
    },

    // ------------------------------------------------------------ the edge's outbox (3d design, sections 6.3 and 7.4)
    // Only the two triggers of 0035_edge_purges write a row of edge_purges; the API's role reads them, moves the four
    // columns of a purge's progress, and (Task 8) deletes a row done 30 days ago. Every time is the database's.

    /** The adapter is off: every row still owed a purge closes as off at once, and nothing is sent. Answers how many. */
    async edgeOff(): Promise<number> {
      const closed = await db.execute(sql`update public.edge_purges set outcome = 'off', done_at = now() where done_at is null returning id`);
      return closed.length;
    },

    /**
     * The rows one round reads: up to `limit` images whose oldest open row is due now, the oldest first, and every open row
     * of those images, in the order of their images and then of their ids. A row written after this read is not among
     * them, whatever its id, so a round closes no row it did not read.
     */
    async edgeDue(limit: number): Promise<{ id: string; mediaId: string }[]> {
      const rows = await db.execute<{ id: string; media_id: string }>(sql`
        with images as (
          select e.media_id, min(e.id) as first from public.edge_purges e
           where e.done_at is null and e.next_at <= now()
           group by e.media_id
           order by min(e.id)
           limit ${limit})
        select e.id::text as id, e.media_id from public.edge_purges e join images i on i.media_id = e.media_id
         where e.done_at is null
         order by i.first, e.id`);
      return rows.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, mediaId: row.media_id }));
    },

    /** The provider took the purge: these rows, the ones a round read, close as accepted. Answers how many. */
    async edgeAccepted(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<number> {
      const closed = await db.execute(sql`update public.edge_purges set outcome = 'accepted', done_at = now() where id = any(${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::bigint[]) and done_at is null returning id`);
      return closed.length;
    },

    /**
     * The purge was not taken: each of these rows counts an attempt and is due again EDGE_RULES.backoffSeconds later,
     * doubled for each attempt before, at most EDGE_RULES.backoffMaxSeconds; a row written EDGE_RULES.giveUpHours ago or
     * earlier is given up, as failed. Answers how many were given up and the oldest time among them.
     */
    async edgeFailed(ids: readonly string[]): Promise<{ gaveUp: number; oldestAt: string | null }> {
      const giveUp = sql`e.created_at <= now() - make_interval(hours => ${EDGE_RULES.giveUpHours}::int)`;
      const [row] = await db.execute<{ gave_up: number; oldest_at: string | null }>(sql`
        with failed as (
          update public.edge_purges e
             set attempts = e.attempts + 1,
                 next_at = now() + make_interval(secs => least(${EDGE_RULES.backoffSeconds}::int * power(2, e.attempts), ${EDGE_RULES.backoffMaxSeconds}::int)),
                 outcome = case when ${giveUp} then 'failed' end,
                 done_at = case when ${giveUp} then now() end
           where e.id = any(${`{${ids.join(",")}}`}::bigint[]) and e.done_at is null
          returning e.outcome, e.created_at)
        select (count(*) filter (where outcome = 'failed'))::int as gave_up,
               to_char(min(created_at) filter (where outcome = 'failed') at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as oldest_at
          from failed`);
      return { gaveUp: row!.gave_up, oldestAt: row!.oldest_at };
    },

    /**
     * The job's own alert edge_purge_failed (3d design, section 7.14, "Alerts a job writes"): one row of the outbox of
     * alerts with its kind's priority and scope and its facts, counts and times only, under F's daily rule: none while a
     * row of the kind was written in the last 24 hours. F's two legs push and mail it. Answers whether it wrote one.
     */
    async edgeAlert(facts: { count: number; oldestAt: string }): Promise<boolean> {
      const entry = ALERT_KINDS.edge_purge_failed;
      const written = await db.execute(sql`
        insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts)
        select 'edge_purge_failed', ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope}, ${JSON.stringify(facts)}::jsonb
         where not exists (select 1 from public.alert_outbox o where o.kind = 'edge_purge_failed' and o.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24))
        returning id`);
      return written.length > 0;
    },

    /**
     * For each of these images that has an outbox row, in the order given, its newest row as staff read it (3d design,
     * section 10.3): its outcome, or pending while it has none, and when it was done, or written while it is pending. An
     * image with no row never stopped being public and gets no entry.
     */
    async purges(mediaIds: readonly string[]): Promise<EdgePurgeView[]> {
      if (mediaIds.length === 0) return [];
      const rows = await db.execute<{ media_id: string; outcome: EdgePurgeView["outcome"] | null; at: string }>(sql`
        select distinct on (e.media_id) e.media_id, e.outcome, to_char(coalesce(e.done_at, e.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as at
          from public.edge_purges e
         where e.media_id = any(${uuidArray(mediaIds)})
         order by e.media_id, e.id desc`);
      const newest = new Map(rows.map((row) => [row.media_id, row]));
      return mediaIds.flatMap((id) => {
        const row = newest.get(id);
        return row ? [{ mediaId: id, outcome: row.outcome ?? "pending", at: row.at }] : [];
      });
    },

    /** The same for every image row of these posts, erased or not, by post, in their order on the post: an order's items. */
    async postPurges(postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, EdgePurgeView[]>> {
      const byPost = new Map<string, EdgePurgeView[]>();
      if (postIds.length === 0) return byPost;
      const rows = await db.execute<{ post_id: string; media_id: string; outcome: EdgePurgeView["outcome"] | null; at: string }>(sql`
        select m.post_id, m.id as media_id, e.outcome, to_char(coalesce(e.done_at, e.created_at) at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"') as at
          from post_media m
          join lateral (select x.outcome, x.done_at, x.created_at from public.edge_purges x where x.media_id = m.id order by x.id desc limit 1) e on true
         where m.post_id = any(${uuidArray(postIds)})
         order by m.post_id, m.position, m.id`);
      for (const row of rows) byPost.set(row.post_id, [...(byPost.get(row.post_id) ?? []), { mediaId: row.media_id, outcome: row.outcome ?? "pending", at: row.at }]);
      return byPost;
    },

    async moderationStates(afterId: string | null, limit: number): Promise<{ id: string; postId: string; moderationState: MediaRow["moderationState"]; erasedAt: Date | null }[]> {
      const found = await db
        .select({ id: postMedia.id, postId: postMedia.postId, moderationState: postMedia.moderationState, erasedAt: postMedia.erasedAt })
        .from(postMedia)
        .where(and(isNotNull(postMedia.postId), afterId === null ? undefined : gt(postMedia.id, afterId)))
        .orderBy(postMedia.id)
        .limit(limit);
      return found.map((row) => ({ id: row.id, postId: row.postId!, moderationState: row.moderationState, erasedAt: row.erasedAt }));
    },

    /**
     * Deletes at most `limit` disposable rows (DISPOSABLE), the lowest ids first, inside the caller's transaction, and
     * answers the ids of the rows that are gone, in id order. The candidates are locked in id order inside the delete,
     * so the disposal and an intake's hold never lock one post's images in opposite orders; a candidate that another
     * transaction is making retained is waited for, checked again and skipped, and the batch is filled from the next ids.
     * The keep trigger decides for each row: a report that froze a candidate's post after this statement began is not
     * seen by its filter, and is seen by the trigger.
     *
     * The candidates are a materialized common table expression, which runs once. As a plain sub-select of the delete
     * they could run again for every row the delete looks at, when the planner joins the two by a nested loop: each run
     * skips the rows this statement has deleted already and lets the next ones in, so one call deleted more than its
     * limit (measured: 33 rows under a limit of 25).
     */
    async dropDisposable(tx: DbTx, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
      const rows = (await tx.execute(sql`
        with batch as materialized (
          select m.id
          from post_media m
          join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
          left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
          where ${DISPOSABLE}
          order by m.id
          limit ${limit}
          for update of m)
        delete from post_media where id in (select id from batch)
        returning id`)) as unknown as { id: string }[];
      return rows.map((row) => row.id).sort();
    },

    /**
     * How many rows the disposal should have taken by now: every disposable row none of whose holds ended, and none of
     * whose marks (its own erasure, its post's deletion or erasure) was set, within the last day. A hold ends when it is
     * released or when its time passes, whichever comes first. A row whose freeze ended within the last day may be
     * counted until the next round takes it: nothing records when a freeze ends.
     */
    async overdueDeletions(): Promise<number> {
      const [row] = (await db.execute(sql`
        select count(*)::int as n
        from post_media m
        join profiles o on o.id = m.owner_id
        left join posts p on p.id = m.post_id
        where ${DISPOSABLE}
          and not exists (select 1 from media_holds h where h.media_id = m.id and least(h.released_at, h.until) > now() - interval '1 day')
          and (m.erased_at is null or m.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.deleted_at is null or p.deleted_at <= now() - interval '1 day')
          and (p.erased_at is null or p.erased_at <= now() - interval '1 day')`)) as unknown as { n: number }[];
      return row!.n;
    },
  };
}

export type MediaRepo = ReturnType<typeof createMediaRepo>;
```

### Replace `apps/api/src/moderation/author.ts` (whole file)

```ts
import {
  AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE,
  mediaPath,
  type AuthorCasesPage,
  type DecisionAppeal,
  type DecisionContent,
  type DecisionStatement,
  type DecisionView,
  type ExportFormat,
  type OrderTexts,
  type PostModeration,
  type RuleId,
} from "@korbat/contracts";
import { askPersonOf, authorDecision, authorDecisions, chipFacts, type AuthorAppealFacts, type AuthorDecisionFacts, type AuthorDecisionRow } from "./author-repo";
import { objectionOf } from "./automated-repo";
import { ModerationError, type ModerationDeps } from "./context";
import { decisionStatement } from "./statement";
import { orderNoticeOf } from "./statement-repo";
import { decisionStandingView, reportingStandingView } from "./standing";
import { activeStrikesOf } from "./standing-repo";

/**
 * What the author of a post or the holder of an account reads about korbat's decisions on it (3c design, sections 7.6 and
 * 10): the list of decisions they were told of, one decision with its statement's data and the content it was made on,
 * the same decisions as their export lists them (section 7.11), and the facts behind the chip on their own post.
 * Everything here is built from the author's queries and the statement's
 * data, neither of which can reach a report: an author learns the source of a decision as a category, and nothing else
 * about who reported or how often.
 */

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- page cursors

const CURSOR_TIME = /^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}T[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}[.][0-9]{6}Z$/;
const CURSOR_ID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/;

/** Where a page of one of the app's moderation lists starts: after the row with this time (to the microsecond, as text) and id. */
export interface ListCursor {
  at: string;
  id: string;
}

/** A list's cursor: the last row's sort key as an opaque word. */
export const encodeListCursor = (cursor: ListCursor): string => Buffer.from(JSON.stringify([cursor.at, cursor.id]), "utf8").toString("base64url");

/** Reads a cursor back; anything this module did not write is refused, never guessed at. */
export function decodeListCursor(cursor: string): ListCursor {
  let parts: unknown;
  try {
    parts = JSON.parse(Buffer.from(cursor, "base64url").toString("utf8"));
  } catch {
    throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  }
  if (!Array.isArray(parts) || parts.length !== 2) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  const [at, id] = parts as unknown[];
  if (typeof at !== "string" || !CURSOR_TIME.test(at) || typeof id !== "string" || !CURSOR_ID.test(id)) throw new ModerationError("invalid_request");
  return { at, id };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the list

/** GET /api/moderation/cases: the decisions about the viewer's account that they were told of, newest first, 20 a page. */
export async function authorCases(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, viewer: string, cursor?: string): Promise<AuthorCasesPage> {
  const after = cursor === undefined ? null : decodeListCursor(cursor);
  const found = await authorDecisions(deps.apiDb, viewer, after, AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE + 1);
  const page = found.slice(0, AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE);
  const last = page.at(-1);
  return {
    decisions: page.map((row) => ({
      id: row.id,
      kind: row.kind,
      outcome: row.outcome as AuthorCasesPage["decisions"][number]["outcome"],
      decidedOn: row.decidedOn,
      post: row.post,
      actions: row.actions,
      endedInterim: row.endedInterim,
      ruleId: row.ruleId as RuleId | null,
      legal: row.legal,
      appealUntil: row.appealUntil,
      reversedOn: row.reversedOn,
      appeal: row.appeal,
      strike: row.strike,
      // 3e Task 5: what a row says of a restriction of reporting and of the measures a reversal ended; absent where none.
      ...(row.reportingDays !== null ? { reportingDays: row.reportingDays } : {}),
      ...(row.endedStanding.length > 0 ? { endedStanding: row.endedStanding } : {}),
      // 3e's review (people7): a suspension's or a termination's own words, and a lift's or a withdrawal's.
      ...(row.standingMeasure !== null ? { standingMeasure: row.standingMeasure } : {}),
      ...(row.liftedStanding !== null ? { liftedStanding: row.liftedStanding } : {}),
      // 3f: an order's notice, or the reinstatement after one, names no rule.
      ...(row.order !== null ? { order: row.order } : {}),
      // 3f's review (people9): an order decision's row shows the day its author was told.
      ...(row.toldOn !== null ? { toldOn: row.toldOn } : {}),
      // 3d Task 6 (section 9.4): a program's decision, whose screen shows [auto.chip].
      byProgram: row.byProgram,
    })),
    // One row more than the page was read: only then is there a next page.
    nextCursor: found.length > AUTHOR_CASES_PAGE_SIZE && last ? encodeListCursor({ at: last.sortAt, id: last.id }) : null,
    // The block "Your standing" above the list: the strikes that count now.
    activeStrikes: await activeStrikesOf(deps.apiDb, viewer),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- one decision

/**
 * The content a decision was made on, or the reason it is not shown; the first that applies, in this order (3c design,
 * section 10). The database's one predicate says whether the snapshot's content may be shown at all. Where it may not,
 * an R4 redaction of the post or the account is named before a plain erasure: content that was erased because it
 * doxxed someone is said to be gone for that reason, whichever decision is viewed. A snapshot withheld without being
 * erased is one whose post's content was erased since, which only a redaction does.
 */
function contentOf(facts: AuthorDecisionFacts): DecisionContent {
  if (facts.withheld) {
    if (facts.redacted || !facts.erased || facts.erasedOn === null) return { kind: "r4_redacted" };
    return { kind: "erased", contentErasedOn: facts.erasedOn, postKept: facts.targetType === "post" && !facts.postDeleted && !facts.postErased };
  }
  if (facts.targetType === "account") return { kind: "account", handle: facts.handle, displayName: facts.displayName ?? "", bio: facts.bio ?? "" };
  // A sealed image is shown to nobody, its author included, and an image of a post its author deleted is kept for the
  // case and served to nobody: for either, the answer carries how many there are and nothing of them. Otherwise the
  // author's own image route serves each image, a withheld or removed one too; an image whose description the snapshot
  // does not hold was erased before the copy was taken, and is not listed.
  const imagesHidden = facts.sealed ? "sealed" : facts.postDeleted ? "deleted_by_author" : null;
  const images =
    imagesHidden === null
      ? facts.images.flatMap((image) => (image.alt === null ? [] : [{ id: image.id, alt: image.alt, width: image.width, height: image.height, small: mediaPath(image.id, "small"), large: mediaPath(image.id, "large") }]))
      : [];
  return { kind: "post", body: facts.body ?? "", deletedByAuthor: facts.postDeleted, images, imageCount: facts.images.length, imagesHidden };
}

/**
 * The author's appeal as their screen shows it (3c design, section 7.7). A pending appeal says whether anyone may review
 * it now and whether its review is an admin's, in the database's own two answers, which name nobody. An answered one
 * carries the statement of the decision that answered it: the review, or the correction that reversed everything before
 * a review came, read as every statement is and so told to the author in the same words as its mail.
 */
async function appealOf(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, appeal: AuthorAppealFacts): Promise<DecisionAppeal> {
  if (appeal.answeredBy === null || appeal.result === null || appeal.answeredOn === null) {
    // An appeal that is not answered always has a reviewer state: the database answers null only for an answered one.
    return { state: "pending", filedAt: appeal.filedAt, reviewer: appeal.reviewer ?? "none_eligible", needsAdmin: appeal.needsAdmin };
  }
  const answer = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, appeal.answeredBy);
  if (!answer) throw new Error("an appeal is answered by a decision that does not exist");
  return { state: "answered", filedAt: appeal.filedAt, answeredOn: appeal.answeredOn, result: appeal.result, answeredBy: appeal.answeredBy, statement: answer.statement };
}

/**
 * GET /api/moderation/decisions/:id: one decision as its author reads it, or not_found: for an id that names no
 * decision, for a decision about someone else, and for one its author was not told of.
 */
export async function authorDecisionView(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb"> & Partial<Pick<ModerationDeps, "config">>, viewer: string, decisionId: string): Promise<DecisionView> {
  const facts = await authorDecision(deps.apiDb, viewer, decisionId);
  if (!facts) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  const found = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, decisionId, deps.config?.HOME_STATE ?? null);
  if (!found) throw new ModerationError("not_found");
  // 3f (section 10.4): an order's notice is read fresh, with the authority's words and (Task 4) the day the preservation's
  // end erased the post; the post is never shown while the order's measure stands, nor after that erasure.
  const notice = found.statement.order ? await orderNoticeOf(deps.apiDb, decisionId, deps.config?.HOME_STATE ?? null) : null;
  return {
    id: decisionId,
    ...found.statement,
    appealUntil: facts.appealUntil,
    reversedOn: facts.reversedOn,
    content: facts.orderInForce || facts.toldWhileDisabled || (notice?.erasedOn ?? null) !== null ? null : contentOf(facts),
    ...(notice !== null ? { orderTexts: notice.texts, erasedOn: notice.erasedOn } : {}),
    appeal: facts.appeal === null ? null : await appealOf(deps, facts.appeal),
    strike: facts.strike,
    // 3e Task 4: where the decision's suspension or termination stands now, beside the statement that never changes.
    standing: await decisionStandingView(deps.apiDb, decisionId),
    // 3e Task 5: and where its restriction of reporting stands now.
    reportingStanding: await reportingStandingView(deps.apiDb, decisionId),
    // 3d Task 6 (sections 7.10, 9.4 and 10.2): "Ask for a person" on a program's decision, read fresh; null otherwise.
    askPerson: await askPersonOf(deps.apiDb, decisionId),
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the export's decisions

/** A decision as the account's export lists it. */
export type ExportedDecision = ExportFormat["moderation"]["decisions"][number];

/** How many decisions the export reads at a time: one statement for the page, and then each decision's statement. */
const EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE = 100;

/**
 * One decision as the export writes it (3c design, section 7.11), from the two things its author's screens are built
 * from: its row in the list and its statement's data. So the entry holds what those screens show and nothing they do
 * not: the facts and the reason of a decision that restricted nothing are not in the statement's data, and a text that
 * was erased is null there. A statement names its source as a category; the entry does not carry even that.
 */
export function exportedDecision(
  row: Pick<AuthorDecisionRow, "id" | "decidedOn" | "post" | "appeal">,
  statement: DecisionStatement,
  texts: OrderTexts | null = null,
  erasedOn: string | null = null,
  objection: { text: string; createdAt: string } | null = null,
): ExportedDecision {
  return {
    id: row.id,
    decidedOn: row.decidedOn,
    // The entry of the export's `posts` a decision about a post concerns: a post keeps its row through its deletion.
    postId: row.post?.id ?? null,
    kind: statement.kind,
    outcome: statement.outcome,
    ground: statement.ground,
    ruleId: statement.ruleId,
    rulesVersion: statement.rulesVersion,
    measures: statement.measures.map((measure) => ({ kind: measure.kind, mediaId: measure.mediaId, noEffect: measure.noEffect })),
    reversals: statement.reversals.map((reversal) => ({ kind: reversal.kind, mediaId: reversal.mediaId })),
    facts: statement.facts,
    reason: statement.reason,
    legalReference: statement.legalReference,
    appeal: row.appeal === null ? null : row.appeal === "pending" ? { state: "pending", result: null } : { state: "answered", result: row.appeal },
    // 3f (W.7): an order's notice as its facts, with the authority's words read at the export's time and (Task 4) the day
    // the preservation's end erased the post.
    ...(statement.order ? { order: statement.order, ...(texts ? { orderTexts: texts } : {}), erasedOn } : {}),
    // 3d Task 8 (W.10): what the statement says of automated means, read as the statement reads it (a decision made before
    // 3d: false, not_automated and null), and the text its subject sent with "Ask for a person", with its time.
    automatedDetection: statement.automatedDetection ?? false,
    automatedDecision: statement.automatedDecision ?? "not_automated",
    signal: statement.signal ?? null,
    objection,
  };
}

/**
 * The export's `decisions` (ModerationForAccount.exportFor): every decision about the account that its Cases screen
 * lists, which are those its author was told of, newest first as the screen lists them. Read through the list's own
 * query, a page at a time, and each decision's statement through the statement's own read, so no decision the author was
 * not told of, and nothing a statement does not tell, can be in an export.
 */
export async function exportedDecisions(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, accountId: string): Promise<ExportedDecision[]> {
  const exported: ExportedDecision[] = [];
  let after: ListCursor | null = null;
  for (;;) {
    const page: AuthorDecisionRow[] = await authorDecisions(deps.apiDb, accountId, after, EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE);
    for (const row of page) {
      const found = await decisionStatement(deps.apiDb, row.id);
      // A decision is a row for good: one the list has just named has a statement.
      if (!found) throw new Error("a decision in its author's list has no statement");
      const notice = found.statement.order ? await orderNoticeOf(deps.apiDb, row.id, null) : null;
      // 3d Task 8 (W.10): only a program's decision can have been asked about.
      const objection = found.statement.automatedDecision === "fully" ? await objectionOf(deps.apiDb, row.id) : null;
      exported.push(exportedDecision(row, found.statement, notice?.texts ?? null, notice?.erasedOn ?? null, objection));
    }
    const last = page.at(-1);
    // A page that is not full is the last one.
    if (page.length < EXPORT_PAGE_SIZE || !last) return exported;
    after = { at: last.sortAt, id: last.id };
  }
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the chip

/**
 * ModerationForSocial.authorFacts: for each of these posts that the viewer wrote and that is withheld or removed, the
 * decision its chip names. One query a page, asked only when the viewer wrote some of the page's restricted posts.
 */
export function authorFacts(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, viewer: string, postIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, PostModeration>> {
  return chipFacts(deps.apiDb, viewer, postIds);
}
```

```ts
import { sql } from "drizzle-orm";
import { ALERT_KINDS, statementMatchKind, type AutomatedDecidedParams, type CaseFlag, type MatchHashType, type MatchKind, type SignalHandled, type SignalKind, type StatementSignal } from "@korbat/contracts";
import type { DbTx } from "@korbat/db";
import { iso, rows, type Runner } from "./repo";

/**
 * The automated decision's statements (3d design, sections 6.6, 7.9 and 7.10; Task 6): the signals, a decision without a
 * decider, the requests for a person, and what the case page, the queue, the home screen and the statement read of them.
 * Every write is the API's role's, through the grants and triggers of the migration automated_decisions: a signal's last
 * four columns are set once each, an objection is inserted once and refused unless its decision's measure is in force,
 * and a decision without a decider stands only when decision_holds passes at commit.
 */

/** A signal as the step reads it. */
export interface SignalRow {
  id: string;
  kind: SignalKind;
  mediaId: string;
  score: number | null;
  thresholdVersion: number | null;
  /** 3d Task 7: a known_match's record; null for a score. */
  matchId: string | null;
  createdAt: string;
  intakeItemId: string | null;
  decisionId: string | null;
  handledAt: string | null;
  handled: SignalHandled | null;
}

type RawSignal = {
  id: string;
  kind: SignalKind;
  media_id: string;
  score: number | null;
  threshold_version: number | null;
  match_id: string | null;
  created_at: string;
  intake_item_id: string | null;
  decision_id: string | null;
  handled_at: string | null;
  handled: SignalHandled | null;
};

const SIGNAL_COLUMNS = sql`s.id, s.kind, s.media_id, s.score, s.threshold_version, s.match_id, ${iso("s.created_at")} as created_at, s.intake_item_id, s.decision_id, ${iso("s.handled_at")} as handled_at, s.handled`;

const signalOfRow = (row: RawSignal): SignalRow => ({
  id: row.id,
  kind: row.kind,
  mediaId: row.media_id,
  score: row.score === null ? null : Number(row.score),
  thresholdVersion: row.threshold_version,
  matchId: row.match_id,
  createdAt: row.created_at,
  intakeItemId: row.intake_item_id,
  decisionId: row.decision_id,
  handledAt: row.handled_at,
  handled: row.handled,
});

/**
 * Step 1 of the automated step (7.9): the signal of a score, one statement that does nothing when the image has a
 * signal of the kind already, handled or not (automated_signals_one is over all rows), so a handled one is never written
 * again beside it. Answers the new signal's id, or null when there was one.
 */
export async function insertScoreSignal(q: Runner, signal: { mediaId: string; score: number; thresholdVersion: number }): Promise<string | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`insert into public.automated_signals (kind, media_id, score, threshold_version)
        values ('r1_score', ${signal.mediaId}::uuid, ${signal.score}::real, ${signal.thresholdVersion}::smallint)
        on conflict (media_id, kind) do nothing
        returning id`,
  );
  return row?.id ?? null;
}

/**
 * 3d Task 7 (7.9 step 1): the signal of a match record of an image on a post, one statement that does nothing when the
 * image has a match's signal already, handled or not. Answers the new signal's id, or null when there was one.
 */
export async function insertMatchSignal(q: Runner, signal: { mediaId: string; matchId: string }): Promise<string | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`insert into public.automated_signals (kind, media_id, match_id)
        values ('known_match', ${signal.mediaId}::uuid, ${signal.matchId}::uuid)
        on conflict (media_id, kind) do nothing
        returning id`,
  );
  return row?.id ?? null;
}

/** A signal by its id, or null. Inside the step it is a statement of its own after the profile's lock. */
export async function signalOf(q: Runner, signalId: string): Promise<SignalRow | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<RawSignal>(q, sql`select ${SIGNAL_COLUMNS} from public.automated_signals s where s.id = ${signalId}::uuid`);
  return row ? signalOfRow(row) : null;
}

/** The image's signal of a kind, or null. */
export async function signalFor(q: Runner, mediaId: string, kind: SignalKind): Promise<SignalRow | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<RawSignal>(q, sql`select ${SIGNAL_COLUMNS} from public.automated_signals s where s.media_id = ${mediaId}::uuid and s.kind = ${kind}`);
  return row ? signalOfRow(row) : null;
}

/** Step 2.2's last write: the finding's item on its signal, once (the guard refuses a second). */
export async function joinSignal(tx: DbTx, signalId: string, itemId: string): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`update public.automated_signals set intake_item_id = ${itemId}::uuid where id = ${signalId}::uuid`);
}

/**
 * What the step did with the signal, once, with the decision of a measure: `measure` names its decision, every other end
 * names none. The guard forces handled_at to the database's now().
 */
export async function signalHandled(tx: DbTx, signalId: string, handled: SignalHandled, decisionId: string | null = null): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`update public.automated_signals set handled = ${handled}, handled_at = now(), decision_id = ${decisionId}::uuid where id = ${signalId}::uuid`);
}

/**
 * A decision without a decider (7.9 step 2.4), from the params the system's audit row will carry: no decider and no text;
 * everything else the row holds is the triggers'. The id is the API's, so the audit row and the signal can name it.
 */
export async function insertSystemDecision(tx: DbTx, row: { id: string; caseId: string; params: AutomatedDecidedParams }): Promise<void> {
  const p = row.params;
  await tx.execute(
    sql`insert into public.decisions (id, case_id, kind, reviews_decision_id, seen_state_version, through_seq, outcome, ground, rule_id, rules_version, redress_version, category, category_keyword,
                                      snapshot_id, snapshot_digest, facts_digest, reason_digest, legal_reference_digest, decided_by)
        values (${row.id}::uuid, ${row.caseId}::uuid, ${p.kind}::decision_kind, null, ${p.stateVersion}::int, ${p.throughSeq}::int, ${p.outcome}::decision_outcome,
                ${p.ground}::decision_ground, ${p.ruleId}, ${p.rulesVersion}::smallint, ${p.redressVersion}::smallint, ${p.category}, null,
                ${p.snapshotId}::uuid, ${p.snapshotDigest}, null, null, null, null)`,
  );
}

/**
 * The sweep's own read (7.9, "What starts it"): the signals of these kinds that no step handled, between one minute and
 * `hours` hours old, the oldest first: what a crash or a failed step left. The minute leaves a step started by an entry
 * its time to commit.
 */
export async function unhandledSignals(q: Runner, kinds: readonly SignalKind[], hours: number, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
  if (kinds.length === 0 || limit <= 0) return [];
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select s.id from public.automated_signals s
         where s.handled_at is null and s.kind = any(${`{${kinds.join(",")}}`}::text[])
           and s.created_at < now() - make_interval(mins => 1) and s.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => ${hours}::int)
         order by s.created_at, s.id limit ${limit}::int`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/**
 * The fact `count` of the alert automation_capped: the findings that stand without a measure since the cap was met, that
 * is the signals handled `capped` since the newest one a program took a measure on.
 */
export async function cappedSinceLastMeasure(q: Runner): Promise<number> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ n: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n from public.automated_signals s
         where s.handled = 'capped'
           and s.handled_at >= coalesce((select max(m.handled_at) from public.automated_signals m where m.handled = 'measure'), '-infinity'::timestamptz)`,
  );
  return row!.n;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- "Ask for a person"

/** The one statement that writes an objection; its trigger refuses objection_not_open, and a second one meets the key. */
export async function insertObjection(q: Runner, decisionId: string, text: string): Promise<void> {
  await q.execute(sql`insert into public.automated_objections (decision_id, text) values (${decisionId}::uuid, ${text})`);
}

/** The requests for a person whose measure is in force: unanswered, since nothing stores an answer. With the oldest's time. */
export async function objectionsWaiting(q: Runner): Promise<{ count: number; oldestAt: string | null }> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ n: number; oldest: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n, ${iso("min(o.created_at)")} as oldest from public.automated_objections o
         where exists (select 1 from public.measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = o.decision_id)`,
  );
  return { count: row!.n, oldestAt: row!.oldest };
}

/**
 * The sweep's daily alert automated_waiting (7.14, "Alerts a job writes"): when requests for a person have waited longer
 * than the published target with their measures in force, one row of the outbox with their count and the oldest one's
 * time, under F's daily rule: none while a row of the kind was written in the last 24 hours. Answers whether it wrote one.
 */
export async function automatedWaitingAlert(q: Runner, targetHours: number): Promise<boolean> {
  const entry = ALERT_KINDS.automated_waiting;
  const written = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`insert into public.alert_outbox (kind, priority, scope, facts)
        select 'automated_waiting', ${entry.priority}, ${entry.scope},
               jsonb_build_object('count', w.n, 'oldestAt', to_char(w.oldest at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.MS"Z"'))
          from (select count(*)::int as n, min(o.created_at) as oldest from public.automated_objections o
                 where o.created_at < now() - make_interval(hours => ${targetHours}::int)
                   and exists (select 1 from public.measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = o.decision_id)) w
         where w.n > 0
           and not exists (select 1 from public.alert_outbox x where x.kind = 'automated_waiting' and x.created_at > now() - make_interval(hours => 24))
        returning id`,
  );
  return written.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what staff read

/** Home's two counts of a program's measures (8.2): those in force waiting for a person, and those whose author asked for one. */
export async function automatedOverview(q: Runner, max: number): Promise<{ waiting: number; oldestAt: string | null; objected: number; oldestObjectionAt: string | null; cases: string[]; objectedCases: string[] }> {
  const [waiting] = await rows<{ n: number; oldest: string | null; cases: string[] | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n, ${iso("min(w.decided_at)")} as oldest,

                  select d.case_id, d.decided_at from public.measures_in_force m join public.decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id where d.decided_by is null) x
                 group by x.case_id order by min(x.decided_at), x.case_id limit ${max}::int) c) as cases

  );
  const [objected] = await rows<{ n: number; oldest: string | null; cases: string[] | null }>(

                 group by x.case_id order by min(x.created_at), x.case_id limit ${max}::int) c) as cases
          from (select d.case_id, o.created_at from public.automated_objections o join public.decisions d on d.id = o.decision_id

/**

export async function queueFlags(q: Runner, caseIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, CaseFlag>> {

  const found = await rows<{ case_id: string; items: number; reporters: number }>(

    sql`select c.id as case_id, f.items, f.reporters
          from unnest(${`{${caseIds.join(",")}}`}::uuid[]) as c(id) cross join lateral public.case_flag(c.id) f
         where f.coordinated`,
  );
  return new Map(found.map((row) => [row.case_id, { items: row.items, reporters: row.reporters }]));
}

/** The case answer's read of its own case's flag ([case.flag]): the two counts while case_flag answers true, else null. */
export async function caseFlag(q: Runner, caseId: string): Promise<CaseFlag | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ coordinated: boolean; items: number; reporters: number }>(q, sql`select f.coordinated, f.items, f.reporters from public.case_flag(${caseId}::uuid) f`);
  return row !== undefined && row.coordinated ? { items: row.items, reporters: row.reporters } : null;
}

/**
 * 3d Task 8 (design, sections 6.8 and 7.14): the retention job's step automation_records, one call of the database's
 * erase_automation_records in the step's transaction. The function decides every rule itself, against the database's
 * clock and automation_rules(), so the job names nothing and the API learns only how many rows it changed.
 */
export async function eraseAutomationRecords(tx: DbTx): Promise<number> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ n: number }>(tx, sql`select public.erase_automation_records() as n`);
  return row!.n;
}

 * (erase_automation_records takes the text with its decision's texts), for the export's entry of that decision; null for a
 * decision without one.
 */
export async function objectionOf(q: Runner, decisionId: string): Promise<{ text: string; createdAt: string } | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ text: string; created_at: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select o.text, ${iso("o.created_at")} as created_at from public.automated_objections o where o.decision_id = ${decisionId}::uuid and o.text is not null`,
  );
  return row ? { text: row.text, createdAt: row.created_at } : null;

/** The request for a person about a program's measure in force on the case (CaseView.objection), or null; the oldest when several stand. */
export async function caseObjection(q: Runner, caseId: string): Promise<{ text: string; createdAt: string } | null> {

    sql`select o.text, ${iso("o.created_at")} as created_at from public.automated_objections o join public.decisions d on d.id = o.decision_id
         where d.case_id = ${caseId}::uuid and o.text is not null and exists (select 1 from public.measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = o.decision_id)
         order by o.created_at limit 1`,
  );
  return row ? { text: row.text, createdAt: row.created_at } : null;
}

/**
 * 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.11 step 6 and W.8): whether the decision's case holds a program's finding on a match, of
 * either kind: moderation_csam_lifted then goes in its variant that leaves out "staff may open them".
 */
export async function decisionCaseHasMatch(q: Runner, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ matched: boolean }>(
    q,
    sql`select exists (select 1 from public.decisions d join public.intake_items i on i.case_id = d.case_id join public.automated_signals s on s.intake_item_id = i.id
                        where d.id = ${decisionId}::uuid and s.kind = 'known_match') as matched`,
  );
  return row!.matched;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- what the statement reads

/**
 * The automated finding a statement speaks of (DecisionStatement.signal; 7.10, 10.2), read from the decision's own
 * columns and its signal, never from a later event. A decision without a decider: its own signal. A person's decision:
 * the first program's item it considered (a final decision the items it answered; one taken while deciding the items
 * unanswered at its time), and a correction or a review the decision it is about's. For a score, `viewed` is true on a
 * person's decision when the case's access log holds that person's view of the signal's image on this case before the
 * decision and the decision is not stored as unseen; null on a program's. Null when the decision considered no program's
 * finding. It reads the program's items and nothing of a report: no sender, no word and no count.
 */
export async function statementSignal(q: Runner, decisionId: string, matchOf?: (matchId: string) => Promise<{ source: string; hashType: MatchHashType; matchKind: MatchKind; listed: boolean } | null>): Promise<StatementSignal | null> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ kind: SignalKind; viewed: boolean | null; match_id: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`with d as (select x.id, x.case_id, x.kind, x.decided_by, x.decided_at, x.unseen, x.reviews_decision_id from public.decisions x where x.id = ${decisionId}::uuid),
             -- The decision whose considered items count: the reviewed one for a review or a correction, else itself.
             c as (select coalesce(r.id, d.id) as id, coalesce(r.decided_by, d.decided_by) as decided_by, coalesce(r.kind, d.kind) as kind,
                          coalesce(r.decided_at, d.decided_at) as decided_at, d.case_id
                     from d left join public.decisions r on r.id = d.reviews_decision_id and d.kind::text in ('review', 'correction'))
        select s.kind, s.match_id,
               case when d.decided_by is null then null
                    else not d.unseen and exists (select 1 from public.case_access_log l
                                                    where l.case_id = d.case_id and l.staff_id = d.decided_by and l.kind = 'image_viewed'
                                                      and l.media_id = s.media_id and l.at < d.decided_at) end as viewed
          from d, c, public.automated_signals s
         where (c.decided_by is null and s.decision_id = c.id)
            or (c.decided_by is not null and s.intake_item_id in (
                  select i.id from public.intake_items i
                   where i.case_id = c.case_id
                     and case when c.kind::text = 'final' then i.answered_by = c.id
                              else i.created_at <= c.decided_at
                                   and (i.answered_by is null or (select a.decided_at from public.decisions a where a.id = i.answered_by) > c.decided_at) end))
         order by s.created_at, s.id limit 1`,
  );
  if (!row) return null;
  if (row.kind === "known_match") {
    // 3d Task 7 (10.2, W.3): the source's name, the kind of match derived from the hash type (exact only for a
    // cryptographic hash's exact match) and whether the source lists the class; never the hash type, the list version or
    // the classification string. viewed is null for a match: nobody at korbat opens such an image.
    const record = row.match_id === null || matchOf === undefined ? null : await matchOf(row.match_id);
    if (record === null) return { kind: row.kind, source: null, matchKind: null, listedAs: null, viewed: null };
    return { kind: row.kind, source: record.source, matchKind: statementMatchKind(record.hashType, record.matchKind), listedAs: record.listed ? "csam" : "other", viewed: null };
  }
  return { kind: row.kind, source: null, matchKind: null, listedAs: null, viewed: row.viewed };
}
```

```ts
/** A reply as the case page shows it: its text while korbat keeps it, which an erasure blanks. */
```
