  const [row] = await rows<{ handle: string }>(q, sql`select p.handle from intake_items i join profiles p on p.id = i.reporter_account_id where i.id = ${itemId}::uuid`);
  return row?.handle ?? null;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the console: the queue

/** A row of the queue with its sort key: the lane, whether it is deferred, the oldest unanswered item's time to the microsecond, and the id. */
export interface QueueRead {
  id: string;
  lane: Lane;
  targetType: TargetType;
  openedAt: string;
  oldestOpenAt: string;
  /** The same time as the database holds it, to the microsecond: the cursor's. */
  sortAt: string;
  openItems: number;
  rules: string[];
  categories: string[];
  allegesIllegal: boolean;
  suspect: boolean;
  reexamination: boolean;
  deferred: boolean;
  /** 3d Task 6: an unanswered program's finding citing R1 or R2; a program's measure in force; a request for a person about one. */
  foundByProgram: boolean;
  takenByProgram: boolean;
  objected: boolean;
}

/**
 * The place after which a page of the queue begins: the last row's sort key. 3d Task 6: with whether the case was
 * objected, which sorts first inside its lane.
 */
export interface QueueCursor {
  lane: number;
  objected: boolean;
  deferred: boolean;
  sortAt: string;
  id: string;
}

/**
 * Open cases in the queue's order: by lane, then (only with the emergency switch on) the deferred ones last within their
 * lane, then by the oldest unanswered item, then by id. A case is deferred when every unanswered item of it comes from an
 * unproven source: in lanes 1 and 2 a signed-out intake or an account under 48 hours old, in lane 0 a signed-out intake
 * only, so a new account reporting a threat against itself is never deferred. Nothing else orders the queue: no count of
 * reports and no standing of a reporter. `limit` rows after `after`.
 *
 * 3d Task 6 (design, sections 7.10 and 8.3): a case whose author asked for a person about a program's measure in force
 * sorts first inside its lane, before the switch's deferral and before age, so MODERATION_DEFER_UNPROVEN never moves it
 * down; the two other marks of a program move nothing.
 */
export async function queueRows(q: Runner, options: { deferUnproven: boolean; after: QueueCursor | null; limit: number }): Promise<QueueRead[]> {
  const after = options.after;
  const found = await rows<{
    id: string;
    lane: Lane;
    target_type: TargetType;
    opened_at: string;
    oldest_open_at: string;
    sort_at: string;
    open_items: number;
    rules: string;
    categories: string;
    alleges_illegal: boolean;
    suspect: boolean;
    reexamination: boolean;
    deferred: boolean;
    found_by_program: boolean;
    taken_by_program: boolean;
    objected: boolean;
  }>(
    q,
    sql`with open_cases as (
          select c.id, c.lane, c.target_type, c.opened_at, coalesce(c.oldest_open_at, c.opened_at) as oldest_open_at, u.open_items, u.rules, u.categories, u.alleges_illegal, u.suspect, u.reexamination,
                 (${options.deferUnproven}::boolean and u.unproven) as deferred, u.found_by_program,
                 exists (select 1 from measures_in_force m join decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id where m.case_id = c.id and d.decided_by is null) as taken_by_program,
                 exists (select 1 from automated_objections o join decisions d on d.id = o.decision_id
                          where d.case_id = c.id and exists (select 1 from measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = o.decision_id)) as objected
            from cases c
           cross join lateral (
             select count(*)::int as open_items,
                    coalesce(string_agg(distinct n.rule_id, ',' order by n.rule_id), '') as rules,
                    coalesce(string_agg(distinct n.category, ',' order by n.category), '') as categories,
                    coalesce(bool_or(i.alleges_illegal), false) as alleges_illegal,
                    coalesce(bool_or(i.suspect), false) as suspect,
                    coalesce(bool_or(i.reexamines_item_id is not null), false) as reexamination,
                    coalesce(bool_or(n.kind::text = 'automated' and n.rule_id in ('R1', 'R2')), false) as found_by_program,
                    coalesce(bool_and(n.channel = 'signed_out'
                                      or (c.lane > 0 and exists (select 1 from profiles r where r.id = i.reporter_account_id and r.created_at > now() - interval '48 hours'))), false) as unproven
               from intake_items i join intakes n on n.id = i.intake_id
              where i.case_id = c.id and i.answered_by is null) u
           where c.closed_at is null)
        select o.id, o.lane, o.target_type, ${iso("o.opened_at")} as opened_at, ${iso("o.oldest_open_at")} as oldest_open_at,
               to_char(o.oldest_open_at at time zone 'UTC', 'YYYY-MM-DD"T"HH24:MI:SS.US"Z"') as sort_at,
               o.open_items, o.rules, o.categories, o.alleges_illegal, o.suspect, o.reexamination, o.deferred, o.found_by_program, o.taken_by_program, o.objected
          from open_cases o
         where ${after === null ? sql`true` : sql`(o.lane, not o.objected, o.deferred, o.oldest_open_at, o.id) > (${after.lane}::smallint, ${!after.objected}::boolean, ${after.deferred}::boolean, ${after.sortAt}::timestamptz, ${after.id}::uuid)`}
         order by o.lane, not o.objected, o.deferred, o.oldest_open_at, o.id
         limit ${options.limit}::int`,
  );
  const list = (joined: string) => (joined === "" ? [] : joined.split(","));
  return found.map((row) => ({
    id: row.id,
    lane: row.lane,
    targetType: row.target_type,
    openedAt: row.opened_at,
    oldestOpenAt: row.oldest_open_at,
    sortAt: row.sort_at,
    openItems: row.open_items,
    rules: list(row.rules),
    categories: list(row.categories),
    allegesIllegal: row.alleges_illegal,
    suspect: row.suspect,
    reexamination: row.reexamination,
    deferred: row.deferred,
    foundByProgram: row.found_by_program,
    takenByProgram: row.taken_by_program,
    objected: row.objected,
  }));
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the console: the overview

/** Per lane, the open cases and since when the oldest unanswered item of the lane waits. A lane without an open case has no row. */
export async function openByLane(q: Runner): Promise<{ lane: Lane; open: number; oldestAt: string | null }[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ lane: Lane; open: number; oldest: string | null }>(q, sql`select lane, count(*)::int as open, ${iso("min(oldest_open_at)")} as oldest from cases where closed_at is null group by lane`);
  return found.map((row) => ({ lane: row.lane, open: row.open, oldestAt: row.oldest }));
}

/**
 * The pending appeals as the home screen counts them: how many wait, how many of them this person may review, and how
 * many no staff account may review now (the database's appeal_reviewer_state is not `available`).
 */
export async function appealCounts(q: Runner, person: Reviewer): Promise<{ waiting: number; mayReview: number; withoutReviewer: number }> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ waiting: number; may_review: number; without_reviewer: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(*)::int as waiting,
               (count(*) filter (where ${mayReview(person)}))::int as may_review,
               (count(*) filter (where public.appeal_reviewer_state(a.id) is distinct from 'available'))::int as without_reviewer
          from appeals a join decisions d on d.id = a.decision_id where a.answered_by is null`,
  );
  return { waiting: row!.waiting, mayReview: row!.may_review, withoutReviewer: row!.without_reviewer };
}

/** The reveals of the last 30 days, newest first, at most `max`, with how many there are in all: time, staff handle and case. */
export async function recentReveals(q: Runner, max: number): Promise<{ total: number; items: { at: string; handle: string; caseId: string }[] }> {
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; handle: string; case_id: string; total: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("l.at")} as at, p.handle, l.case_id, (count(*) over ())::int as total
          from case_access_log l join profiles p on p.id = l.staff_id
         where l.kind = 'identity_revealed' and l.at >= now() - interval '30 days'
         order by l.at desc, l.id desc limit ${max}::int`,
  );
  return { total: found[0]?.total ?? 0, items: found.map((row) => ({ at: row.at, handle: row.handle, caseId: row.case_id })) };
}

/** Per staff handle, the images viewed and the findings opened since midnight UTC. */
export async function staffToday(q: Runner): Promise<{ images: { handle: string; count: number }[]; findings: { handle: string; count: number }[] }> {
  const images = await rows<{ handle: string; count: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select p.handle, count(*)::int as count from case_access_log l join profiles p on p.id = l.staff_id where l.kind = 'image_viewed' and l.at >= ${TODAY} group by p.handle order by p.handle`,
  );
  const findings = await rows<{ handle: string; count: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select p.handle, count(*)::int as count from intakes n join profiles p on p.id = n.finding_by where n.kind = 'finding' and n.received_at >= ${TODAY} group by p.handle order by p.handle`,
  );
  return { images: images.map((row) => ({ handle: row.handle, count: row.count })), findings: findings.map((row) => ({ handle: row.handle, count: row.count })) };
}

/** The three kinds of mail by what they wait for, and the decided items the daily release has not released. Counts only. */
export interface MailCounts {
  receipts: number;
  authorMails: number;
  outcomes: number;
}

/**
 * Mails pending for more than an hour, counted from when each became due (an intake's receipt, a decision's time, an
 * outcome's release); mails recorded failed whose give-up time (`giveUpDays` after that same moment) falls in the last 30
 * days; and the items with an outcome that the daily release has not released 26 hours after their decision, or whose
 * changed outcome has waited that long. The release takes about a day at most, so any of the last means it is not
 * finishing.
 */
export async function mailAndReleaseCounts(q: Runner, giveUpDays: number): Promise<{ waiting: MailCounts; failed: MailCounts; releaseOverdue: number }> {
  const gaveUp = (at: string) => sql.raw(`${at} + make_interval(days => ${Number(giveUpDays)}) >= now() - interval '30 days'`);
  const [row] = await rows<Record<string, number>>(
    q,
    sql`select
          (select count(*)::int from intakes where receipt = 'pending' and received_at < now() - interval '1 hour') as receipts_waiting,
          (select count(*)::int from decisions where author_mail = 'pending' and decided_at < now() - interval '1 hour') as author_waiting,
          (select count(*)::int from intake_items where outcome_mail = 'pending' and coalesce(revised_sent_at, outcome_sent_at) < now() - interval '1 hour') as outcomes_waiting,
          (select count(*)::int from intakes where receipt = 'failed' and ${gaveUp("received_at")}) as receipts_failed,
          (select count(*)::int from decisions where author_mail = 'failed' and ${gaveUp("decided_at")}) as author_failed,
          (select count(*)::int from intake_items where outcome_mail = 'failed' and ${gaveUp("coalesce(revised_sent_at, outcome_sent_at)")}) as outcomes_failed,
          (select count(*)::int from intake_items i
            where i.outcome is not null and i.outcome_sent_at is null
              and coalesce((select d.decided_at from decisions d where d.id = i.answered_by), i.created_at) < now() - interval '26 hours')
          + (select count(*)::int from intake_items i where i.revision_pending_at < now() - interval '26 hours') as release_overdue`,
  );
  return {
    waiting: { receipts: row!.receipts_waiting!, authorMails: row!.author_waiting!, outcomes: row!.outcomes_waiting! },
    failed: { receipts: row!.receipts_failed!, authorMails: row!.author_failed!, outcomes: row!.outcomes_failed! },
    releaseOverdue: row!.release_overdue!,
  };
}

/** The decisions of the last 30 days that lifted the protection of reported images: each lifted seal, and each final answer to a suspect item without a seal. Newest first, at most `max`, with their total. */
export async function recentProtectionLifted(q: Runner, max: number): Promise<{ total: number; items: { at: string; handle: string; caseId: string; kind: "unsealed" | "dismissed" }[] }> {
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; handle: string; case_id: string; kind: "unsealed" | "dismissed"; total: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("d.decided_at")} as at, p.handle, d.case_id, (count(*) over ())::int as total,
               case when exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'unseal_media') then 'unsealed' else 'dismissed' end as kind
          from decisions d join profiles p on p.id = d.decided_by
         where d.decided_at >= now() - interval '30 days'
           and (exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'unseal_media')
                or (d.kind = 'final' and d.suspect and not exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind = 'seal_media')))
         order by d.decided_at desc, d.id desc limit ${max}::int`,
  );
  return { total: found[0]?.total ?? 0, items: found.map((row) => ({ at: row.at, handle: row.handle, caseId: row.case_id, kind: row.kind })) };
}

/** The recorded choices not to seal of the last 30 days, newest first, at most `max`, with their total: time, staff handle and case, never the reason. */
export async function recentSealsDeclined(q: Runner, max: number): Promise<{ total: number; items: { at: string; handle: string; caseId: string }[] }> {
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; handle: string; case_id: string; total: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("t.created_at")} as at, p.handle, t.case_id, (count(*) over ())::int as total
          from staff_texts t join profiles p on p.id = t.author_id
         where t.kind = 'seal_declined' and t.created_at >= now() - interval '30 days'
         order by t.created_at desc, t.id desc limit ${max}::int`,
  );
  return { total: found[0]?.total ?? 0, items: found.map((row) => ({ at: row.at, handle: row.handle, caseId: row.case_id })) };
}

/** The seals taken while deciding that are in force, by the view's one definition, newest first: who took each, on which case, and what its list covers. */
export async function interimSealsInForce(q: Runner, max: number): Promise<{ total: number; items: { at: string; handle: string | null; caseId: string; posts: number; images: number }[] }> {
  // 3d Task 6: a seal a program took (Task 7's automatic seal) has no decider: the left join keeps it, with no handle.
  const found = await rows<{ at: string; handle: string | null; case_id: string; posts: number; images: number; total: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select ${iso("d.decided_at")} as at, p.handle, m.case_id, (count(*) over ())::int as total,
               (select count(*)::int from seal_posts s where s.action_id = m.id) as posts,
               (select coalesce(sum(s.images), 0)::int from seal_posts s where s.action_id = m.id) as images
          from measures_in_force m join decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id left join profiles p on p.id = d.decided_by
         where m.kind = 'seal_media' and m.decision_kind = 'interim'
         order by d.decided_at desc, m.id desc limit ${max}::int`,
  );
  return { total: found[0]?.total ?? 0, items: found.map((row) => ({ at: row.at, handle: row.handle, caseId: row.case_id, posts: row.posts, images: row.images })) };
}

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 8.2 and 10.3): the quarantine's counts for the home screen, the four values of
 * quarantine_counts() and nothing else: the API's role reaches the quarantine through such functions alone.
 */
export async function quarantineCounts(q: Runner): Promise<{ dueIn: number; dueOut: number; undestroyed: number; oldest: string | null }> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ due_in: number; due_out: number; undestroyed: number; oldest: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select c.due_in, c.due_out, c.undestroyed, ${iso("c.oldest")} as oldest from public.quarantine_counts() c`,
  );
  return { dueIn: row!.due_in, dueOut: row!.due_out, undestroyed: row!.undestroyed, oldest: row!.oldest };
}

/**
 * 3d (design, sections 6.1, 8.4 and 10.3): where the files of each of these seals are, by seal_custody(action), keyed by
 * the seal's ledger row: counts and one time, never a file's name or digest.
 */
export async function sealCustody(q: Runner, actionIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Map<string, { files: number; moved: number; movedAt: string | null; toReturn: number; filesLeft: number; lost: number }>> {
  const custody = new Map<string, { files: number; moved: number; movedAt: string | null; toReturn: number; filesLeft: number; lost: number }>();
  for (const actionId of actionIds) {
    const [row] = await rows<{ files: number; moved: number; moved_at: string | null; to_return: number; files_left: number; lost: number }>(
      q,
      sql`select c.files, c.moved, ${iso("c.moved_at")} as moved_at, c.to_return, c.files_left, c.lost from public.seal_custody(${actionId}::uuid) c`,
    );
    custody.set(actionId, { files: row!.files, moved: row!.moved, movedAt: row!.moved_at, toReturn: row!.to_return, filesLeft: row!.files_left, lost: row!.lost });
  }
  return custody;
}

/** What became of a mail korbat owed: the delivery states a send can end in. */
export type MailState = "sent" | "suppressed" | "no_address" | "failed";

/**
 * Records what became of a decision's statement mail, only while it is still pending, so a late answer never overwrites
 * one already recorded. True when this call recorded it.
 */
/**
 * How long a transaction that records a mail's result waits for the row it records it on. Such a transaction holds the
 * row while the relay takes the mail (at most the mailer's 30 seconds), so a second sender of the same mail waits here,
 * and then finds it recorded.
 */
export const MAIL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS = 5_000;

/**
 * The start of a transaction that will send a mail and record its result on a row (3c design, section 7.8, as the review
 * of the built code corrected it): the wait for a lock is bounded, and the rows are then taken with one of the three
 * functions below, before anything is sent. Taking a row for update is a write: a database that answers reads and cannot
 * write (a server in recovery, a full disk, default_transaction_read_only) refuses it, so a mail whose result could not
 * be recorded is never sent, however often it is tried. The result is recorded in the same transaction.
 */
export async function beginMailRecord(tx: DbTx): Promise<void> {
  await tx.execute(sql`select set_config('lock_timeout', ${`${MAIL_LOCK_TIMEOUT_MS}ms`}::text, true)`);
}

/**
 * Whether a later decision lifted the decision's suspension or termination, or a reversal broke its basis (3e's review,
 * proofs1): its statement, still owed, is then never sent. A statement of its own, read after the decision's row is held.
 */
export async function standingWithdrawn(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ withdrawn: boolean }>(
    tx,
    sql`select exists (select 1 from decision_actions a
                        where a.decision_id = ${decisionId}::uuid and a.kind::text in ('suspend', 'terminate')
                          and (exists (select 1 from decision_actions r where r.reverses_action_id = a.id) or public.standing_basis_broken_at(a.id) is not null)) as withdrawn`,
  );
  return row?.withdrawn === true;
}

/** Takes a decision's row while its statement's mail is still owed; false, and nothing is taken, when it is not. */
export async function lockPendingAuthorMail(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from decisions where id = ${decisionId}::uuid and author_mail = 'pending' for no key update`)).length > 0;
}

/** Takes a notice's row while its receipt is still owed (pending, or, with `folded`, folded into an update); false when it is not. */
export async function lockPendingReceipt(tx: DbTx, intakeId: string, folded = false): Promise<boolean> {
  const states = folded ? sql`receipt in ('pending', 'folded')` : sql`receipt = 'pending'`;
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from intakes where id = ${intakeId}::uuid and ${states} for no key update`)).length > 0;
}

/** Takes, in one id order, the rows of these items whose outcome mail is still owed, and answers their ids. */
export async function lockPendingOutcomeLines(tx: DbTx, itemIds: readonly string[]): Promise<Set<string>> {
  if (itemIds.length === 0) return new Set();
  const locked = await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`select id from intake_items where id = any(${uuids(itemIds)}) and outcome_mail = 'pending' order by id for no key update`);
  return new Set(locked.map((row) => row.id));
}

export async function recordAuthorMail(q: Runner, decisionId: string, state: MailState): Promise<boolean> {
  const updated = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`update decisions set author_mail = ${state}::delivery_state, author_mail_at = case when ${state}::text = 'sent' then now() else author_mail_at end
         where id = ${decisionId}::uuid and author_mail = 'pending' returning id`,
  );
  return updated.length > 0;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- the dispatch job

/** A time as a timestamptz parameter. */
const at = (time: Date) => sql`${time.toISOString()}::timestamptz`;

/** The notices whose receipt is still pending and that were received before `before`, oldest first, at most `limit`. */
export async function pendingReceipts(q: Runner, before: Date, limit: number): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select id from intakes where receipt = 'pending' and received_at < ${at(before)} order by received_at, id limit ${limit}::int`)).map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The decisions whose statement mail is still pending and that were decided before `before`, oldest first. The decision caps bound how many there can be. */
export async function pendingAuthorMails(q: Runner, before: Date): Promise<string[]> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select id from decisions where author_mail = 'pending' and decided_at < ${at(before)} order by decided_at, id`)).map((row) => row.id);
}

/**
 * The daily release, through the database's one function for it: every item answered before the cut-off is released with
 * its outcome as of the cut-off, and every released item whose outcome a review or a correction changed before it gets
 * its new outcome. The function refuses a cut-off in the database's future; a cut-off its clock has not reached yet (the
 * API's clock running ahead of it) is therefore taken as now. Answers how many items it changed.
 */
export async function releaseOutcomes(q: Runner, cutoff: Date): Promise<number> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ n: number }>(q, sql`select public.release_outcomes(least(${at(cutoff)}, now())) as n`);
  return row!.n;
}

/**
 * The contacts whose notice is still owed something: an item unanswered (a re-examination included), an item's outcome
 * mail pending or a changed outcome waiting for its release, or its receipt pending or folded. A line or a receipt that
 * was given up is owed nothing more.
 */
export async function contactsOwed(q: Runner): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ contact_id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select distinct n.contact_id from intakes n
         where n.contact_id is not null
           and (n.receipt in ('pending', 'folded')
                or exists (select 1 from intake_items i where i.intake_id = n.id and (i.outcome is null or i.outcome_mail = 'pending' or i.revision_pending_at is not null)))`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.contact_id);
}

/** One released item whose outcome mail is pending, with what its line's words follow from. */
export interface OutcomeLineRow {
  id: string;
  intakeId: string;
  ref: string;
  contactId: string | null;
  reporterId: string | null;
  position: number;
  targetType: TargetType;
  targetId: string;
  namedHandle: string | null;
  hasCase: boolean;
  suspect: boolean;
  shownOutcome: string;
  changed: boolean;
  reexamines: boolean;
  /** A decision answered it: a link that named nothing was answered without one. */
  byDecision: boolean;
  reexamined: boolean;
  ruleId: string | null;
  rulesVersion: number | null;
  decisionUnseen: boolean;
  /** The answering decision holds a seal. */
  sealed: boolean;
  /** 3e: the answering decision retires the handle of the account the item is about. */
  retired: boolean;
  /** 3e: the answering decision suspends or terminates that account. */
  measure: boolean;
  /** Every measure of the answering decision changed nothing when it was imposed. */
  noEffect: boolean;
  /** 3d Task 7: the answering decision is recorded as partly automated; absent reads false. */
  partly?: boolean;
  /** For an item about a post: the post quotes another. */
  quotes: boolean;
}

/** Every released item whose outcome mail is still pending, whichever round released it, by notice and position. */
export async function pendingOutcomeLines(q: Runner): Promise<OutcomeLineRow[]> {
  const found = await rows<Record<string, unknown>>(
    q,
    sql`select i.id, i.intake_id, n.ref, n.contact_id, i.reporter_account_id, i.position, i.target_type, i.target_id, i.named_handle, i.case_id is not null as has_case, i.suspect,
               i.shown_outcome, i.revised_sent_at is not null as changed, i.reexamines_item_id is not null as reexamines, i.answered_by is not null as by_decision,
               exists (select 1 from intake_items r where r.reexamines_item_id = i.id) as reexamined,
               d.rule_id, d.rules_version, coalesce(d.unseen, false) as decision_unseen,
               exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = i.answered_by and a.kind = 'seal_media') as sealed,
               exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = i.answered_by and a.kind = 'retire_handle') as retired,
               exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = i.answered_by and a.kind in ('suspend', 'terminate')) as measure,
               ${answerChangedNothing} as no_effect, coalesce(d.automated_decision = 'partially', false) as partly,
               coalesce((select p.quote_of_id is not null from posts p where i.target_type = 'post' and p.id = i.target_id), false) as quotes
          from intake_items i join intakes n on n.id = i.intake_id left join decisions d on d.id = i.answered_by
         where i.outcome_sent_at is not null and i.outcome_mail = 'pending' and i.shown_outcome is not null
         order by n.received_at, n.id, i.position, i.created_at, i.id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({
    id: row.id as string,
    intakeId: row.intake_id as string,
    ref: row.ref as string,
    contactId: row.contact_id as string | null,
    reporterId: row.reporter_account_id as string | null,
    position: row.position as number,
    targetType: row.target_type as TargetType,
    targetId: row.target_id as string,
    namedHandle: row.named_handle as string | null,
    hasCase: row.has_case as boolean,
    suspect: row.suspect as boolean,
    shownOutcome: row.shown_outcome as string,
    changed: row.changed as boolean,
    reexamines: row.reexamines as boolean,
    byDecision: row.by_decision as boolean,
    reexamined: row.reexamined as boolean,
    ruleId: row.rule_id as string | null,
    rulesVersion: row.rules_version as number | null,
    decisionUnseen: row.decision_unseen as boolean,
    sealed: row.sealed as boolean,
    retired: row.retired as boolean,
    measure: row.measure as boolean,
    noEffect: row.no_effect as boolean,
    partly: row.partly as boolean,
    quotes: row.quotes as boolean,
  }));
}

/** The notices of signed-out notifiers whose receipt the 24-hour cap folded: each rides in its address's next update. */
export async function foldedReceipts(q: Runner): Promise<NoticeRow[]> {
  const found = await rows<NoticeColumns>(q, sql`select ${noticeColumns} from intakes where receipt = 'folded' and contact_id is not null order by received_at, id`);
  return found.flatMap((row) => noticeOf(row) ?? []);
}

/** Records what became of these items' outcome mails, only where one is still pending. */
export async function recordOutcomeMails(q: Runner, itemIds: readonly string[], state: MailState): Promise<void> {
  if (itemIds.length === 0) return;
  await q.execute(sql`update intake_items set outcome_mail = ${state}::delivery_state where id = any(${uuids(itemIds)}) and outcome_mail = 'pending'`);
}

/** Records what became of a receipt that rode in an update, only while it is still pending or folded. */
export async function recordCarriedReceipt(q: Runner, intakeId: string, state: MailState): Promise<void> {
  await q.execute(
    sql`update intakes set receipt = ${state}::delivery_state, receipt_sent_at = case when ${state}::text = 'sent' then now() else receipt_sent_at end
         where id = ${intakeId}::uuid and receipt in ('pending', 'folded')`,
  );
}

/** A decision that holds an announced suspension or termination, as a condition on decision `d`. */
const HOLDS_ANNOUNCED = sql`exists (select 1 from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind::text in ('suspend', 'terminate') and a.announced)`;

/**
 * The receipts and the statement mails still unsent `days` days after they were due, recorded as given up; answers their
 * ids. 3e (design, section 7.14 item 3): the statement mail of a decision that holds an announced measure is left out:
 * its outcome fixes the measure's start, so each is given up alone, under its subject's profile lock (giveUpAnnouncedMail).
 */
export async function giveUpReceiptsAndAuthorMails(q: Runner, now: Date, days: number): Promise<{ receipts: string[]; authorMails: string[] }> {
  const due = sql`${at(now)} - make_interval(days => ${days}::int)`;
  const receipts = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`update intakes set receipt = 'failed' where receipt in ('pending', 'folded') and received_at < ${due} returning id`);
  // 3f: a mail is owed from the time it became owed, which for a notice released after a hold is its informed_at, and for
  // the mail that an order's notice grew the newest record of the authority's words: never from the decision's own time,
  // which may be weeks before.
  const owedSince = sql.raw(`greatest(d.decided_at, coalesce(d.informed_at, d.decided_at),
      coalesce((select max(e.at) from public.legal_order_items i join public.legal_order_events e on e.order_id = i.order_id and e.kind = 'texts_recorded'
                 where i.id = d.order_item_id), d.decided_at))`);
  const authorMails = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`update decisions d set author_mail = 'failed' where d.author_mail = 'pending' and ${owedSince} < ${due} and not ${HOLDS_ANNOUNCED} returning d.id`);
  return { receipts: receipts.map((row) => row.id), authorMails: authorMails.map((row) => row.id) };
}

/** The statement mails of decisions that hold an announced measure, still unsent `days` days after the decision, with each decision's subject: each is given up alone. */
export async function announcedMailsDue(q: Runner, now: Date, days: number): Promise<{ decisionId: string; subjectId: string }[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string; subject: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select d.id, (select a.subject_account_id from decision_actions a where a.decision_id = d.id and a.kind::text in ('suspend', 'terminate')) as subject
          from decisions d where d.author_mail = 'pending' and d.decided_at < ${at(now)} - make_interval(days => ${days}::int) and ${HOLDS_ANNOUNCED}
         order by d.decided_at, d.id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({ decisionId: row.id, subjectId: row.subject }));
}

/**
 * Gives up one announced measure's statement mail, in a transaction whose caller took the subject's profile row first
 * (the lock order, item 4): the decision's row is updated only while its mail is still pending, and the database stamps
 * the time and fixes the start from it (decisions_mail_forward, decisions_mail_standing). True when this call gave it up.
 */
export async function giveUpAnnouncedMail(tx: DbTx, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await rows<{ id: string }>(tx, sql`update decisions set author_mail = 'failed' where id = ${decisionId}::uuid and author_mail = 'pending' returning id`)).length > 0;
}

/** The outcome lines still unsent `days` days after their release, or after the release of their changed outcome, recorded as given up; answers their ids. */
export async function giveUpOutcomeMails(q: Runner, now: Date, days: number): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`update intake_items set outcome_mail = 'failed'
         where outcome_mail = 'pending' and coalesce(revised_sent_at, outcome_sent_at) < ${at(now)} - make_interval(days => ${days}::int) returning id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** An unanswered item in the urgent lane that has waited long enough to be alerted about again, with what decides whether it still calls for someone. */
export interface UrgentItemRow {
  caseId: string;
  targetType: TargetType;
  targetId: string;
  suspect: boolean;
  /** When the item arrived, in epoch milliseconds. */
  arrivedMs: number;
  /** Whether a decision taken while deciding, a note, or a recorded choice not to seal came after the item arrived. */
  interimAfter: boolean;
  noteAfter: boolean;
  declinedAfter: boolean;
  /** When the newest recorded choice not to seal of the case was saved, in epoch milliseconds, to the millisecond. */
  newestDeclinedMs: number | null;
  /** A post case's post is not visible: withheld, removed, or deleted by its author. */
  postHidden: boolean;
}

/**
 * The unanswered items of open cases in the urgent lane that arrived before `before`, the cases that have waited longest
 * first and each case's items together. "After the item arrived" compares the item's time with the decision's or the
 * text's, as the view of measures in force does: no later than.
 */
export async function urgentItems(q: Runner, before: Date): Promise<UrgentItemRow[]> {
  const after = (kind: string) => sql.raw(`exists (select 1 from staff_texts t where t.case_id = c.id and t.kind = '${kind}' and t.created_at >= i.created_at)`);
  const found = await rows<Record<string, unknown>>(
    q,
    sql`select c.id as case_id, c.target_type, c.target_id, i.suspect,
               floor(extract(epoch from i.created_at) * 1000)::float8 as arrived_ms,
               exists (select 1 from decisions d where d.case_id = c.id and d.kind = 'interim' and d.decided_at >= i.created_at) as interim_after,
               ${after("note")} as note_after, ${after("seal_declined")} as declined_after,
               (select floor(extract(epoch from max(t.created_at)) * 1000)::float8 from staff_texts t where t.case_id = c.id and t.kind = 'seal_declined') as newest_declined_ms,
               coalesce((select p.state <> 'visible' from posts p where c.target_type = 'post' and p.id = c.target_id), false) as post_hidden
          from intake_items i join cases c on c.id = i.case_id
         where c.closed_at is null and i.lane = 0 and i.outcome is null and i.created_at < ${at(before)}
         order by c.oldest_open_at, c.id, i.seq`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => ({
    caseId: row.case_id as string,
    targetType: row.target_type as TargetType,
    targetId: row.target_id as string,
    suspect: row.suspect as boolean,
    arrivedMs: Number(row.arrived_ms),
    interimAfter: row.interim_after as boolean,
    noteAfter: row.note_after as boolean,
    declinedAfter: row.declined_after as boolean,
    newestDeclinedMs: row.newest_declined_ms === null ? null : Number(row.newest_declined_ms),
    postHidden: row.post_hidden as boolean,
  }));
}

/**
 * The cases past their lane's response time (24 hours in lanes 0 and 1, seven days in lane 2, counted from the oldest
 * unanswered item), per lane with the oldest one's time, and the open cases that have held a measure taken while
 * deciding for more than 24 hours, whatever their lane.
 */
export async function waitingCases(q: Runner, now: Date): Promise<{ lanes: { lane: Lane; count: number; oldest: Date }[]; interim: number; replies: { count: number; oldest: Date } | null }> {
  const found = await rows<{ lane: Lane; n: number; oldest: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select lane, count(*)::int as n, ${iso("min(oldest_open_at)")} as oldest from cases
         where closed_at is null and oldest_open_at < ${at(now)} - case when lane = 2 then interval '7 days' else interval '24 hours' end
         group by lane order by lane`,
  );
  const [held] = await rows<{ n: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(distinct m.case_id)::int as n from measures_in_force m join decisions d on d.id = m.decision_id join cases c on c.id = m.case_id
         where m.decision_kind = 'interim' and c.closed_at is null and d.decided_at < ${at(now)} - interval '24 hours'`,
  );
  // 3e (design, section 7.14): the replies to a suspension or a termination that no decision answered for longer than
  // korbat's aim, with the oldest one's time.
  const [replies] = await rows<{ n: number; oldest: string | null }>(
    q,
    sql`select count(*)::int as n, ${iso("min(r.filed_at)")} as oldest from suspension_replies r
         where r.answered_by is null and r.filed_at < ${at(now)} - make_interval(hours => ${REPLY_AIM_HOURS}::int)`,
  );
  return {
    lanes: found.map((row) => ({ lane: row.lane, count: row.n, oldest: new Date(row.oldest) })),
    interim: held!.n,
    replies: replies!.n > 0 && replies!.oldest !== null ? { count: replies!.n, oldest: new Date(replies!.oldest) } : null,
  };
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------- retention

/**
 * The SQL of the retention job and of the overview's late erasures (3c design, sections 6.4, 7.3 and 7.9). Every time is
 * the database's own: each erase function checks its due rule against the database's now(), so the job asks with the same
 * clock, and one clock decides what is due. The periods are the contracts' RETENTION, handed over as numbers.
 *
 * The candidates are read from the partial indexes that hold only what is left to erase, so a round's work follows what
 * is left, never every case ever closed. The freeze is read here only to keep a case that holds nothing but snapshots of
 * a frozen post out of the candidates: for every snapshot the one function that erases one decides.
 */

/** The cases that hold a row erase_case_evidence would change: an unerased snapshot that is not of a frozen post, an unerased note or draft, an appeal statement, or an unreleased hold. */
const CANDIDATE_CASES = sql`
  select s.case_id from evidence_snapshots s where s.erased_at is null and not (s.target_type = 'post' and public.post_frozen(s.target_id))
  union select t.case_id from staff_texts t where t.confirmed_at is null and t.erased_at is null
  union select d.case_id from appeals a join decisions d on d.id = a.decision_id where a.statement is not null
  union select h.case_id from media_holds h where h.released_at is null`;

/** A final decision citing R4 that is not redacted yet and one of whose R4 measures is in force, as `d`. */
const REDACTABLE = sql`d.kind = 'final' and d.rule_id = 'R4' and d.redacted_at is null
  and exists (select 1 from measures_in_force m where m.decision_id = d.id and m.kind in ('remove', 'remove_media', 'reset_bio', 'reset_display_name'))`;

/** A decision one of whose statement texts is unerased, as `d`, joined to the profile `p` of its case's subject. */
const STATEMENT_HELD = sql`from decisions d
  join cases c on c.id = d.case_id
  join profiles p on p.id = case when c.target_type = 'account' then c.target_id else (select x.author_id from posts x where x.id = c.target_id) end
  where exists (select 1 from staff_texts t where t.digest in (d.facts_digest, d.reason_digest, d.legal_reference_digest) and t.erased_at is null)`;

/** The candidate cases whose evidence is due now, in id order. */
export async function dueCases(q: Runner): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select k.case_id as id from (${CANDIDATE_CASES}) k where public.case_evidence_due_at(k.case_id) <= now() order by 1`);
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The unerased intakes whose record is due now. None is due before `days` days after it was received, which the index is read by. */
export async function dueIntakes(q: Runner, days: number): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(
    q,
    sql`select n.id from intakes n where n.erased_at is null and n.received_at <= now() - make_interval(days => ${days}::int) and public.intake_due_at(n.id) <= now() order by n.received_at, n.id`,
  );
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The R4 decisions that are final for their author and not redacted yet. The redaction itself answers false for one whose post is frozen. */
export async function dueRedactions(q: Runner): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select d.id from decisions d where ${REDACTABLE} and public.decision_final_at(d.id) <= now() order by d.decided_at, d.id`);
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

/** The decisions that still hold a statement text and whose subject's profile was deleted at least `months` months ago. */
export async function dueStatements(q: Runner, months: number): Promise<string[]> {
  const found = await rows<{ id: string }>(q, sql`select d.id ${STATEMENT_HELD} and p.deleted_at <= now() - make_interval(months => ${months}::int) order by d.decided_at, d.id`);
  return found.map((row) => row.id);
}

const changedBy = async (q: Runner, call: ReturnType<typeof sql>): Promise<number> => (await rows<{ n: number }>(q, sql`select ${call} as n`))[0]!.n;

/** Deletes the drafts nobody confirmed that are older than `hours` hours; never a note, a recorded choice not to seal or a confirmed text. */
export const sweepStaffTexts = (q: Runner, hours: number) => changedBy(q, sql`public.sweep_staff_texts(now() - make_interval(hours => ${hours}::int))`);
/** Erases a due case's snapshots (never one of a frozen post), notes, drafts and appeal statements, and releases its holds. */
export const eraseCaseEvidence = (q: Runner, caseId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_case_evidence(${caseId}::uuid)`);
/** Erases a due intake's record: its explanation, its cited law, who sent it and its re-examinations' statements. */
export const eraseIntake = (q: Runner, intakeId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_intake(${intakeId}::uuid)`);
/** Erases the statement texts of a decision whose subject's account has been deleted for 12 months. */
export const eraseStatementTexts = (q: Runner, decisionId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_statement_texts(${decisionId}::uuid)`);
/** Deletes the access rows older than `months` months, erasing first the reveal reasons they name. */
export const deleteAccessLog = (q: Runner, months: number) => changedBy(q, sql`public.delete_access_log(now() - make_interval(months => ${months}::int))`);
/** Forgets that a deleted account sent its reports; 0 for an account whose auth row is not marked deleted. */
export const forgetReporter = (q: Runner, accountId: string) => changedBy(q, sql`public.forget_reporter(${accountId}::uuid)`);
/**
 * 3e: erases the text of every reply to a suspension or a termination that is answered and whose decision is final for
 * its author, keeping its digest and its row; an unanswered reply keeps its text however old. Answers how many it erased.
 */
export const eraseReplyStatements = (q: Runner) => changedBy(q, sql`public.erase_reply_statements()`);
/** 3e: deletes the marks and the tallies of reports sent on a UTC day before the frame of the reporting counts; answers how many rows. */
export const forgetReportCounts = (q: Runner) => changedBy(q, sql`public.forget_report_counts()`);

/** Makes an R4 restriction's erasure final; false when it changed nothing (its post is frozen, or another round was faster). */
export async function redactR4(q: Runner, decisionId: string): Promise<boolean> {
  return (await rows<{ done: boolean }>(q, sql`select public.redact_r4_body(${decisionId}::uuid) as done`))[0]!.done;
}

/** The overview's late erasures that this module's tables answer: what each step should have changed more than a day ago. */
export interface LateErasures {
  caseEvidence: number;
  intakeRecords: number;
  statements: number;
  redactions: number;
  drafts: number;
  accessLog: number;
}

/**
 * How much each due rule is late by more than a day. A case that holds only snapshots of a frozen post is no candidate
 * and never counted, and a redaction whose post is frozen would change nothing now, so it is not counted either: both
 * wait for an admin's answer, not for the job.
 */
export async function lateErasures(q: Runner, periods: { intakeDays: number; statementMonths: number; draftHours: number; accessLogMonths: number }): Promise<LateErasures> {
  const [row] = await rows<{ case_evidence: number; intake_records: number; statements: number; redactions: number; drafts: number; access_log: number }>(
    q,
    sql`select
      (select count(*)::int from (${CANDIDATE_CASES}) k where public.case_evidence_due_at(k.case_id) < now() - interval '1 day') as case_evidence,
      (select count(*)::int from intakes n
        where n.erased_at is null and n.received_at <= now() - make_interval(days => ${periods.intakeDays}::int) and public.intake_due_at(n.id) < now() - interval '1 day') as intake_records,
      (select count(*)::int ${STATEMENT_HELD} and p.deleted_at < now() - make_interval(months => ${periods.statementMonths}::int) - interval '1 day') as statements,
      (select count(*)::int from decisions d join cases c on c.id = d.case_id
        where ${REDACTABLE} and public.decision_final_at(d.id) < now() - interval '1 day'
          and not (c.target_type = 'post' and public.post_frozen(c.target_id))) as redactions,
      (select count(*)::int from staff_texts t
        where t.kind not in ('note', 'seal_declined') and t.confirmed_at is null and t.created_at < now() - make_interval(hours => ${periods.draftHours}::int) - interval '1 day') as drafts,
      (select count(*)::int from case_access_log l where l.at < now() - make_interval(months => ${periods.accessLogMonths}::int) - interval '1 day') as access_log`,
  );
  return { caseEvidence: row!.case_evidence, intakeRecords: row!.intake_records, statements: row!.statements, redactions: row!.redactions, drafts: row!.drafts, accessLog: row!.access_log };
}

 * erases the evidence of the cases and the records of the intakes that are due, makes R4 redactions final, erases the
 * statements of accounts deleted for 12 months, erases the texts of replies to suspensions that are answered and final
 * and forgets the reporting counts of the days before their frame (3e design, section 7.14), deletes the old access rows,
 * and deletes the image rows that a case or a freeze kept and nothing retains any more. 3f adds three steps before the
 * disposal (design, sections 6.4, 7.11 and 7.18): the end of each order's preservation that is due, which erases the
 * post's content while the order's measure stands; the records of orders three years after their last event; and the
 * contact point's messages 30 days after they were handled, with the outbox rows that old; Task 5 the records to
 * authorities, and Task 6 the restore gaps closed as not needed or imported 12 months ago, with the copy marks that old
 * but the newest (sections 6.6 and 7.18). 3d Task 8 adds three more before the disposal (design, sections 6.8, 6.10 and
 * 7.14): automation_records, the erasure of match records with their refusals' account and objection, of requests for a
 * person with their decision's texts, and of signals; edge_purges, the edge's outbox rows done EDGE_RULES.keepDays ago; and
 * tools_off, the forgetting of the hashes and the ratings a tool that is off left behind.
 *
 * MODERATION_RETENTION=off holds every step but tools_off, which is held by nothing but its tool's setting: forgetting
 * what a tool that is off left behind never takes evidence or a record a restore must keep, and the rules page and the
 * terms say of a tool that is off that korbat keeps nothing of it. So the job runs while the switch is off as well, and
 * its round then runs tools_off alone.
 *
 * The job only names what it believes is due. Each erase function of migration 0018 checks its own rule again, against
 * values the API role cannot set, and the two gates of the freeze decide for every snapshot and every image row: so a
 * wrong candidate, or an API that asks early, erases nothing.
 *

 * changed something and writes nothing when it did not. A row that raises is rolled back alone, logged with the step and
 * the row's id, and tried again at the next round: a case that keeps failing never stops another case's erasure. No log
 * line carries an address, a handle or an account id.

const MINUTE_MS = 60_000;

/** The job's name: its lock is `job:moderation-retention`, and its log lines carry it. */
export const RETENTION_JOB = "moderation-retention";
/** The time between the end of one round and the start of the next. */
export const RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS = 10 * MINUTE_MS;
/** The audit action of every step that changed something. It is written by the server itself, never under a step-up. */
export const RETENTION_ACTION = "moderation_retention";
/** What the API logs at every start while the job is switched off, which the README's restore steps do for a restore window. */

/** The steps, by the name their audit rows and log lines carry. */
export type RetentionStep =
  | "drafts"
  | "case_evidence"
  | "intake_record"
  | "redaction"
  | "statements"
  | "reply_statements"
  | "report_counts"
  | "access_log"
  | "order_preservation"
  | "order_records"
  | "contact_messages"
  | "authority_records"
  | "restore_gaps"
  | "automation_records"
  | "edge_purges"
  | "tools_off"
  | "images";

/** What one round did, for its log line and for the tests: counts only. */
export interface RetentionReport {
  /** The drafts deleted. */

  /** The cases whose evidence was erased, the intakes whose record was, the R4 decisions redacted and the decisions whose statements were erased. */
  cases: number;
  intakes: number;
  redactions: number;
  statements: number;
  /** 3e: the replies whose text was erased, and the marks and daily tallies of reporting deleted with their frame. */
  replies: number;
  reportCounts: number;
  /** 3f: the preservations ended (with or without an erasure), the orders whose records were erased, and the rows of messages and outbox deleted. */
  preservations: number;
  orderRecords: number;
  contactMessages: number;
  /** 3f Task 5: the rows of the records to authorities deleted (notification records, productions and released holds). */
  authorityRecords: number;
  /** 3f Task 6: the restore gaps closed as not needed or imported, and the copy marks but the newest, deleted 12 months on. */
  restoreGaps: number;
  /** The access rows deleted, with the reveal reasons erased before them. */
  accessLog: number;
  /**
   * 3d Task 8: the rows erase_automation_records changed (match records erased, refusals that lost their account and
   * objection, objections erased, signals deleted), the edge's outbox rows deleted, and the hashes and ratings forgotten
   * while their tool is off.
   */
  automationRecords: number;
  edgePurges: number;
  toolsOff: number;
  /** The size of each batch of image rows the disposal deleted, in order; the last one is smaller than a full batch. */
  batches: number[];
  /** The steps and rows that raised and were left for the next round. */
  failed: number;
}

/** The ids a step's audit row names; each is null where the step has none. */
interface StepIds {
  caseId?: string;
  intakeId?: string;
  decisionId?: string;
  /** 3f: an order's item and order, and whether the end of the item's preservation erased its post's content. */
  itemId?: string;
  orderId?: string;
  erased?: boolean;
  /** 3f's review (proofs3): the erased order's kind, receipt and opening as they stood, which tco-counts reads. */

}

/**
 * One step, or one row of a step, in a transaction of its own: the change, then its audit row as the transaction's last
 * statement, since the insert holds the chain's head until the commit. A change of nothing writes nothing. A lock is
 * waited on for at most ten seconds, so a transaction left open elsewhere costs this row a round, never the job.
 */
async function inStep(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb">, step: RetentionStep, ids: StepIds, change: (tx: DbTx) => Promise<number>): Promise<number> {
  return deps.apiDb.transaction(async (tx) => {
    await tx.execute(sql`set local lock_timeout = '10s'`);
    const count = await change(tx);
    if (count > 0) {
      await appendAuditRow(tx, {
        actorId: SYSTEM_ACTOR_ID,
        action: RETENTION_ACTION,
        targetType: null,
        targetId: null,
        requestId: null,
        // Ids and counts only, never a text. 3f's steps add their own ids, and only they, so the rows of 3c's and 3e's keep their form.
        metadata: {
          step,
          caseId: ids.caseId ?? null,
          intakeId: ids.intakeId ?? null,
          decisionId: ids.decisionId ?? null,
          ...(ids.itemId !== undefined ? { itemId: ids.itemId, erased: ids.erased ?? false } : {}),
          ...(ids.orderId !== undefined ? { orderId: ids.orderId } : {}),
          ...(ids.order !== undefined ? { kind: ids.order.kind, receivedAt: ids.order.receivedAt, openedAt: ids.order.openedAt } : {}),
          count,
        },
      });
    }
    return count;
  });
}

/**
 * The disposal: the one deleter of image rows that a case or a freeze kept, in batches. Each batch is a transaction of
 * its own with its audit row, and its files are requested right after its commit and before the next batch. They are
 * never requested before the commit: a disposable row is not disposable for good (a report may freeze a deleted post's
 * images at any moment), so a batch rolled back after its request would lose the files of rows a freeze then keeps.
 *
 * No row goes unless its files can be found again. The media module notes inside the batch's transaction that the files
 * are owed (a batch whose note cannot be written does not commit), and the request is written from that note when this
 * process stops between the commit and the request, or when the request fails. A failed request ends the step for the
 * round, and every round begins by asking again for what is still owed, by this job or by the account's purge: while
 * that cannot be written no batch is taken, so a volume that takes no requests costs one batch's wait and never a second
 * batch's rows. The failure is logged with the step; what is owed is counted among the overview's late erasures.
 */
async function dispose(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log">, report: RetentionReport): Promise<void> {
  const owed = await deps.media.requestOwed();
  if (owed > 0) {
    report.failed++;
    deps.log.error({ job: RETENTION_JOB, step: "images", owed }, "moderation-retention: files of image rows that are gone are still owed a request; no batch is taken until they can be asked for");
    return;
  }
  for (;;) {
    let ids: string[] = [];
    await inStep(deps, "images", {}, async (tx) => {
      ids = await deps.media.dropDisposable(tx);

/** The three settings a round reads: whether retention is on, and whether each tool is off. */
export type RetentionSettings = Pick<Config, "MODERATION_RETENTION" | "MEDIA_MATCH" | "R1_CLASSIFIER">;

/**
 * One round. A plain function, so the tests call it directly. With `config`, as the job runs it, MODERATION_RETENTION=off
 * holds every step but tools_off, which forgets the hashes while MEDIA_MATCH is off and the ratings while R1_CLASSIFIER is
 * off. Without it, as the tests of the other steps call it, every step but tools_off runs: no tool is known to be off.
 */
export async function retentionRound(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log"> & { config?: RetentionSettings }): Promise<RetentionReport> {
  const report: RetentionReport = {
    drafts: 0,
    cases: 0,
    intakes: 0,
    redactions: 0,
    statements: 0,
    replies: 0,
    reportCounts: 0,
    preservations: 0,
    orderRecords: 0,
    contactMessages: 0,
    authorityRecords: 0,
    restoreGaps: 0,
    accessLog: 0,
    automationRecords: 0,
    edgePurges: 0,
    toolsOff: 0,
    batches: [],
    failed: 0,
  };
  /** A step in a try of its own: what it raises is logged with the step, and the round goes on. */
  const step = async (name: RetentionStep, run: () => Promise<void>) => {
    try {
      await run();
    } catch (err) {
      report.failed++;
      deps.log.error({ err, job: RETENTION_JOB, step: name }, "moderation-retention: a step failed; the round goes on");
    }
  };
  /** Each row of a step in a try of its own, under the row's id; the change may add to what its audit row names. */
  const each = async (name: RetentionStep, key: "caseId" | "intakeId" | "decisionId" | "orderId", ids: readonly string[], change: (tx: DbTx, id: string, named: StepIds) => Promise<number>): Promise<number> => {
    let done = 0;
    for (const id of ids) {
      try {
        const named: StepIds = { [key]: id };
        if ((await inStep(deps, name, named, (tx) => change(tx, id, named))) > 0) done++;
      } catch (err) {
        report.failed++;
        deps.log.error({ err, job: RETENTION_JOB, step: name, [key]: id }, "moderation-retention: a row failed and was left as it was; the round goes on");
      }
    }
    return done;
  };
  /**
   * 3d Task 8 (7.14): the step tools_off, held by nothing but each tool's setting: one transaction for both statements,
   * with one audit row of the step and its count when it changed anything. Without a configuration no tool is known to be
   * off, and it does nothing.
   */
  const toolsOff = async () => {
    if (deps.config === undefined) return;
    const { MEDIA_MATCH, R1_CLASSIFIER } = deps.config;
    await step("tools_off", async () => {
      report.toolsOff = await inStep(deps, "tools_off", {}, async (tx) => (MEDIA_MATCH === "off" ? await deps.media.forgetHashes(tx) : 0) + (R1_CLASSIFIER === "off" ? await deps.media.forgetScores(tx) : 0));
    });
  };
  /** One line for a round that did something or failed somewhere: counts only. */
  const logRound = () => {
    const images = report.batches.reduce((sum, size) => sum + size, 0);
    const orders = report.preservations + report.orderRecords + report.contactMessages + report.authorityRecords + report.restoreGaps;
    const automation = report.automationRecords + report.edgePurges + report.toolsOff;
    if (report.drafts + report.cases + report.intakes + report.redactions + report.statements + report.replies + report.reportCounts + orders + automation + report.accessLog + images + report.failed > 0) {
      deps.log.info({ job: RETENTION_JOB, ...report, images }, "moderation-retention: round");
    }
  };

  // MODERATION_RETENTION=off, in the job's configuration: tools_off alone.
  if (deps.config !== undefined && deps.config.MODERATION_RETENTION !== "on") {
    await toolsOff();
    logRound();
    return report;

  await step("drafts", async () => {
    report.drafts = await inStep(deps, "drafts", {}, (tx) => sweepStaffTexts(tx, RETENTION.draftHours));
  });
  await step("case_evidence", async () => {
    report.cases = await each("case_evidence", "caseId", await dueCases(deps.apiDb), eraseCaseEvidence);
  });
  await step("intake_record", async () => {
    report.intakes = await each("intake_record", "intakeId", await dueIntakes(deps.apiDb, RETENTION.intakeDays), eraseIntake);
  });
  // The redaction answers false, and nothing is written, while its post is frozen: the next round asks again.
  await step("redaction", async () => {
    report.redactions = await each("redaction", "decisionId", await dueRedactions(deps.apiDb), async (tx, id) => ((await redactR4(tx, id)) ? 1 : 0));
  });
  await step("statements", async () => {
    report.statements = await each("statements", "decisionId", await dueStatements(deps.apiDb, RETENTION.statementMonths), eraseStatementTexts);
  });
  // 3e: each of the two is one call of its function, which checks its own rule against values the API role cannot set
  // (the reply's answer, the decision's finality, the frame of standing_rules()), so its audit row names no id.
  await step("reply_statements", async () => {
    report.replies = await inStep(deps, "reply_statements", {}, (tx) => eraseReplyStatements(tx));
  });
  await step("report_counts", async () => {
    report.reportCounts = await inStep(deps, "report_counts", {}, (tx) => forgetReportCounts(tx));
  });
  await step("access_log", async () => {
    report.accessLog = await inStep(deps, "access_log", {}, (tx) => deleteAccessLog(tx, RETENTION.accessLogMonths));
  });
  // 3f: each item whose preservation is due, in a transaction of its own. A post still frozen answers false and writes
  // nothing, so its item is named again at the next round, as an R4 redaction is; the erased image rows are then taken
  // by the disposal below, in this same round, and their files requested after its commit.
  await step("order_preservation", async () => {
    for (const id of await duePreservations(deps.apiDb)) {
      const ids: StepIds = { itemId: id };
      try {
        const ended = await inStep(deps, "order_preservation", ids, async (tx) => {
          const done = await endPreservation(tx, id);
          // Read by the audit row, which inStep writes after this change.
          ids.erased = done.erased;
          return done.ended ? 1 : 0;
        });
        if (ended > 0) report.preservations++;
      } catch (err) {
        report.failed++;
        deps.log.error({ err, job: RETENTION_JOB, step: "order_preservation", itemId: id }, "moderation-retention: a row failed and was left as it was; the round goes on");
      }
    }
  });
  await step("order_records", async () => {
    // Each order in a transaction of its own; its audit row counts the rows of its records deleted and (3f's review,
    // proofs3) names the order's kind and its receipt and opening as they stand when erased, read first in the same
    // transaction: tco-counts reads them to know whose year's figures the erasure took, since the opening's own row may
    // name another kind (a correction) or be missing (an order written again by restore-import).
    report.orderRecords = await each("order_records", "orderId", await dueOrderRecords(deps.apiDb), async (tx, id, named) => {
      const facts = await erasedOrderFacts(tx, id);
      if (facts !== null) named.order = facts;
      return eraseOrderRecords(tx, id);
    });
  });
  // One call, which checks its own period against the database's clock: its audit row names no id.
  await step("contact_messages", async () => {
    report.contactMessages = await inStep(deps, "contact_messages", {}, (tx) => deleteContactMessages(tx));
  });
  // 3f Task 5: one call, which checks its own rule (three years, a seal in force, an archive not destroyed, an authority's
  // "not to the person") and answers a count: its audit row names no id, and the API learns nothing of the records.
  await step("authority_records", async () => {
    report.authorityRecords = await inStep(deps, "authority_records", {}, (tx) => eraseAuthorityRecords(tx));
  });
  // 3f Task 6: one call, which checks its own period (gap_keep_months) against the database's clock and never deletes a
  // gap that a decision closed, whose statement reads the lost day from it: its audit row names no id.
  await step("restore_gaps", async () => {
    report.restoreGaps = await inStep(deps, "restore_gaps", {}, (tx) => deleteRestoreGaps(tx));
  });
  // 3d Task 8 (6.8, 7.14): one call, which checks its own periods (automation_rules().match_keep_days, 3c's schedule for a
  // statement's texts) against the database's clock and answers a count: its audit row names no id.
  await step("automation_records", async () => {
    report.automationRecords = await inStep(deps, "automation_records", {}, (tx) => eraseAutomationRecords(tx));
  });
  // 3d Task 8 (6.3, 7.14): the edge's outbox rows done EDGE_RULES.keepDays ago, through the media module, which owns them.
  await step("edge_purges", async () => {
    report.edgePurges = await inStep(deps, "edge_purges", {}, (tx) => deps.media.forgetPurges(tx));
  });
  await toolsOff();
  await step("images", () => dispose(deps, report));

  logRound();
  return report;
}

/**
 * The job: a round every ten minutes, counted from the end of the one before, on one API instance at a time. Its rounds
 * read the configuration: with MODERATION_RETENTION=off each runs tools_off alone.
 */
export function createRetentionJob(deps: Pick<ModerationDeps, "apiDb" | "media" | "log"> & { config?: RetentionSettings }, lock: JobLock) {
  return createJob({ name: RETENTION_JOB, intervalMs: RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS, lockTtlMs: RETENTION_INTERVAL_MS, lock, log: deps.log, run: () => retentionRound(deps) });
}
