```ts
  heldUploads: z.object({ open: Count, oldest: z.iso.datetime().nullable(), objected: Count, capped: Count }),
});
export type StaffOverview = z.infer<typeof StaffOverview>;

/**
 * 3d Task 7 (design, sections 8.6 and 10.3): the release block of a held upload ended as report, as on a seal without its
 * posts: the record upload-report opened (sent, its reference, the authority's assessment shown as what it is, when the
 * files were handed over), whether both of the image's files are in the quarantine by record, the leave that stands, and
 * whether the uploader's notice of a release taken now would be held; silence_days; and, once released, the release's
 * time, ground, the day after which no backup that is deleted on time holds the file, and whether its notice is held.
 */
export const UploadRelease = z.object({
  reported: z.boolean(),
  theirReference: z.string().max(400).nullable(),
  answer: z.enum(["not_illegal", "illegal", "no_assessment", "other"]).nullable(),
  answeredAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  handedOverAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  quarantined: z.boolean(),
  leave: ReleaseLeave.nullable(),
  tellHeld: z.boolean(),
  silenceDays: z.number().int().positive().nullable(),
  releasedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  basis: z.enum(RELEASE_BASES).nullable(),
  backupsClearAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  noticeHeld: z.boolean().nullable(),
});
export type UploadRelease = z.infer<typeof UploadRelease>;

/** How many held uploads one page of GET /api/staff/uploads lists. */
export const UPLOADS_PAGE_SIZE = 50;

/**
 * 3d Task 7 (design, sections 7.12 step 3, 8.6 and 10.3): one refusal on Held uploads, never an image, a hash, a file's
 * name or a handle: when it was refused; its match's record; `otherRefusals`, the one thing an admin is given about the
 * uploader, the count of the same uploader's other refusals whose hold has not ended or ended as report, never one ended
 * as no_report; whether the uploader's account still exists; the objection; its end, with `deletesAt` for an end as
 * no_report (the image row's hold_until, after which the sweeper deletes it); whether the record of a report is set; and
 * for an end as report the release block.
 */
export const HeldUpload = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  refusedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  match: MatchRecord,
  otherRefusals: Count,
  uploaderGone: z.boolean(),
  objection: z.string().nullable(),
  objectedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  endedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  endAs: z.enum(UPLOAD_ENDS).nullable(),
  endReason: z.enum(UPLOAD_END_REASONS).nullable(),
  deletesAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  reported: z.boolean(),
  quarantined: z.boolean(),
  release: UploadRelease.nullable(),
});
export type HeldUpload = z.infer<typeof HeldUpload>;

/**
 * GET /api/staff/uploads: the refusals whose hold has not ended, oldest first; then those ended as report and not
 * released; then those released or ended as no_report in the last DESTRUCTIVE_DAYS days, UPLOADS_PAGE_SIZE a page.
 */
export const UploadsPage = z.object({ uploads: z.array(HeldUpload).max(UPLOADS_PAGE_SIZE), nextCursor: z.string().nullable() });
export type UploadsPage = z.infer<typeof UploadsPage>;
export const UploadsQuery = z.object({ cursor: z.string().regex(/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{1,400}$/).optional() });
export type UploadsQuery = z.infer<typeof UploadsQuery>;

/**
 * 3f Task 6 (sections 7.17, 8.8 and 10.2): GET /api/staff/restore, what an import after a restore found lost, in the order
 * in which it is taken again. `importedAt` is the newest import's time, null when none ever ran (the console then hides
 * the screen's entry). `mayOpen` is true when no gap of the classes 1 to 3 is open, and `retentionMay` when none of the
 * classes 1 to 5 is. A gap: its class, when the lost row was written and its action, the case or the order (and the item)
 * it names when the restored database holds them, the lost decision's action kinds, and its closing. `holds` are the
 * orders whose notice the restored database holds back, with each one's end as imported, for [restore.holds]. No
 * metadata beyond these.
 */
export const RestoreGap = z.object({
  id: z.uuid(),
  class: z.enum(GAP_CLASSES),
  actedAt: z.iso.datetime(),
  action: z.string().min(1),
  caseId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  orderId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  itemId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  kinds: z.array(z.enum(ACTION_KINDS)),
  closedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  disposition: z.enum(GAP_DISPOSITIONS).nullable(),
  closedByDecisionId: z.uuid().nullable(),
  /** 3d Task 2 ([restore.sealAgain], 8.7): the gap's case is about a post that is released, so a seal taken again freezes nothing. */
  released: z.boolean().optional(),
  /**
   * 3d Task 7 ([restore.holdEnd], 8.7): a lost end of a held upload's hold, with the way it ended and whether the restored
   * database holds the refusal (an admin ends it again the same way) or not (only release-replay closes the gap).
   */
  hold: z.object({ endAs: z.enum(UPLOAD_ENDS), present: z.boolean() }).optional(),
});
export type RestoreGap = z.infer<typeof RestoreGap>;
/** How many gaps one read of After a restore lists at most: every open gap, then the newest import's closed ones. */
export const RESTORE_GAPS_MAX = 1000;
export const RestoreView = z.object({
  importedAt: z.iso.datetime().nullable(),
  mayOpen: z.boolean(),
  retentionMay: z.boolean(),
  gaps: z.array(RestoreGap).max(RESTORE_GAPS_MAX),
  holds: z.array(z.object({ orderId: z.uuid(), holdUntil: z.iso.datetime().nullable() })).max(OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX),
});
export type RestoreView = z.infer<typeof RestoreView>;

/** One of the Standing screen's lists: how many rows there are, and at most OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX of them. */
const StandingList = <T extends z.ZodType>(row: T) => z.object({ total: Count, items: z.array(row).max(OVERVIEW_LIST_MAX) });

/**
 * GET /api/staff/standing (3e design, sections 7.5, 7.12, 8.6 and 10.3): four lists, each newest first, read from the
 * ledger's views; people are handles, and no row names a reporter. None is a queue key and none is weighted.
 *   - `atThreeStrikes`: the accounts with the ladder's number of active strikes, one of them newer than the account's
 *     newest measure of the ladder that stands, and no suspension or termination that stands and has not ended: the
 *     newest strike's rule and day, the most days an announced suspension could take now, and whether a termination
 *     could be announced.
 *   - `reportingRecords`: the accounts whose rule reports hold marks "manifestly unfounded" (the restriction of
 *     reporting's task fills it; until then it is empty).
 *   - `noticesUndelivered`: the announced measures of live accounts whose notice mail was recorded `failed`, with the
 *     start that follows; never a deleted account's `no_address`.
 *   - `terminationsWaiting`: the terminations that stand, with the day each becomes final, or what holds it: a pending
 *     appeal, or an unanswered reply (`replyOnTime` true when the reply came before the start, so it has not started).
 */
export const StandingLists = z.object({
  atThreeStrikes: StandingList(
    z.object({ handle: z.string(), caseId: z.uuid().nullable(), activeStrikes: Count, ruleId: z.enum(RULE_IDS), newestOn: UtcDay, maxDays: z.number().int().min(STANDING_DAYS.min).max(STANDING_DAYS.max).nullable(), mayTerminate: z.boolean() }),
  ),
  reportingRecords: StandingList(z.object({ handle: z.string(), caseId: z.uuid().nullable(), reports: Count, unfounded: Count, warnedOn: UtcDay.nullable(), marksSince: Count.nullable() })),
  noticesUndelivered: StandingList(z.object({ handle: z.string(), caseId: z.uuid(), decidedOn: UtcDay, startsAt: z.iso.datetime() })),
  terminationsWaiting: StandingList(
    z.object({ handle: z.string(), caseId: z.uuid(), decidedOn: UtcDay, finalOn: UtcDay.nullable(), heldBy: z.enum(["appeal", "reply"]).nullable(), replyOnTime: z.boolean().nullable() }),
  ),
});
export type StandingLists = z.infer<typeof StandingLists>;
```

```ts
import { ORDER_NOTICE } from "./statement";
/**
 * The public rulebook. korbat restricts content when it breaks one of these rules, or when it is illegal under EU law or
 * the law of an EU country and korbat is told about it in a notice. Opinions are never a reason. Every decision cites one
 * of these rules or the law.
 *
 * The rulebook is versioned: a decision records the version it was made under, and its statement is always rendered with
 * that version's text, so an old statement reads exactly as it was sent whatever the rules say now.
 */
export type Automation =
  | "none"                 // report-driven, human decides
  | "withhold_for_review"  // automation may hide from others pending a human
  | "auto_remove"          // automation may remove (R2 only)
  // 3d (design, section 10.8, W.4): version 4's two values. A program's score may flag an image for a moderator and,
  // where the owner switched that on, withhold it until the moderator decides (R1); a match may seal a post's images until
  // an admin answers (R2). Versions 1 to 3 keep their values and render as sent.
  | "flag_or_withhold"
  | "seal_for_review";

export interface Rule {
  id: string;
  title: string;
  text: string;
  allowed: string[];
  notAllowed: string[];
  automation: Automation;
  /** Decided by an admin: every final decision under the rule, whether it acts or not. */
  seniorQueue: boolean;
}

/** Version 1: the six rules as they stood before moderation cases. Kept as it was, for the decisions made under it. */

  {

    text: "Images or text whose primary purpose is sexual arousal are not allowed. This includes nudity presented sexually, explicit sexual acts, and sexualised depictions of anyone. Images that score high on the automated check are hidden from others until a person reviews them; the author can always see their own post.",
    allowed: ["Medical or educational discussion of sexuality without explicit imagery", "Art with non-sexual nudity in a clearly artistic or historical context", "Frank discussion of sexual politics or policy"],
    notAllowed: ["Pornographic images or video", "Sexually explicit text posted for arousal", "Links whose preview is pornographic"],
    automation: "withhold_for_review",
    seniorQueue: false,
  },
  {
    id: "R2",

    text: "Any sexualised depiction of a minor is removed automatically on a hash match, the account is suspended, and the material is reported to the relevant authority. This is the only rule enforced without a human decision first. Appeals are reviewed by a senior moderator.",
    allowed: ["Reporting or discussing child safety issues without imagery", "News about arrests or legislation"],
    notAllowed: ["Any sexualised image of a minor, real or generated", "Links to such material", "Solicitation"],
    automation: "auto_remove",
    seniorQueue: true,
  },
  {

    title: "No targeted hatred or harassment based on protected traits",
    text: "Attacking a person or group because of race, ethnicity, national origin, religion, disability, sex, sexual orientation, or gender identity is not allowed. The line is attacking people for what they are, not disagreeing with what they think or do.",
    allowed: ["Criticism of any religion's doctrine or any government's policy", "Arguing that a political movement is wrong or harmful", "Blunt, offensive, or unpopular opinions about ideas"],
    notAllowed: ["Slurs directed at a person or group", "Calling for a protected group to be harmed or excluded", "Sustained pile-ons against one person because of a protected trait"],
    automation: "none",

  },
  {

    title: "No doxxing",
    text: "Publishing someone's private information without consent is not allowed: home address, phone number, private email, workplace details intended to enable harassment, financial or ID documents, or private images. When a report is credible the post is hidden from others while a person decides, because the harm is immediate.",
    allowed: ["Public business contact details", "Information a public figure has published about themselves", "Linking to public court records in a news context"],
    notAllowed: ["Posting someone's home address or phone number", "Sharing private messages or images without consent", "Coordinating to find where someone lives"],
    automation: "none",
    seniorQueue: false,
  },
  {
    id: "R5",
    title: "No direct threats of violence",
    text: "Stating an intent to physically harm a specific person or group, or calling for others to do so, is not allowed. Hyperbole, dark humour, and discussion of violence in news, history, or fiction are allowed. Cases go to the senior queue.",
    allowed: ["Discussing wars, crimes, or historical violence", "Obvious hyperbole ('I could kill for a coffee')", "Fiction and satire"],
    notAllowed: ["'I will hurt you' directed at a person", "Calling for a named person to be attacked", "Posting a target list"],

  },
  {

    text: "Repetitive unsolicited posting, deceptive schemes, malware links, and pretending to be another person or organisation are not allowed. Parody and fan accounts are fine when clearly labelled.",
    allowed: ["Promoting your own work in your own posts", "Clearly labelled parody accounts", "Sharing a link once in a relevant thread"],
    notAllowed: ["Posting the same link across many threads", "Phishing or crypto giveaway scams", "An account presenting itself as a real person or brand it is not"],
    automation: "none",
    seniorQueue: false,
  },
] as const satisfies readonly Rule[];

/**
 * Version 2, with moderation cases: nothing is automated (a person decides every case; the automated checks of R1 and R2
 * return with a later version), R2 says how reported images are handled without anyone opening them, R4 and R5 say who
 * hides content while a case is decided and who decides it, and R6 names coordinated manipulation. R3 is unchanged.
 */
const RULES_V2 = [
  {

    text: "Images or text whose primary purpose is sexual arousal are not allowed. This includes nudity presented sexually, explicit sexual acts, and sexualised depictions of anyone.",

  },
  {

Whoever is on duty may seal them while an admin decides: sealed images are shown to nobody, their author included. An admin either seals them for good, in which case they are kept only for the authorities and reported to them, or answers without a seal. Every final decision on a report or finding under this rule, whether it acts or not, and every review of one, is taken by an admin. Only an admin can lift a seal, and a seal for good only on the authorities' answer; an appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images.",
    automation: "none",
  },
  RULES_V1[2],
  {
    ...RULES_V1[3],
    text: "Publishing someone's private information without consent is not allowed: home address, phone number, private email, workplace details intended to enable harassment, financial or ID documents, or private images. When a moderator finds a report credible, the post is hidden from others while the moderator decides, because the harm is immediate. The number of reports never decides it.",
  },
  {
    ...RULES_V1[4],
    text: "Stating an intent to physically harm a specific person or group, or calling for others to do so, is not allowed. Hyperbole, dark humour, and discussion of violence in news, history, or fiction are allowed. Any moderator may hide a reported threat from others at once while an admin decides, and may lift that again. Every final decision on a report under this rule, whether it acts or not, is taken by an admin, and only an admin corrects one. An appeal against a restriction under it is reviewed by a moderator who made none of the case's decisions and did not report it themselves, and waits while korbat has none.",
  },
  {
    ...RULES_V1[5],
    title: "No spam, scams, impersonation or coordinated manipulation",
    text: "Repetitive unsolicited posting, deceptive schemes, malware links, and pretending to be another person or organisation are not allowed. Parody and fan accounts are fine when clearly labelled. Coordinating several accounts, your own or other people's, to like, repost or report together is not allowed.",
    allowed: [...RULES_V1[5].allowed, "Asking your followers to read or share a post"],
    notAllowed: [...RULES_V1[5].notAllowed, "A group of accounts liking each other's posts on cue to lift them in Explore", "Reporting someone together to get them removed"],
  },
] as const satisfies readonly Rule[];

/**
 * Version 3, with account sanctions (3e design, section 18, W.4): version 2 with one change, to R6, which now also names
 * report after report that is plainly unfounded, and says that a notice of illegal content is never restricted.
 */
const RULES_V3 = [
  RULES_V2[0],
  RULES_V2[1],
  RULES_V2[2],
  RULES_V2[3],
  RULES_V2[4],
  {
    ...RULES_V2[5],
    text: `${RULES_V2[5].text} Sending report after report that is plainly unfounded is not allowed either: after a warning, korbat may stop taking an account's reports under these rules for a limited time. A notice of illegal content is never restricted.`,
    allowed: [...RULES_V2[5].allowed, "Reporting in good faith something that turns out to break no rule"],
    notAllowed: [...RULES_V2[5].notAllowed, "Reporting the same account again and again for posts that plainly break no rule"],
  },
] as const satisfies readonly Rule[];

/** R2's sentence of version 3 that version 4 changes (3d review ruling 2: staff never open an image a match names). */
const R2_V3_LOOK = "After an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image.";

/**
 * Version 4, with transparency and automation (3d design, section 18, W.4): version 3 with three changes. R1 says what a
 * program may do with a rating, and R2 what a comparison with lists of known material may do, each pointing to the rules
 * page's list of what runs today; and R2's sentence on staff opening images after an answer without a seal gains its
 * exception for an image that an automated comparison matched. R3 to R6 are unchanged.
 */
const RULES_V4 = [
  {
    ...RULES_V3[0],
    text: `${RULES_V3[0].text} korbat may let a program rate uploaded images against this rule. An image it rates as likely within the rule is put before a moderator, and korbat may hide that one image from other people until the moderator has decided; its author still sees it, is told at once and can ask for a person. No program removes anything or judges text. Whether a program runs and what runs today is stated under Automation on the rules page.`,
    automation: "flag_or_withhold",
  },
  {
    ...RULES_V3[1],
    text: `${RULES_V3[1].text.replace(R2_V3_LOOK, "After an admin has answered without a seal, staff may open them like any other image, except an image that an automated comparison matched: korbat's staff do not open such an image at any time.")} korbat may compare the fingerprint of an uploaded image with lists of images that a named body has classified as child sexual abuse material. An upload that the body reports as an exact match with such an entry is not accepted, now or later, and is held unseen until an admin has decided what happens to the file. When an image that is already on a post matches in that way, it is put before an admin at once, korbat keeps that post's images until the admin has answered, and korbat may seal them at once until then. A match with such an entry that the body does not report as exact refuses no upload and is never sealed by a program; on a post it is put before an admin in the same way, and korbat keeps that post's images until the admin has answered. A match is a comparison of fingerprints, not korbat's finding about an image; korbat's staff do not open an image that a match names; and nothing is removed by a program. Whether a comparison runs, with which body, and what runs today is stated under Automation on the rules page.`,
    automation: "seal_for_review",
  },
  RULES_V3[2],
  RULES_V3[3],
  RULES_V3[4],
  RULES_V3[5],
] as const satisfies readonly Rule[];

/** The version a decision made now records. */
export const RULES_VERSION = 4;

/** Every version of the rulebook, by its number. */
export const RULEBOOKS = { 1: RULES_V1, 2: RULES_V2, 3: RULES_V3, 4: RULES_V4 } as const satisfies Record<number, readonly Rule[]>;

/** The rules in force. */
export const RULES = RULEBOOKS[RULES_VERSION];

/** One version of the rulebook as the rules page's change log prints it: the day it came into force and what it changed. */
export interface RulesChange {
  version: number;
  /** The day the version came into force, as the pages print a day. */
  date: string;
  summary: string;
}

/**
 * The rulebook's change log (3d design, sections 2 row 7, 9.2 and 10.8; W.1), oldest first: one dated sentence a version.
 * The day is a literal written by the task that ships the version; versions 1 to 3 carry the day of the commit that added
 * each to this file. The rules page prints it newest first.
 */
export const RULES_CHANGES: readonly RulesChange[] = [
  { version: 1, date: "2026-09-14", summary: "The six rules as first published." },
  {
    version: 2,
    date: "2026-10-04",
    summary:
      "A person decides every case; the automated checks that R1 and R2 named are withdrawn until they exist. R2 says how reported images are handled without anyone opening them. R4 and R5 say who may hide content while a case is decided and who decides it. R6 names coordinated manipulation.",
  },
  { version: 3, date: "2026-10-12", summary: "R6 names repeated, plainly unfounded reporting." },
  // 3d Task 8 (W.1, W.4): the day version 4 came into force.
  { version: 4, date: "2026-10-19", summary: "R1 and R2 say what an automated tool may do when one is switched on, and point to the list of what runs today." },
];

export type RuleId = (typeof RULES)[number]["id"];

/** A rule as one version of the rulebook words it: the current version unless told. Undefined for an id or a version that does not exist. */
export function getRule(id: string, version: number = RULES_VERSION): Rule | undefined {
  const book: readonly Rule[] | undefined = (RULEBOOKS as Record<number, readonly Rule[]>)[version];
  return book?.find((rule) => rule.id === id);
}

export function isRuleId(id: string): id is RuleId {
  return RULES.some((rule) => rule.id === id);
}

/** What a statement of reasons tells its author they can do about the decision. Which text applies follows from the decision's own kind and outcome. */
export interface RedressTexts {
  /** A final decision that restricts: korbat's appeal. `{deadline}` stands for the last day of the appeal, which the statement fills in. */
  appeal: string;
  /** A decision taken while korbat decides. */
  interim: string;
  /** Any other decision, which its author cannot appeal. */
  notAppealable: string;
  // Version 2 (3e design, section 18, W.3). Their numbers are literals of the version, held to STANDING_RULES by a table
  // test: a changed number is a new version, so an old statement keeps its own.
  /** After a strike's sentence: the prior warning of what strikes lead to. */
  strikeNext?: string;
  /** An announced suspension or termination: the reply before the start. */
  reply?: string;
  /** A suspension or termination taken at once: the reply while it runs. */
  replyAtOnce?: string;
  /** A kept answer to a reply. `{deadline}` stands for the last day of the appeal of the decision it keeps. */
  replyAnswered?: string;
  /** After a warning about reporting: what may follow it. */
  warnNext?: string;
  /** An announced measure: the appeal does not wait for the start. */
  appealNow?: string;
  /** Version 3 (3f design, W.2 and W.3): the notice of an authority's order, ORDER_NOTICE. */
  order?: typeof ORDER_NOTICE;
  /**
   * Version 4 (3d design, W.4): "Ask for a person" in the place of `interim`, on a decision without a decider: `askPerson`
   * for a program's withhold of an image, `askAdmin` for its seal of a post's images; and `uploadObject`, the objection to
   * a refused upload (Task 7's notice).
   */
  askPerson?: string;
  askAdmin?: string;
  uploadObject?: string;
}

/**
 * The version of the redress texts a decision made now records. 3d Task 6 (design, section 10.8; W.4): 4, since a
 * program's decision records the version whose askPerson it prints, so the version cannot wait for the rulebook's.
 */
export const REDRESS_VERSION = 4;

const OUTSIDE_KORBAT = "complain to the Digital Services Coordinator of the EU country where you live (Article 53 of the Digital Services Act).";

const REDRESS_V1 = {
  appeal: `You can appeal this decision once, free of charge, within six months of being told, until {deadline}: choose "Appeal" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator who took no part in the case reviews it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  interim: `This applies while korbat decides, and ends with its decision. If korbat's decision restricts your post or profile, you can appeal it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  notAppealable: `korbat's appeal does not apply to this decision. Where an earlier decision about this content still stands in part, its own screen in korbat says whether you can still appeal it. You can go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
} as const;

/** Account sanctions (3e): six more texts beside version 1's three, which version 2 holds word for word. */
const REDRESS_V2 = {
  strikeNext:
    "A strike restricts nothing by itself. When an account has 3 active strikes, a moderator may decide to suspend it for a limited time or, after three suspensions in 365 days, an admin may decide to terminate it. You would be told first and could reply before anything is restricted.",
  reply: `Before it starts you can reply: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and say anything you want the moderator to weigh. A reply sent before the start holds the start until a moderator has read it and answered you; if the decision is kept, it then starts with the answer, and never before the time you were given. A reply sent later is read and answered too, and can end this measure, but does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
  replyAtOnce: `You can reply at any time while it runs: choose "Reply" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases. A moderator reads your reply and answers you, and can end this measure at once; the reply does not pause it. You can reply once. Replying does not use up your appeal.`,
  replyAnswered: `This answer is not appealed by itself. The appeal is against the decision it keeps: once, free of charge, until {deadline}, with "Appeal" on that decision's screen under Settings, Cases. The six months for it count from this answer when you replied before the start, and otherwise from the day you were told of that decision. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  warnNext: "If 3 of the reports you send after this warning are marked that way while it counts, a moderator may restrict your reports under korbat's rules for up to 30 days.",
  appealNow: "You can appeal from now; you do not have to wait for the start. An appeal does not hold the start: only a reply sent before the start does.",
} as const;

/**
 * 3d (design, W.4): version 3's texts word for word, and three that join. Each number in them is a literal of this
 * version, held to AUTOMATION_RULES.objectionTargetHours by the package's table test: a changed target is a new version,
 * so an old statement keeps its own.
 */
const REDRESS_V4 = {
  askPerson: `You can ask for a person now: choose "Ask for a person" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and write anything a person should know. You can send one message. korbat's target is that a moderator answers within 24 hours; the measure does not end by itself before a person has decided. A measure a program takes cannot be appealed as such: ask for a person instead. The moderator's decision can be appealed, if it restricts your post. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  askAdmin: `You can ask for a person now: choose "Ask for a person" on this decision's screen under Settings, Cases, and write anything a person should know. You can send one message. korbat's target is that an admin answers within 24 hours; the measure does not end by itself before a person has decided. A measure a program takes cannot be appealed as such: ask for a person instead. The admin's decision can be appealed, if it seals the images for good; an appeal of a seal waits until the authorities have assessed the images. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
  uploadObject: `You can object, free of charge: choose "Object" on this screen and write anything the admin should know. You can send one message, at any time before the hold is lifted or korbat has released the file, also after an admin has decided to report it. An admin, not a program, decides what happens to the file. Nobody at korbat can accept the image, since nobody opens it. You can also go to court, or ${OUTSIDE_KORBAT}`,
} as const;

/** Every version of the redress texts, by its number, kept as the rulebooks are. */
export const REDRESS_TEXTS = {
  1: REDRESS_V1,
  2: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2 },
  /**
   * 3f (design, section 10.7; W.3): version 2's nine texts word for word, and the group `order`, the notice of an
   * authority's order (ORDER_NOTICE of the statement's module), so a notice reads under its own version.
   */
  3: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2, order: ORDER_NOTICE },
  /** 3d Task 6 (W.4): version 3's texts word for word, and the three of "Ask for a person" and the upload's objection. */
  4: { ...REDRESS_V1, ...REDRESS_V2, order: ORDER_NOTICE, ...REDRESS_V4 },
} as const satisfies Record<number, RedressTexts>;

/** The redress texts of one version. Undefined for a version that does not exist. */
export function getRedress(version: number): RedressTexts | undefined {
  return (REDRESS_TEXTS as Record<number, RedressTexts>)[version];
}

// The statement of reasons, rendered over the rulebooks and the redress texts above. The package exports only this file,
// so the app, the console and the API reach the statement through it.
export {
  IMAGE_LOST_NOTICE,
  ORDER_NOTICE,
  RELEASE_DAY_NOTICE,
  RELEASE_NOTICE,
  STATEMENT_WORDS,
  UPLOAD_NOTICE,
  releaseNoticeParagraphs,
  uploadNoticeParagraphs,
  retireEnd,
  statementParagraphs,
  type OrderNoticeExtras,
  type RetireEnd,
  type StatementInput,
} from "./statement";
```
